postings.title: 3PL Operations Manager
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
Europe 3PL operations manager

Position Overview

The European 3PL Manager owns Nebius's network of external warehouses and the performance of the 3PL partners who run them. The role ensures that high-value data center hardware stored and handled by third parties is received, stored, picked and shipped to the same standard as in Nebius-operated sites.

The manager controls 3PL operations through SLAs, KPIs, audits and system data, coordinates daily flows between 3PLs and internal teams (Transport, Planning, Back Office, ITDC, Security), and drives cost, compliance and continuous improvement across all external locations.

Key Responsibilities

- 3PL Network & Partner Management

- Manage the portfolio of external warehouses and 3PL partners across EMEA/US/APAC.

- Own contracts, SLAs and rate cards together with Procurement and Legal; prepare renewals and renegotiations.

- Run monthly operational reviews and quarterly business reviews (QBRs) with each 3PL; agree and track improvement plans.

- Act as the primary escalation point for 3PL partners and for internal teams on 3PL-related issues.

- Operations Control

- Set and enforce operating standards for 3PLs: receiving, put-away, storage, picking, packing, dispatch and returns (RMA).

- Ensure 3PLs follow Nebius SOPs for handling heavy, fragile, high-value equipment (racks, GPU servers, HSM devices).

- Monitor daily operational performance through WMS data, reports and site visits; act on deviations.

- Lead root-cause analysis of incidents (damage, loss, mis-shipments, delays) and follow corrective and preventive actions to closure.

- Inventory Control & Audits

- Ensure inventory accuracy at external sites: cycle counts, annual stock takes and reconciliation with ERP/WMS.

- Organise periodic on-site audits and inspections of 3PL warehouses (process, security, safety, documentation).

- Coordinate with Back Office on stock discrepancies, adjustments and asset records.

- Support internal and external (SOX) audits for inventory held by third parties.

- Coordination with Internal Teams

- Align inbound and outbound volumes with Logistics Planning and Transport so 3PLs have capacity and labour in time.

- Coordinate with ITDC and Project Managers on staging, kitting and release of hardware to data center sites.

- Work with Security on access control, CCTV, pre-arrival information and secure-storage requirements at 3PL sites.

- Ensure accurate and timely data exchange between 3PL systems and Nebius ERP/WMS (integrations, ASNs, stock reports).

- Cost Management

- Own the 3PL budget: storage, handling, value-added services and accessorial charges.

- Validate 3PL invoices against contracts and actual activity together with Back Office; resolve disputes.

- Track cost per pallet / rack / movement and identify savings through consolidation, space optimisation and renegotiation.

- Network Development: Onboarding & Exit

- Assess needs for new external storage based on DC expansion plans and capacity forecasts.

- Lead 3PL selection (RFI/RFQ, site assessment) with Procurement and onboard new partners: SOPs, system setup, training, go-live.

- Manage 3PL exits and stock transfers with zero loss and full traceability.

- Compliance & Risk

- Ensure 3PL operations meet security, safety, insurance and customs requirements (e.g. bonded storage where applicable).

- Maintain audit-ready documentation on contracts, SLAs, audits and incidents.

- Identify operational and dependency risks in the 3PL network and maintain contingency plans.

- Team Leadership

- Lead 3PL / External Warehouse Specialists as the function scales; set priorities, onboard and develop them.

- Define workflows, responsibilities and escalation paths between the 3PL team, Warehouse Operations and Transport.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

KPI

Definition

SLA compliance

% of 3PL SLA targets met (dock-to-stock, order cycle time, on-time dispatch)

Inventory accuracy

% match between 3PL physical stock and Nebius ERP/WMS

Incident rate

Damage, loss and mis-shipment cases per 1,000 movements

CAPA closure

% of corrective actions closed by due date

Audit results

Score / findings from 3PL on-site audits and SOX tests

Cost per unit

3PL cost per pallet / rack / movement vs. budget

Invoice accuracy

% of 3PL invoices matching contract and activity without dispute

Expectations

Autonomy: Full ownership of the 3PL network and partner performance; escalates contract, budget and major-risk decisions.

Impact: Directly affects hardware availability, inventory accuracy and warehousing cost across all external sites.

Leadership: Leads 3PL specialists and steers partner teams without direct authority.

Travel: Regular trips to 3PL sites for audits, reviews and onboarding.

Work Mode: Hybrid, with regular presence at key logistics sites.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

The role 

Nebius is hiring a senior Account Executive to drive customer acquisition and growth across APJ. This is a strategic hunter role, focused on expanding adoption of our AI and cloud platform with new and existing customers in the region.

You will own complex, high-value sales cycles end to end—building executive relationships, uncovering new opportunities, working closely with partners, and closing deals that drive long-term customer value. Success in this role requires strong consultative selling skills, the ability to translate complex business needs into tailored solutions, and comfort operating in a fast-moving, innovative environment.

This role blends strategic thinking with hands-on execution and will play a key role in helping customers unlock the full potential of Nebius’ AI and cloud offerings.

This role is also a core member of our founding APJ team, currently operating remotely out of Singapore.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Own and grow your territory: Build and execute a strategic territory plan, delivering against revenue and growth targets.

- Negotiation & closing: Lead complex, multi-stakeholder negotiations with C-suite and senior decision-makers, closing deals that support long-term partnerships.

- Solution selling: Demonstrate the value of Nebius’ AI and cloud platform through consultative discovery, tailored presentations, and product demonstrations.

- Client engagement: Develop trusted relationships with key stakeholders across the enterprise, aligning solutions to customer-specific challenges and outcomes.

- Team orchestration: Partner closely with Sales Engineers, Industry Specialists, Partners, and Customer Success to deliver differentiated value propositions.

- Forecasting & execution: maintain strong forecast accuracy and delivering against ACV and activity targets.

- Market presence: Represent Nebius at regional and industry events, webinars, and customer forums.

- Subject matter expertise: Stay current on industry trends, emerging technologies, and the competitive landscape to position our solutions effectively.

We expect you to have: 

- 10+ years of B2B sales experience, ideally in AI, cloud, data infrastructure, or related technologies.

- A proven track record of exceeding sales targets, generating pipeline, and maintaining forecast accuracy.

- Experience selling cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), AI solutions, or complex enterprise technologies.

- Strong commercial acumen, including value-based selling, executive storytelling, negotiation, and multi-year deal structuring.

- A genuine interest in working in a high-growth, startup environment, with a desire to directly impact company growth.

- Willingness and ability to travel within the region as needed.

It will be an added bonus if you have:

- Proficiency in additional regional languages beyond English.

- Prior experience in a high-growth or early-stage startup environment.

postings.title: AI Science Writer, Nebius Academy (Contract)
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
About Nebius Academy and Nebius Science 

Nebius Academy is Nebius’s education and research initiative. It offers advanced programs in machine learning and generative AI, supports academic research through cloud grants, and works with universities and research institutions around the world.

Nebius Science is the research media lab within Nebius Academy. We cover AI research, AI-driven science, and the people and ideas shaping both fields.

Since launching in 2026, Nebius Science has highlighted the work of our researchers, covered major AI conferences and emerging research trends, and developed joint editorial projects with recipients of Nebius research grants. 

Our work spans original features, technical explainers, weekly Paper Picks, research webinars, the Nebius Science Paper Club, and interviews with leading researchers.

Our goal is to make serious research accessible without flattening its complexity, and to create a meeting point for researchers, engineers, and the wider scientific community.

The role

Nebius Science is looking for an AI Science Writer based in the EU. This is an ongoing contract role with a fixed monthly retainer and opportunities for growth, including the potential to transition to a full-time position at Nebius.

You may be an AI/ML researcher or engineer who moved into journalism, a computer science graduate with substantial editorial experience, or a technical writer who has worked directly with research teams. Whatever your path, you should be able to read a technical paper, understand the underlying method, assess its limitations, and turn it into a clear and compelling story.

A central part of the role will be producing weekly reviews of new AI models, architectures, and in-house research. You should be able to identify what is genuinely new and explain how it works creatively across a range of formats.

These reviews can be visual as well as written. You will be expected to develop clear, engaging infographics, diagrams, charts, and other multimedia elements, creating them yourself by using AI tools where appropriate or working with designers and multimedia producers.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Produce scientific and technical reviews of new AI models, architectures, papers, in-house research and trends.

- Turn model architectures and complex technical ideas into clear visual narratives by developing infographics, diagrams, charts, and other multimedia components for your stories.

- Interview researchers, engineers, founders, and scientific leaders.

- Cover major research conferences, emerging fields, and important debates across the AI ecosystem.

- Write and edit across formats, including analytical reports, features, interviews, explainers, newsletters, webinar scripts, and social content.

- Host or moderate research webinars, interviews, and other on-camera formats.

- Work with researchers to verify technical claims while preserving a clear editorial voice.

- Collaborate with designers and multimedia producers on more complex visual stories.

- Experiment with models, agents, coding, and automation to improve research, editorial, and visual-production workflows.

We expect you to have: 

- Have professional or academic experience in AI/ML research, machine learning engineering, or a closely related technical field.

- Have a degree in computer science, machine learning, mathematics, physics, engineering, computational science, or another relevant technical discipline.

- Be comfortable reading papers, inspecting model architectures, comparing results, and discussing technical details directly with researchers.

- Have strong visual instincts and be able to explain technical mechanisms through diagrams, infographics, charts, or other multimedia formats.

- Write with precision and flair, using LLMs to support your work, not to do the writing for you.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

About the role

Location: Amsterdam
Duration: 3 months
Start date: January 2027
Compensation: Paid
Eligibility: Current University student (Computer Science or related field), Recent Graduate or Early Career specialist
Work authorization: Permitted to work in the job's location

Capacity Management sits at the intersection of technology, infrastructure planning and business priorities. Our work depends on close collaboration with engineering, supply chain, product, finance and sales. We coordinate multiple areas of activity, manage cross-functional agreements and help the organization understand what capacity is available, where it is needed and which dependencies may affect delivery.

As Nebius grows, this operating model needs to be easy to understand — not only for our team, but also for the many people who work with us. Today, much of this knowledge is distributed across different documents, tools and individuals.

We are looking for a student or recent graduate to help us turn this complex environment into a clear and useful knowledge base. Your primary project will be to redesign and build the Capacity Management home page and supporting documentation in Confluence.

This is not simply a content-formatting assignment. You will need to speak with stakeholders, understand technical and managerial realities, identify connections and gaps, and translate what you learn into a structure that people can actually use.

Your responsibilities will include

- 

Learning how the Capacity Management function operates and how it interacts with other teams.

- 

Interviewing team members and cross-functional stakeholders to collect and validate information.

- 

Mapping our main areas of responsibility, workflows, dependencies and stakeholder interfaces.

- 

Designing a clear information architecture for the Capacity Management Confluence space.

- 

Creating a practical home page that helps different audiences find the right information quickly.

- 

Developing or improving onboarding materials for new team members and partners.

- 

Documenting key processes, ownership areas, terminology, decision paths and working agreements.

- 

Collecting feedback from users and improving the content based on how it works in practice.

What we expect

- 

You are currently completing, or have recently completed, a degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, operations management or a related field.

- 

You can bring structure to incomplete, scattered or ambiguous information.

- 

You can explain complex subjects in simple, precise language.

- 

You are comfortable asking questions, listening carefully and following up until you understand how something really works.

- 

You can distinguish between a process as it is intended to work and how it works in practice.

- 

You are interested in cloud infrastructure, technical operations and cross-functional project management.

- 

You pay attention to detail without losing sight of the larger picture.

- 

You are comfortable collaborating with both technical specialists and managers.

You do not need to be a cloud infrastructure expert when you join. Curiosity, analytical thinking and the ability to learn quickly are more important.

It would be an advantage if you have

- 

Experience with Confluence or similar collaboration tools.

- 

Worked on university, volunteer or personal projects involving several stakeholders.

- 

Familiarity with cloud infrastructure concepts, capacity planning or service operations.

- 

An interest in technical project or program management as a career.

What you will gain

This Early Talent Program offers a close-up view of how cross-functional management works in a fast-growing cloud infrastructure organization.

You will have the opportunity to:

- 

See how technical, commercial and operational priorities are coordinated in practice.

- 

Discover the real-world dependencies behind cloud infrastructure at scale.

- 

Learn how capacity decisions connect engineering, hardware, finance, product and customer demand.

- 

Understand how ownership boundaries, working agreements and escalation paths are created.

- 

Work with experienced specialists and managers across several functions.

- 

Deliver a visible project that will be used for onboarding and day-to-day collaboration.

By the end of the program, you should have a much deeper understanding of the managerial complexity behind large-scale technical systems — and concrete experience turning that complexity into something clear and actionable.

What success looks like

A successful Early Talent will result in:

- 

A clear and navigable Capacity Management home page.

- 

A documented overview of the team’s purpose, responsibilities and boundaries.

- 

An understandable map of our main activities, stakeholders and dependencies.

- 

Practical onboarding guidance for new team members and cross-functional partners.

- 

An agreed structure and ownership model for keeping the documentation current.

- 

Positive feedback from the people who use the space.

If the Early Talent is successful, we will be happy to discuss an opportunity to continue with the team in a full-time Project Manager position, subject to performance, mutual fit and business needs.

- Energy Systems Engineering

- Mission-critical operations

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Role Overview 

We are seeking a Compliance Due Diligence Specialist to further improve our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) and due diligence assessment framework and processes. This person will be responsible for day-to-day execution of due diligence assessments for various third parties. 

This role is ideal for someone with a solid compliance due diligence foundation who wants to dig down to investigating third parties, contribute to process improvements, and help scale a modern compliance function in a fast-growing tech environment. 

You will work closely with Ethics & Compliance, Legal, HR, and various other business and technology teams to ensure compliance is practical, efficient, and embedded into business operations. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Conduct third-party due diligence assessments, including risk scoring, screening, verification, and documentation of third-party risk profiles 

- Perform name screening against sanctions, PEP, adverse media, and related lists, and coordinate resolution of positive matches within established timelines 

- Manage internal due diligence for medium and high-risk third parties, including desktop checks, review of ownership structures, beneficial owners, and site visits where feasible

postings.description:
About Nebius:

About the Role

We are seeking a Construction Project Manager to lead the delivery of mission-critical data center projects from preconstruction through commissioning and turnover. This is an owner-side role responsible for managing scope, schedule, budget, quality, and safety across ground-up builds, expansions, and fit-outs of critical facilities. You will be the primary point of accountability for general contractors, design teams, commissioning agents, and equipment vendors, ensuring facilities are delivered on an aggressive speed-to-market timeline without compromising reliability.

What You'll Do

- Lead end-to-end project delivery for data center construction, owning cost, schedule, scope, quality, and safety from site selection support and preconstruction through Level 5 commissioning and operational handover.

- Manage general contractors, architects, MEP engineers, and specialty subcontractors, holding the project team accountable to contractual milestones and design intent.

- Drive coordination of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems — including utility power and substations, switchgear, UPS, generators, and air- and liquid-cooling infrastructure — recognizing that power and cooling drive the critical path.

- Develop and maintain integrated project schedules, identify critical-path risks early, and implement recovery plans to protect on-time, on-budget delivery.

- Manage project budgets, change orders, contingency, and forecasting; review pay applications and validate work in place.

- Own the commissioning process in partnership with the CxA, ensuring scripts, levels (L1–L5), and acceptance criteria are met before energization and turnover to operations.

- Enforce a strict safety culture, including the specific hazards of working in and around energized electrical environments and live critical facilities.

- Provide clear, regular reporting to leadership on schedule, budget, risk, and key decisions.

- Manage long-lead equipment procurement and vendor coordination, mitigating supply-chain risk on generators, switchgear, chillers, and cooling units.

- Support due diligence on site selection, including utility power availability, fiber, water, and constructability factors.

What You'll Bring

- 7+ years of construction project management experience, with at least 3 years delivering data centers or comparable mission-critical / critical-environment facilities (hospitals, semiconductor fabs, pharma, or large-scale industrial).

- Direct working knowledge of data center MEP systems: power distribution, redundancy topologies (N+1, 2N), UPS, generators, and air and liquid cooling.

- Familiarity with the commissioning process and Uptime Institute Tier standards.

- Demonstrated ability to manage multimillion-dollar budgets and complex, schedule-driven projects with multiple stakeholders.

- Strong command of project controls, scheduling software (P6 or MS Project), and construction management platforms (Procore or similar).

- Excellent contractor and vendor management skills, with the ability to hold teams accountable while maintaining productive relationships.

- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related field — or equivalent field experience.

- Willingness to travel to and be on-site at project locations as required.

Nice to Have

- Experience delivering for hyperscale or colocation clients.

- Exposure to liquid-cooling deployments and high-density rack environments.

- PMP, CCM, or relevant OSHA certifications.

- Experience managing projects in greenfield or speculative-build environments.

Why This Role Matters

The work you deliver is the physical backbone of cloud and AI infrastructure. These facilities have to be built fast, built right, and run without interruption — and the project manager is the single person who makes all of that come together.

You have a portfolio of customer stories people actually choose to watch, and campaigns that break through industry noise and deliver awareness, purchase intent and brand love. This role begins as an individual contributor: a coach to some of the world’s best agencies and a collaborator with talented colleagues. Your portfolio backs up your taste, your drive to collaborate across teams to find the best stories, and your willingness to roll up your sleeves and ship your best work. You’ll build and maintain the look and feel of the Nebius customer video library, turn customer co-marketing into targeted demand-building campaigns, establish the visual identity of content across web pages, deliver still photography, experiment with graphics, and show the world what great looks like.

You’ll lead the creative vision for how Nebius tells customer stories on camera: how they look, how they’re shot, and how fast they move from location to a landing page, a stage, a paid ad or a sales deck. You’ll do this partly with your own hands (filming, recording sound, directing on set and rough cutting) and partly through agency talent you hire, brief and hold to your high bar. You’re proficient in AI workloads, both training and inference, and you understand the AI ecosystem, including what matters to AI-native labs and digital-native enterprises. You tell stories beyond the classic customer story, with the technical cool factor that makes a builder want to follow the work.

This is a creative athlete’s job. You’ll need the range to hit shots from every angle with very little direction, because many days you’ll be inventing the processes and outcomes you want to bring into the world.

Jobs to be done

For each job below, you’ll define how it gets done, build a repeatable process behind it, and champion it across the company.
Capture our customer as the hero: When a customer does something remarkable with Nebius, you capture their voice, their outcomes, the people leading the work and the process that got them there. You set the creative vision and visual bar for all customer storytelling, from a 20-second, high-energy social cutdown to a 20-minute documentary film, and you push past the classic customer story into series, podcasts and formats a builder would follow on their own.

Build the AI content engine: When one interview needs to become 15 assets, you build the system that does it: transcript to cutdowns to social cards, with review and brand-voice checks built in. You document it, run it, and teach the team and agencies to use it.

Multiply the shoot: When sales, product marketing and brand each need the same story in a different format, you version it for every channel that needs it (paid social, organic, sales enablement, events, the website and press) without losing the complete story. You do it with an AI-powered content engine you design and own.

Earn reach beyond owned channels: Great content lives beyond owned channels. You build earned and partner distribution: influencers, publications and media, customer-posted content we amplify, G2 and other third-party sources. You measure it by views, reach and pickup. 

Scale through agencies: When demand outgrows what you can shoot yourself, you source, brief, hire and manage external production, editing and post-production agencies and small crews, holding them to one consistent creative standard.

Remove handoffs: When a shoot needs someone to point a camera, mic a subject, direct performance and support the edit, you step up. On location, you work as videographer and producer, sometimes leading sound and direction solo.

Set the visual bar high: You define what best-in-class looks like, develop a unique Nebius-owned storytelling look and feel, and experiment to find what’s next. Then you hold the bar as volume increases.

Build future capabilities: You keep a pipeline of customer stories moving through pre-production, production, post and versioning at the same time, across a global roster of customers. When the business is ready for a deeper customer marketing bench, you set the strategy for expanding high-quality creative through AI mechanisms and people.

How we’ll know it’s working

Success is measured on both pipeline and brand. You’ll set targets with us and report against them. Examples include reach of customer content beyond owned channels, the number of customers posting and amplifying their stories, Nebius share of voice, and content-influenced pipeline.

What to expect in the interview

Bring examples of work that earned real reach, not just work that shipped, with the results (views, reach, pickup). Be ready to walk us through an AI content workflow you built, end to end. We’ll ask how you think about outcomes in pipeline and brand terms.

Requirements

- Customer-hero craft: a portfolio of customer stories people actually choose to watch, across video, social, podcast and series, not just PDFs and case studies. Include work that earned real reach, not just work that shipped.

- Distribution: a track record of earned and partner / third-party distribution beyond owned channels (influencers, publications and media, customer-posted content you amplify, G2 and other third-party sources), with results to show in views, reach and pickup.

- Creative storytelling range: stories beyond the classic customer story, with a builder / technical cool factor. The test: would a builder follow your work on its own?

- AI-native content systems: you have built AI systems for content creation (for example, one interview repurposed into 15 assets, transcript to cutdowns to social cards, review and brand-voice checks) and can walk us through a workflow you built.

- 8+ years of progressive content leadership experience in a senior role at a B2B company, leading or building a creative, content or production team.

- A track record of building brands and pipeline through content and campaign creative, tracking results and improving creative outcomes to hit goals.

- Hands-on experience filming, directing and editing, including true documentary or observational shooting, not only studio or talking-head interviews.

- Technical credibility: a portfolio of AI-native or developer-facing content where the audience is builders, and the comfort to interview AI directors and chief researchers at that level.

- Comfort operating with very little direction and a lot of ambiguity, and the judgment to make the call anyway.

- Taste: an eye for what makes a story worth watching, and the confidence to say no to a shot, script or edit that doesn’t meet the bar.

- Experience hiring, briefing and managing external agencies or freelance crews.

- Willingness to travel frequently and shoot on short notice.

Bonus:

- Experience scaling a one-person creative function into a small team that works through agencies.

- Sound design, color grading or motion graphics skills you can bring to an edit yourself.

- A network of production and editing talent you’d bring with you.

- Experience building customer advocacy or reference-style content.

- Prior experience at a fast-growing infrastructure, cloud or AI company.

Competencies

- Cross-functional player/coach: As comfortable directing others as you are picking up the camera and cutting the edit yourself.

- End-to-end athlete: Moves fluidly between filming, sound, directing and rough cutting without waiting for a handoff.

- Taste-maker: Has a clear point of view on what’s good, and the nerve to defend it under deadline pressure.

- Builder: Comfortable creating a workflow, an AI content engine, an agency bench and a quality bar from nothing.

- Thrives in ambiguity: Doesn’t wait for a brief. Writes the brief, rallies a team around the vision and delivers against it.

- Startup speed, global scale: Moves like a startup across time zones without slowing down.

- Generous collaborator: Brings out the best in producers, editors and agency partners rather than doing their jobs for them. Looks good when they look good.

- Outcome thinker: Defines success in pipeline and brand terms before the shoot, distributes for reach beyond owned channels, and reports on both. 

Compensation 

We offer competitive salaries, plus bonus, and equity based on your experience. Title and compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Key employee benefits in the US:

- 401(k) plan: Up to 4% company match with immediate vesting.

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Remote work reimbursement: Up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

- Disability & life insurance: Company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

We are seeking a Critical Infrastructure Engineer to help ensure the availability, resilience, and operational readiness of the critical systems supporting Nebius data center IT infrastructure.

The primary objective of this role is uptime.

You will provide technical oversight across the electrical and mechanical infrastructure responsible for delivering reliable power and cooling to our GPU and IT environments. Rather than serving primarily as a maintenance technician, you will verify that critical infrastructure is operated safely, consistently, and in accordance with established SLAs, engineering standards, change-control procedures, and operational best practices.

You will also act as an important bridge between IT infrastructure teams and electrical/mechanical specialists. The ideal candidate understands how servers, networking equipment, racks, and GPU systems operate inside a data center while also having enough exposure to critical facilities systems to understand—and challenge when necessary—the infrastructure supporting them.

The position combines technical analysis, provider governance, change management, incident response, and hands-on familiarity with data center IT environments.

You will work onsite in our Minnesota data center location.

Your responsibilities will include:

Critical Infrastructure & Uptime

- Help ensure the availability and operational readiness of the electrical and mechanical infrastructure supporting production data halls and high-density GPU environments.

- Monitor critical infrastructure performance against contractual SLAs, operational requirements, and established reliability standards.

- Develop a strong understanding of the complete power and cooling path supporting IT equipment and identify conditions that could introduce operational risk.

- Review infrastructure capacity, redundancy, and operating conditions to ensure the environment can reliably support current and planned compute deployments.

- Identify infrastructure risks and work with service providers and internal teams to drive corrective actions before they impact production.

- Support infrastructure planning for data center expansions, capacity increases, and new GPU deployments.

Power & Electrical Infrastructure

- Provide technical oversight of data center electrical infrastructure, including generator plants, automatic transfer switches (ATS), UPS systems, battery banks, switchgear, breakers, busbars, bus plugs, PDUs, and related power distribution equipment.

- Understand electrical distribution from facility-level infrastructure through rack-level delivery and IT equipment.

- Participate in technical reviews involving power capacity, electrical distribution, equipment sizing, redundancy, and infrastructure design.

- Work with electrical engineers and infrastructure providers to evaluate proposed changes and ensure appropriate engineering validation is completed before production implementation.

Cooling & Mechanical Infrastructure

- Understand the cooling architecture supporting high-density GPU and IT environments, including water and glycol loops, rear-door heat exchangers (RDHx), evaporative systems, coolant distribution systems, facility water systems, dry coolers, and chillers.

- Evaluate how cooling infrastructure interacts with GPU systems and high-density racks to maintain required operating conditions.

- Partner with mechanical engineers and service providers to review system performance, capacity constraints, and proposed infrastructure changes.

- Identify potential thermal or cooling risks that could affect compute availability or future capacity.

Provider Governance & Change Control

- Provide technical oversight of third-party critical infrastructure and colocation service providers.

- Ensure provider activities comply with Nebius policies, approved procedures, contractual SLAs, and operational requirements.

- Review and approve change requests involving critical infrastructure supporting production environments.

- Challenge incomplete or high-risk work plans and ensure appropriate testing, rollback procedures, risk analysis, and stakeholder communication are in place before work begins.

- Maintain strong governance around maintenance and infrastructure changes that could affect production availability.

- Hold service providers accountable for corrective actions, operational performance, and agreed service levels.

Incident Response & Operational Risk

- Participate in critical infrastructure incidents and coordinate technical response with providers, Data Center IT, networking, and engineering teams.

- Support root-cause analysis following power, cooling, or infrastructure-related incidents.

- Review incident findings and ensure corrective and preventive actions are documented, assigned, and completed.

- Help develop and continuously improve emergency response procedures, escalation paths, change-control standards, and operational documentation.

- Identify recurring infrastructure risks and drive improvements that increase reliability and reduce the likelihood of customer impact.

IT & Critical Infrastructure Integration

- Work closely with Data Center IT teams to understand how critical infrastructure conditions affect servers, networking equipment, GPU clusters, and other production systems.

- Apply practical knowledge of data center IT operations, including racks, servers, fiber, cabling, network equipment, and hardware deployment.

- Support cross-functional troubleshooting where the root cause may span IT equipment and facility infrastructure.

- Help create stronger operational alignment between IT infrastructure and electrical/mechanical teams.

Reporting & Stakeholder Communication

- Translate complex infrastructure conditions, incidents, risks, and provider performance into clear information for technical and business leadership.

- Develop reports, dashboards, presentations, and operational analyses related to uptime, infrastructure performance, capacity, incidents, and service-provider performance.

- Participate in technical and leadership meetings as a subject-matter resource for data center critical infrastructure.

- Use operational data to identify trends, communicate risk, and drive measurable improvements in reliability and provider performance.

We expect you to have:

- Experience working in data center, cloud infrastructure, colocation, critical facilities, or other mission-critical environments.

- Practical understanding of IT infrastructure, including servers, racks, networking equipment, structured cabling, and fiber.

- Working knowledge of data center electrical infrastructure such as UPS systems, generators, switchgear, PDUs, batteries, breakers, and power distribution.

- Exposure to data center mechanical and cooling systems, including chilled-water, glycol, liquid-cooling, or comparable thermal-management environments.

- Ability to understand how electrical and mechanical infrastructure directly impacts IT equipment availability and performance.

- Experience participating in infrastructure change management, incident response, operational risk management, or maintenance governance.

- Ability to review technical plans, ask detailed engineering questions, identify risk, and work effectively with electrical and mechanical subject-matter experts.

- Strong analytical skills with experience using Excel for reporting, data analysis, and operational metrics.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with engineers, vendors, service providers, and senior leadership.

- A proactive, ownership-driven approach with the ability to operate effectively in a high-availability production environment.

Nice to have:

- Experience supporting high-density GPU, AI, HPC, or hyperscale data center environments.

- Experience with direct-to-chip liquid cooling or other advanced cooling technologies used for high-density compute.

- Experience managing colocation or third-party critical infrastructure providers against contractual SLAs.

- Familiarity with Tier III data center environments and high-availability infrastructure principles.

- Experience developing or implementing change-management, incident-response, or emergency-response procedures.

- Experience supporting infrastructure capacity planning, expansion projects, or new data center deployments.

- Relevant electrical, mechanical, data center, or critical facilities certifications.

Critical Facilities Operations

Oversee the operation and maintenance of:

- Electrical distribution systems (MV/LV)

- UPS systems and battery plants

- Standby diesel generators

- Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS)

- Chillers and chilled water systems

- CRAH and CRAC units

- Air Handling Units (AHUs)

- Pumps and hydronic systems

- Heat exchangers

- Building Management System (BMS)

- Fire detection and suppression systems

- Security and access control systems

Health, Safety & Compliance

- Ensure compliance with Finnish occupational safety legislation, EU directives, environmental regulations, and company policies.

- Manage Permit to Work (PTW), Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), and contractor safety programs.

- Lead incident investigations and implement corrective actions.

- Prepare for and support regulatory inspections and internal audits.

Financial & Vendor Management

- Develop and manage the facilities operating budget.

- Review maintenance contracts and service agreements.

- Monitor vendor performance against established KPIs.

We are looking for a Technical Project Manager to own IT infrastructure in Nebius data centers from the moment it is accepted into operations: acceptance of new sites and GPU clusters from the Project team, and delivery of projects and changes in live production environments. You will work with modern GPU clusters — GPU servers, high-speed networking, compute and storage — acting as the link between the Project team, DC engineers, vendors and IT Operations.

This role represents IT Operations in those projects, sets the acceptance bar and owns the transition into steady-state operations.

Acceptance & operational readiness of new sites and clusters

Represent IT Operations in new site and cluster projects from the planning stage: define acceptance criteria and operational readiness requirements upfront, before build starts.

Own the acceptance process: readiness assessments, acceptance testing against agreed criteria, punch lists, operational sign-off. Acceptance is mandatory — no site or cluster moves into operations without it.

Prepare operations for takeover: operational procedures, tooling, documentation, on-site processes, spares and vendor support in place before sign-off.

- 

Manage the transition period from Project team to IT Operations, including defect follow-up and closure of open items after handover.

Operations projects & change management in live DCs

Manage and deliver IT infrastructure projects and change requests in production data centers: hardware deployments and replacements, capacity changes in accepted clusters, network and cabling changes, decommissioning.

- 

Own the change lifecycle for DC IT infrastructure: change requests, risk and impact assessment, MOPs, maintenance windows, rollback plans, post-implementation review.

- 

Manage risks and dependencies in live environments; proactively identify technical, operational and process issues and drive them to resolution.

- 

Stakeholders, communication & documentation

- 

Lead communication with all stakeholders: transparent progress reporting, expectation management, escalation of critical blockers, timely decision-making.

- 

Lead project meetings, technical reviews and operational readiness discussions with a focus on clear ownership, actionable outcomes and execution.

- 

Maintain project and operational documentation: acceptance criteria and reports, risk registers, issue logs, operational procedures, handover documentation, deployment reports.

- 

Cross-functional coordination & operational excellence

- 

Coordinate engineering, infrastructure, network, security, procurement, hardware lifecycle and operations teams across acceptance and operational phases.

- 

Work directly with data center engineers, vendors, contractors and operations teams.

- 

Lead operational reviews and planning with internal teams; improve reliability, response times and workflows.

- 

Contribute to automation, process improvements and design support as needed.

We expect you to have: 

- 

Proven experience in data center IT infrastructure operations, preferably in high-performance or AI-oriented environments.

- 

Experience accepting IT infrastructure into operations: defining acceptance criteria, running readiness assessments, taking handover from project teams.

- 

Experience running changes in live production environments: change requests, MOPs, maintenance windows, rollback planning.

- 

Solid understanding of data center design and operations: racking, cabling, power planning, cooling considerations.

Hands-on experience with IT hardware in data centers; comfortable on site during live operations.

Experience in project delivery, team coordination and cross-team collaboration.

- 

Strong problem-solving skills; ability to troubleshoot technical and workflow issues across the IT stack.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. About the Role

We are looking for a technically strong, hands-on QA Engineer to join our hardware team on-site at ODM factories in Taiwan. This is not a checklist job - we're looking for someone who enjoys digging deep into technical issues, investigating root causes, and taking ownership of complex hardware problems.You'll be the key person ensuring the quality of our servers and racks before they ship, but more importantly, you'll play a critical role in debugging failures, analyzing test data, and working closely with RnD, logistics, and factory teams to continuously improve the process and the product.This is a deeply technical role that blends hardware validation, manufacturing QA, and problem-solving - perfect for someone who understands how servers are built and tested, and wants to make sure every unit that leaves the factory is production-grade.

What You'll Own

- Technical Investigation & Debugging

- Investigate complex problems (e.g., high GPU failure rate, power-related test failures), gather logs, run diagnostics, and escalate with context to RnD when needed.

- Drive root cause analysis across factory teams and internal engineering groups.

- Document findings and help define preventive actions for recurring problems.

- Act as the first line of technical escalation for hardware issues discovered during factory QA or internal testing.Engineering Support

- Participate in new platform bring-up sessions together with the visiting RnD teams during on-site trips to ODM labs.

- Provide technical support, coordination, and hands-on assistance during the bring-up process.

- Help ensure early-stage hardware behaves as expected, and escalate integration or platform issues to the relevant teams.On-Site Product QA

- Perform visual inspections of completed products (servers, racks) before packaging.

- Define and maintain QA checklists and inspection procedures tailored to different product lines.

- Verify inventory records at the factory against internal system data (part numbers, serials, configurations).

- Oversee the product packaging process for compliance with defined standards.

- Supervise pickup operations: ensure outbound trucks meet shipment conditions and schedules.Failure Rate Monitoring & Analytics

- Collect failure data from vendor-side burn-in and our own test systems.

- Analyze failure trends and estimate spare part needs for future datacenter deployments.

- Use dashboards and structured reporting to communicate insights with QA, engineering, and supply chain teams.Feedback Loop & Quality Improvement

- Gather and process feedback from datacenters on each delivered batch of equipment:
 * Report on packaging issues, impact sensor triggers, shipping anomalies.
 * Assess rack-level build quality: cabling, bracket alignment, labeling.
 * Log systemic hardware issues (design flaws, infant mortality, recurring failures).

- Forward the feedback to the teams: logistics, ODM partners, hardware RnD, QA.Test Infrastructure & Validation

- Assist with deployment and maintenance of test infrastructure on-site.

- Ensure Nebius post-manufacturing hardware validation tests run smoothly (uptime, monitoring, coordination with support team).

- Coordinate real-time issue escalation and basic triage with factory and internal teams.Local Insight & Communication

- Communicate relevant local risks and context (e.g., typhoons, holidays, factory-specific constraints) to our global logistics and hardware teams.

- Maintain productive relationships with factory staff, logistics providers, and internal stakeholders.

Working Conditions & Tools

- During production peaks, issues may arise that require fast, hands-on debugging and resolution on-site. Flexibility is expected: you may need to stay late to investigate failures in freshly built batches or arrive early to verify and unblock outbound truck shipments. Rapid response and clear communication with engineering and factory teams are critical during these high-pressure periods.

- Occasional international travel may be expected to Nebius headquarters in Amsterdam or to datacenters in Europe and the US.

- Daily work tools involve:
 * Managing workflows and escalation via Jira
 * Writing and maintaining technical documentation in Confluence
 * Using Grafana dashboards for monitoring test environments and system health
 * Operating with several internal inventory and test control systems

What You'll Bring

- Strong technical background in hardware or systems engineering, able to independently investigate and troubleshoot complex issues with server systems.

- 5+ years of experience in hardware QA, manufacturing supervision, or server validation.

- A strong background in R&D is a significant plus.

- Solid understanding of server and rack hardware: components, layout, cabling, power/cooling, diagnostics.

- Ability to read and interpret technical documentation (e.g., datasheets, system specs, debug manuals).

- Solid knowledge of electrical engineering fundamentals (e.g., power specs, grounding, signal integrity).

About The Role

Nebius is seeking a Data Center Support Engineer to support large scale bare metal GPU infrastructure powering AI workloads. This role is responsible for operating, troubleshooting, and maintaining production infrastructure across servers, Linux systems, networking, firmware, drivers, and physical data center components.

You will serve as a senior technical escalation point between data center technicians, infrastructure engineering, network engineering, systems engineering, and customer facing teams. The ideal candidate is hands on, comfortable in Linux, strong in hardware diagnostics, and able to troubleshoot complex issues across multiple layers of the infrastructure stack.

What You’ll Do

- Support and troubleshoot production bare-metal GPU infrastructure across Nebius data center environments.

- Diagnose high-priority issues across Linux, hardware, firmware, BIOS, drivers, networking, storage, optics, cabling, and physical infrastructure.

- Perform hardware diagnostics, component replacement, firmware updates, BIOS configuration, break/fix, and infrastructure maintenance.

- Use Linux command-line tools, system logs, BMC data, and hardware health signals to identify root cause.

- Partner with data center technicians and engineering teams to coordinate remote troubleshooting, incident response, RCA, and operational recovery.

- Troubleshoot network connectivity issues involving TCP/IP, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, switch connectivity, optics, cabling, and link-level failures.

- Create troubleshooting guides, runbooks, escalation notes, and knowledge base documentation.

- Use scripting or automation to improve support workflows and reduce manual intervention.

- Participate in on-call or after-hours support for production infrastructure as needed.

- 5+ years of experience in data center operations, infrastructure support, systems administration, hardware support, cloud infrastructure, or similar technical environments.

- Hands-on experience troubleshooting bare metal servers, Linux systems, hardware components, and networking issues in production environments.

- Intermediate Linux command-line proficiency, including service validation, log review, process inspection, network configuration checks, and system diagnostics.

- Experience with server hardware diagnostics, component replacement, firmware updates, BIOS configuration, driver troubleshooting, or BMC tools such as iDRAC, iLO, IPMI, Redfish, or similar.

- Strong networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, routing/switching concepts, optics, cabling, and link-level troubleshooting.

- Experience participating in incident response, escalation handling, root cause analysis, or operational recovery in high-availability environments.

- Strong communication and documentation skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally with data center, infrastructure, network, systems, and engineering teams.

- Experience with NVIDIA GPUs, GPU servers, HPC, AI infrastructure, or high-density compute platforms.

- Experience with Supermicro, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Cisco UCS, Arista, Cisco, Juniper, or similar infrastructure platforms.

- Familiarity with InfiniBand, RoCE, MPO/MTP fiber, high-speed Ethernet, or clustered compute environments.

- Experience with Python, Bash, Ansible, Terraform, PowerShell, or similar automation tools.

- Familiarity with Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow, Grafana, Prometheus, Kubernetes, Docker, or similar operational tools.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

As a Data Center Technician, you will play a vital role in maintaining and optimizing the IT infrastructure within our data center. This includes working hands-on with modern technologies such as the advanced H200 GPU cloud cluster. Your responsibilities will include supporting the data center’s IT infrastructure by troubleshooting and resolving hardware issues, performing hardware and network diagnostics, carrying out physical repairs, and ensuring the smooth operation of critical systems. This is a shift-based role and may also require occasional travel between data center locations.

You will work onsite in our Kansas City, Missouri data center location. 

Your responsibilities will include:

- Diagnosing and resolving issues related to IT hardware and ensuring the continuous support of the data center's IT infrastructure across all compute, storage, and networking platforms.

- Collaborating effectively with internal teams and external contractors to address technical and operational challenges across the data center floor.

- Installing, upgrading, and decommissioning hardware based on operational requests, change requests, and project requirements.

- Managing and maintaining the connectivity of fiber optic cables, copper patch cords, and structured cabling in accordance with Nebius standards and documentation.

- Planning, executing, and monitoring regular IT tasks — including preventive maintenance, break/fix activities, and routine deployments — to maintain and improve data center infrastructure operations.

- Supporting the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) process by assisting with hardware identification, fault documentation, and coordination with the DC Diagnostic & RMA team, in accordance with established Nebius procedures.

- Developing and maintaining clear, accurate documentation including hardware configurations, troubleshooting guides, maintenance logs, and operational runbooks.

- Collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders including shift leads, infrastructure engineers, and DC management to ensure work is completed to standard and on schedule.

- Participating in shift-level technical tasks and project execution as directed by the Senior DC Technician or Lead DC Technician.

- Monitoring and reporting on the status of assigned work items, incidents, and hardware tasks through Nebius ticketing and operational systems.

We expect you to have:

- Hands-on experience diagnosing and resolving server hardware issues in a production or enterprise data center environment.

- A solid understanding of data center operations, server architecture, and network equipment principles.

- Basic proficiency in the Linux operating system and familiarity with command-line tools for system identification, log review, and basic diagnostics.

- Practical experience working with server IT hardware, enterprise-grade network switches, and fiber optic cabling.

- Proficiency with standard documentation and productivity tools including spreadsheets, with the ability to maintain logs, records, and operational reports.

- A proactive, responsible, and quality-focused approach to work with a strong commitment to safety and process adherence.

Core Physical Requirements:

- Ability to stand and remain on your feet for extended periods, typically four or more consecutive hours during active shift operations.

- Ability to safely lift, carry, and position equipment weighing up to 50 pounds unassisted, and heavier loads with appropriate team-lift protocols or mechanical aids.

- Comfortable working at heights including ascending and descending ladders, raised platform equipment, and elevated data center infrastructure.

- Ability to work in confined spaces such as under raised floors, within enclosed rack enclosures, and in cable management pathways.

- Comfortable working in environments with variable temperatures, including cold aisle containment zones and active cooling infrastructure.

- Manual dexterity sufficient to handle small form-factor components, precision cabling, and fine connector installations.

- Visual acuity sufficient to read equipment labels, small-form-factor interface indicators, and detailed wiring diagrams in variable lighting conditions.

- Ability to push or pull equipment carts, server sleds, and wheeled infrastructure weighing up to 500 pounds on level surfaces.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Valid Driving License 

- Project planning skills

- Health insurance: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and families.

- 401(k) plan: Up to 4% company match with immediate vesting.

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Remote work reimbursement: Up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

- Disability & life insurance: Company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.
Base Compensation Range
$30—$42 USD

- Competitive compensation

postings.title: Data Center Technician (Early Talent)
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
About the role

Duration: 3 months
Start date: January 2027
Compensation: Paid
Eligibility: Current University student (Computer Science or related field), Recent Graduate or Early Career specialist 
Work authorization: Permitted to work in the job's location

Program Overview 

The Nebius IT Data Center Technician Early Talent program is a structured 3-month work experience designed to introduce early-career candidates to hands-on enterprise data center operations. Early talent participants are embedded on the data center floor as active team members alongside experienced DC Technicians and senior operations staff. Over the program, participants develop foundational technical skills, learn Nebius operational standards and safety procedures, and progress from fully supervised tasks toward working with increasing independence as their competency is demonstrated and validated. 

What You Will Do 

As an IT Data Center Technician Early Talent participant, you will work on the data center floor under the direct guidance of an experienced DC Technician. All hands-on work begins under close supervision. As you demonstrate proficiency and adherence to Nebius safety and operational standards, you will progressively take on tasks with greater independence — working toward completing assigned activities with minimal supervision by end of program. 

Hardware & Infrastructure 

- Learn to identify, handle, and document server components, rack hardware, and data center equipment under direct technician supervision.

- Observe and assist with physical installation, cabling, and labeling of server hardware in rack enclosures under guidance.

- Assist with hardware inventory counts, asset tagging, and equipment tracking tasks as directed.

- Shadow and support technicians during component replacements, hardware decommissions, and equipment staging activities.

- Begin performing basic rack and stack tasks independently once foundational procedures have been trained and validated.

Cabling & Connectivity 

- Learn copper and fiber cabling standards, patch cord management, and labeling practices used at Nebius data center sites.

- Assist with cable organization, dressing, and documentation under direct technician guidance.

- Support connectivity checks and basic cable tracing tasks as assigned.

Documentation & Ticketing 

- Learn to use Nebius ticketing and asset management systems for logging work, updating hardware records, and tracking assigned tasks.

- Assist with documentation of equipment configurations, cable layouts, and maintenance activities under technician review.

- Begin entering and updating tickets independently for assigned work items once system proficiency is demonstrated.

Safety & Operational Standards 

- Complete all required Nebius data center safety training, site access procedures, and equipment handling certifications at program start.

- Follow all safety protocols, access controls, and site procedures at all times while on the data center floor.

- Never work unsupervised on live infrastructure or perform any task outside your validated scope without direct technician authorization.

- Observe and learn Nebius operational standards including shift handoff procedures, escalation practices, and incident documentation. 

Learning & Development 

- Participate in structured weekly check-ins with your assigned DC Technician mentor to review skill progression and address questions.

- Complete assigned Nebius training modules covering hardware fundamentals, data center operations, and safety throughout the program.

- Shadow senior technicians during escalated incidents, complex deployments, and hardware troubleshooting activities to build technical awareness.

- Actively engage during shadowing activities and take initiative in building your technical knowledge base throughout the 3 months.

Supervision & Progression 

Early talent participants begin under close, continuous supervision for all data center floor activities. This is not a desk-based or observation-only role — you are an active participant on the floor from day one. Progression follows a structured competency model: 

- Weeks 1–3: Orientation and shadowing. All tasks under direct supervision with step-by-step guidance. Focus on safety, site familiarity, system access, and equipment identification.

- Weeks 4–7: Assisted execution. You perform assigned tasks with your mentor present and reviewing all completed work before sign-off.

- Weeks 8–10: Supervised independence. You complete defined tasks independently within your validated scope, checking in at key milestones. Technician remains nearby and available.

- Weeks 11–12: Demonstrated competency. Qualified participants work with minimal supervision on fully validated tasks; technician oversight maintained for any task outside established scope.

Progression is based on demonstrated proficiency and adherence to Nebius standards — not time served. Participants who complete the program with strong evaluations will be considered for the Nebius early talent pipeline. 

Core Physical Requirements 

- Ability to stand and remain on your feet for extended periods during active floor operations.

- Ability to safely lift and position equipment up to 50 pounds unassisted; heavier loads with team-lift support.

- Comfortable working at heights including ladders, raised platforms, and elevated data center infrastructure.

- Ability to work in confined spaces such as under raised floors, within rack enclosures, and in cable management pathways.

- Comfortable in environments with variable temperatures including cold aisle containment zones.

- Manual dexterity to handle small form-factor components, precision cabling, and fine connector installations.

- Ability to push or pull equipment carts and server sleds up to 500 pounds on level surfaces.

Compensation
We offer competitive salaries, ranging from $48k- $72k OTE (On Target Earnings) based on your experience

Key employee benefits in the US:

- Health insurance: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and families.

- 401(k) plan: Up to 4% company match with immediate vesting.

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Disability & life insurance: Company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.
Base Compensation Range
$48,000—$72,000 USD

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

JDC Warehouse Specialist
Position Overview
The Warehouse Specialist runs day-to-day warehouse operations at a Nebius data center site. The role receives, stores and issues high-value hardware (GPU racks, servers, network equipment, spare parts), keeps stock and asset records accurate, and provides equipment to data center engineers on time.
The specialist is the site's hands-on link to the wider logistics function: Transportation and Transport Coordination for arrivals and pickups, Logistics Planning and 3PL Planning for schedules, Back Office for system records, and the Project Office for new processes and tools.
Key Responsibilities
1. Receiving & Dispatch
• Receive inbound shipments per the delivery schedule; check seals, packaging and contents against ASN, packing list and PO.
• Record damage and discrepancies with photos on arrival and hand them to Transport Coordination for insurance cases.
• Prepare outbound shipments and RMA returns: picking, packing, labelling, documents; hand over to carriers at the agreed pickup time.
• Follow handling standards for heavy, fragile and high-value equipment.
2. Provisioning to Data Center Operations
• Issue equipment and spare parts to DC engineers on time, according to requests and project priorities.
• Stage and kit hardware for rack deployments as agreed with ITDC and Project Managers.
• Keep a clear view of what is available on site and flag shortages to the Team Lead and Logistics Planning.
3. Inventory & Asset Control
• Post receipts, issues and transfers in ERP/WMS on the same day as the physical movement.
• Create inventory and asset records for received equipment, including serial numbers.
• Carry out cycle counts and annual stock takes; investigate and report discrepancies to Back Office.
• Keep the warehouse tidy, labelled and organized by location.
4. Security, Safety & Compliance
• Follow site security procedures for deliveries, access control and storage of high-value items.
• Apply safety rules for handling equipment and operating material handling equipment.
• Keep records complete and audit-ready (SOX, internal and external audits).
5. Process & Continuous Improvement
• Work according to global SOPs and site-specific instructions.
• Suggest improvements and report recurring issues to the Team Lead and the Project Office.
• Take part in pilots and rollouts of new processes and tools (WMS/TMS, automations) at the site.
6. Local Expertise
• Provide site-specific knowledge (access rules, dock limits, local carriers and customs specifics) to Transport, Planning and 3PL teams.
• Identify local operational risks and propose practical mitigation.
7. Add-on Roles (when assigned)
• + RMA: own RMA flows at the site — intake, documentation, return shipment, status tracking.
• + Key User (IRG / NetSuite / Project44): first-line support and training for colleagues on the system, test changes, collect feedback for the Project Office.
Expectations
Autonomy: Independently runs daily warehouse tasks at the site within SOPs; escalates discrepancies, damage and security issues to the Team Lead.
Impact: Keeps DC engineers supplied with the right hardware on time and keeps site stock accurate.
Communication: Clear, timely updates to the Team Lead, DC engineers and logistics teams.
Travel: Occasional support to other sites during launches or peaks.
Work Mode: On site; remote work not expected.

- Lead audits, inspections, and documentation for operational readiness 

- Act as the primary point of contact for facility related regulatory interactions

- Participate in FAT/SAT and system validation for critical equipment 

- Ensure smooth transition from construction to steady state operations 

- Validate that systems are operationally ready with proper documentation and procedures 

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- 

- Data Center Operations teams

- Act as the bridge between facilities and IT infrastructure, ensuring both layers operate seamlessly (a key distinction in Nebius environments) 

- Support broader operational goals around scalability, reliability, and standardization

- 7–10+ years of experience in data center or mission critical facilities operations 

- Strong hands on knowledge of critical infrastructure systems: 

- Electrical distribution (UPS, generators, switchgear) 

- Cooling systems (chillers, HVAC, CRAH/CRAC, liquid cooling exposure preferred) 

- Experience operating in high availability environments with strict uptime requirements 

- Proven experience managing vendors, maintenance programs, and incident response 

- Familiarity with BMS/DCIM systems and operational monitoring 

- Experience developing and enforcing SOPs, EOPs, and MOPs 

- Strong understanding of safety, compliance, and regulatory requirements 

Preferred:

- Experience in hyperscale, colocation, or AI/GPU driven data centers 

- Exposure to high-density environments and advanced cooling solutions 

- Experience supporting new site builds, commissioning, or expansions 

- Basic understanding of IT infrastructure (rack, power distribution, hardware) to effectively partner with engineering teams

- Health insurance: 100% company-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and families.

- Remote work reimbursement: Up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

The role

Nebius is seeking an experienced Deputy SOC Manager for its Security Operations Center (SOC). This role is a technical-leaning leadership position that owns the SOC's capability: the strategy and standards the regions run to, the technology the SOC runs on, and how the SOC gets better over time. This role reports to the SOC Manager, under the Detection and Response function within the CISO Office.

You are welcome to work in our offices in Tel Aviv, Israel.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Help define the SOC's strategy and roadmap with the SOC Manager, and turn it into priorities the regions can execute.

- Use operational metrics across regions to find where the SOC is weak and drive the improvements that fix it.

- Work with the Regional SOC Managers on resource allocation and consistency across regions, so each region runs to the same standard.

- Own SOC processes and runbook governance, keeping procedures current, consistent, and followed.

- Apply AI and automation to cyber defense, making the SOC faster and its analysts more effective, with judgment about where it belongs.

- Mentor the Regional SOC Managers and senior analysts as a peer and sounding board, developing the SOC's next layer of leadership. 

- Own how the SOC handles high-severity incidents: the escalation criteria, the coordination process, and the post-incident review, without running individual incidents.

- Support hiring and onboarding, participating in interviews and shaping the analyst ramp-up.

- Share the SOC Manager's accountability for the SOC's performance, stepping in across all of its responsibilities when needed.

We expect you to have: 

- 8-10 years in security operations, including at least 2 years managing people.

Technical Expertise

- Solid understanding of SOC tooling and workflows (EDR, SIEM, SOAR) at the depth needed to lead analysts and challenge investigations.

- Working knowledge of investigation methodology and the incident lifecycle.

- Understanding of attacker TTPs (MITRE ATT&CK) sufficient to assess investigation quality.

- Familiarity with cloud and cloud-native environments as they relate to SOC coverage.

- Certifications such as GCIH, GSOM, or CISM are an advantage.

Leadership & Communication

- Builds trust across teams, leading the SOC from transparency and consistency rather than authority.

- Calm during high-severity incidents, with the judgment to keep the team on the right priorities.

- Genuine investment in people, developing managers and analysts while holding a fair, high bar.

- Fluent in English, written and verbal, comfortable working with international teams and stakeholders
