Detection and Response 

The Detection and Response team is responsible for detection engineering, threat intelligence, and incident response across Nebius Cloud. Its goal is to improve and maintain Nebius's security monitoring capabilities, as well as to build and maintain an end-to-end Security Incident Response program - people, processes, and tools.

The Role

We're hiring a Detection & Response Engineer to build and run our D&R capability from the ground up. You'll work on detection engineering, threat intelligence, and incident response functions across Nebius Cloud. 

You'll be responsible for detection development, handling complex security incidents, forensics, and shaping the D&R strategy.

What you’ll do

- Detection development: maintain low false-positive and false-negative rates. Work closely with alerts consumers (20+ teams) to keep noise low and signal high, ensuring they can act quickly without missing genuine threats.

- Architect and operate detection coverage across our cloud and bare-metal environments

- Build and extend our internal D&R tools and pipelines - onboard new logs, build and automate response runbooks.

- Integrate threat intelligence into detection logic and IR playbooks, tracking adversary TTPs relevant to Cloud infrastructure

- Lead incident response end-to-end: scoping, containment, root cause analysis, post-incident reviews and controlling critical action items are closed to prevent future possible incidents.

- Partner with Compliance and Engineering teams to detect real threats while meeting the needs of both engineers and regulators.

- Define and report on D&R metrics: MTTD, MTTR, detection coverage, false positive rates, etc.

- Build and maintain Security Incident Response program: people, processes, tools.

- Build tools, runbooks, and on-call processes that scale as the company grows.

What we look for

- 6+ years in security operations, detection engineering, or incident response. 

- Deep hands-on experience with cloud-native environments (Kubernetes, Linux workloads, container-based infrastructure).

- Strong detection engineering skills: writing and tuning rules/detections in SIEM platforms (e.g., Chronicle, Splunk, Elastic) and SQL.

- Experience building or operating SOAR workflows and automating response at scale (ideally with Golang and Temporal).

- Working knowledge of threat intelligence frameworks (MITRE ATT&CK, Pyramid of Pain, Kill Chain) and how to operationalize them in detections.

- Solid IR fundamentals: memory forensics, log analysis, network traffic analysis, and post-incident reporting.

- Stakeholder management: able to coordinate across engineers, compliance, legal, executives during active incident phase. Serve as the primary owner and driver for complex changes, as a result of incidents post-mortem.

Nice to have

- Experience with AI/ML and GPU clusters related threats.

- Familiarity with eBPF-based detection or runtime security tooling (Falco, Tetragon).

- Background in threat hunting.

Experience

Job Summary

We are looking for a Optical Network/DWDM-IP Engineer to own the lifecycle of our optical transport network and its integration with the IP/MPLS core. You will be responsible for operating a hybrid ecosystem of short-haul (DC interconnects), metro, and long-haul DWDM systems. This role requires a "Full-Stack Transport" mindset—where you understand the physics of the fiber, signal modulation and could overview the logic of the ip/MPLS part of network.

Job Responsibilities:

- Hybrid Infrastructure Management: Configure, deploy, and scale multi-vendor DWDM systems (Ciena, Nokia-Infinera, ADVA/Adtran) to support 400G/800G+ coherent interfaces.

- Operational Excellence: Lead the troubleshooting of complex optical-to-IP failures, ensuring minimal MTTR for critical backbone spans and DCI links.

- Network Evolution: Design and test new optical solutions, focusing on Open Line Systems (OLS), disaggregated hardware, and pluggable coherent optics (QSFP-DD/OSFP).

- Automation & Data Integrity: Build and maintain the "Source of Truth" (Netbox-based) for lambdas, channels, and dark fiber assets; participating in automate commissioning via Python/gNMI.

- Strategic Collaboration: Work with Data Center Ops and IP Engineering to align optical capacity with traffic engineering (SR-MPLS) demands.

- Vendor & Asset Management: Manage relationships with dark fiber providers and channel suppliers; monitor performance against SLAs.

- 

We Expect You To:

- Deep Optical Expertise: Knowledge of ROADM networks and use-cases, optical amplification (EDFA/Raman), understand Coherent modulation formats and its characteristics in multi span long-haul scenarios.

- IP/MPLS Proficiency: Have an understanding of the IP/MPLS stack (any from BGP/OSPF/IS-IS) to perform initial debugs on packet-over-optical issues.

- Hands-on with Production Platforms: Direct experience with ADVA/Adtran platforms or Ciena /Nokia-Infinera

- Automation Mindset: good to read Python for automating routine of inventory synch

- Diagnostic Precision: Expert use of OTDR, OSA, and BERT equipment for characterization of short, middle, and long-haul fiber spans.

- Mobility: Willingness to travel to key sites in the USA/EU/APAC for critical hardware deployments and complex physical-layer audits.

Preferred Qualifications:

What you will own

- Develop and review electrical designs for new data center builds, expansions and major infrastructure upgrades across EMEA.

- Own HV and MV design inputs from utility point of connection through substations, transformers, switchgear and downstream distribution.

- Support equipment strategy and selection for transformers, MV and LV switchgear, UPS systems, generators, busway and associated protection and control systems.

- Ensure design compliance with applicable IEC and EN standards, local grid requirements, national regulations and Nebius engineering standards.

- Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, site acceptance testing, construction queries, commissioning and final handover to operations.

- Capture lessons learned and contribute to repeatable reference designs, specifications and technical playbooks for rapid EMEA deployment.

What success looks like

- Electrical design risks are identified and resolved before they affect cost, programme or energisation.

- HV and MV systems meet capacity, resilience, safety and maintainability requirements from day one.

- Consultants and suppliers receive clear decisions, standards and technical direction.

- Designs progress efficiently from concept to construction and through commissioning without loss of design intent.

What you will bring

- A degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

- Typically 5 or more years of electrical design experience in data centers, mission-critical facilities, utilities or large industrial environments.

- Strong practical knowledge of HV and MV distribution, substations, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, earthing and utility interconnection.

- Experience producing or reviewing construction-ready electrical design documentation and technical specifications.

- A solid understanding of UPS systems, generators, LV distribution and the interaction between facility power systems and high-density IT loads.

- Working knowledge of relevant IEC and EN standards and the ability to interpret local codes and grid requirements across different EMEA markets.

- Experience with power-system analysis software such as ETAP, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, SKM or equivalent.

- Strong technical judgement, attention to detail and the ability to explain complex trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Fluent professional English and willingness to travel across EMEA.

It would be an advantage if you have

- Experience with hyperscale, neocloud, GPU-dense or liquid-cooled data center environments.

- Experience with EPMS, BMS or SCADA integration and electrical commissioning.

- Knowledge of long-lead electrical equipment strategy and vendor qualification.

- Chartered Engineer status or an equivalent professional engineering certification.

- Experience with BIM, Revit or model-based multidisciplinary design coordination.

postings.title: Electrical Engineer- Data Centers
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The Infrastructure Acquisition Group

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group secures the land, power, and data center capacity that enables the Nebius AI Cloud. We identify where Nebius should grow next, structure the commercial agreements that make that growth possible, and partner across engineering, energy, finance, legal, and development to bring new AI infrastructure online.

We're a small, founding team building this function from the ground up across the Americas, leading the acquisition of colocation, build-to-suit, powered land, and other strategic infrastructure opportunities as one of the world's fastest-growing AI cloud platforms scales.

Examples of Problems We're Solving

Validate electrical feasibility before commercial commitment. A site or agreement is only as good as its ability to support the power capacity and distribution infrastructure required to run it. You'll lead electrical due diligence, utility interconnection analysis, and equipment feasibility review to inform Go / No-Go decisions before deals close.

Keep electrical design decisions ahead of development. Coordinate with Site Selection, Development, Engineering, and Delivery so power distribution topology, redundancy strategy, and equipment assumptions are validated early enough to protect schedule and budget once construction begins.

Build a repeatable technical evaluation program. Help establish the standards, design criteria, and technical readiness gates that will support electrical engineering review across every AI infrastructure acquisition in the Americas.

About the Role

As an Electrical Engineer, you'll provide the technical electrical engineering perspective across the acquisition and development lifecycle — from initial site and deal evaluation through construction readiness. Working within the Infrastructure Acquisition Group, you'll partner with Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Development, Energy, Finance, and Delivery to ensure every project's power distribution, utility interconnection, and equipment assumptions are technically sound before they move forward.

This is a build-phase role on a build-phase team. Many of the technical evaluation standards, design criteria, and readiness gates you'll use are still being written — in some cases, you'll help write them. We're looking for someone who can independently assess complex electrical infrastructure while helping build the systems that make every future evaluation faster, more predictable, and more scalable.

What You'll Own

- Lead electrical engineering evaluation of prospective sites, colocation capacity, and build-to-suit opportunities.

- Own technical assumptions for power distribution topology, capacity, and equipment strategy feeding the pre-construction risk register.

- Assess utility interconnection, on-site generation, and redundancy strategies (N, N+1, 2N) against site conditions and load requirements.

- Recommend Go / No-Go input on electrical feasibility as projects advance through key development milestones.

- Deliver technically validated electrical scope to the Delivery organization with complete documentation and minimized risk.

Technical Due Diligence & Feasibility

- Lead electrical due diligence on prospective sites, existing facilities, and colocation capacity under evaluation.

- Evaluate utility capacity, interconnection queue position, substation requirements, and on-site generation/UPS strategy against projected IT load.

- Assess electrical equipment availability, lead times (transformers, switchgear, generators), and vendor constraints that could affect schedule or capex.

- Ensure electrical assumptions are fully integrated into project budgets, capacity models, and schedules.

Design & Equipment Strategy

- Partner with Engineering to define power distribution topology and redundancy strategy appropriate to each site and deal structure.

- Evaluate EPMS/BMS controls integration and electrical system commissioning requirements early in the acquisition process.

- Provide technical input on switchgear, UPS, and generator selection, redundancy strategy, and capex trade-offs across candidate sites.

- Ensure electrical design intent is preserved as deals move from negotiation into development.

Construction Readiness

- Establish electrical technical readiness criteria as part of project handoff standards.

- Verify electrical design assumptions, equipment specifications, and capacity commitments are complete before turnover to Delivery.

- Identify and resolve electrical technical risks before they impact construction.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Serve as the primary electrical engineering technical interface across Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Development, Energy, and Delivery.

- Coordinate with consulting engineers, utility providers, equipment vendors, and commissioning agents to validate executable electrical strategies.

- Align internal stakeholders and external consultants to prevent technical scope drift as projects move from acquisition into development.

What Success Looks Like

- Ensure every acquisition is grounded in sound electrical engineering judgment before commercial commitment.

- Deliver predictable, technically validated power distribution and redundancy strategies across the portfolio.

- Identify and resolve electrical technical risks before they impact construction.

- Build trusted relationships with utility providers, equipment vendors, consulting engineers, and commissioning partners.

- Help build the technical standards and evaluation processes the Infrastructure Acquisition Group runs on as it scales.

What You'll Bring

- You're comfortable operating in ambiguity and building technical evaluation processes where none exist. You know how to independently assess complex electrical infrastructure while helping define how future projects should be evaluated.

- 8+ years of experience in data center electrical engineering, power systems design, or mission-critical electrical systems.

- Experience with medium-voltage distribution, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, and utility interconnection for high-density AI/hyperscale environments.

- Strong understanding of electrical capacity planning, redundancy topology (N, N+1, 2N), equipment selection, and capex trade-offs in data center design.

- Experience evaluating electrical feasibility of sites or facilities prior to commercial commitment.

- Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting hyperscale data center or AI infrastructure development.

- Experience with EPMS/BMS controls integration and electrical systems commissioning.

- Experience with utility interconnection agreements and interconnection queue strategy.

- Professional Engineer (PE) license or similar professional certification.

- Experience evaluating colocation or build-to-suit electrical infrastructure in a due diligence capacity.

Why Join Nebius

The infrastructure supporting AI is being built now. This is an opportunity to help define how Nebius evaluates and designs the power systems behind every AI infrastructure acquisition while helping build the function itself — the technical standards, design criteria, and evaluation framework that will support infrastructure investments across the Americas. You'll work on some of the industry's largest and most complex AI infrastructure developments while helping shape the physical foundation of the global AI economy.

postings.title: Engineering manager - Network infrastructure - APAC
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The Role
We're looking for an Engineering Manager for Network Infrastructure to own delivery of network infrastructure initiatives in APAC. This is not a role for someone who only coordinates tickets and status. It is a role for someone with an engineering skeleton: a person who has built, operated, broken and recovered things, and can earn the trust of SREs, SWEs, network engineers, and security and platform teams. We are at the early stage of our APAC expansion, so at first you will be hands-on: reviewing designs, stepping into incidents, and writing code or automation when the team needs it, with a high degree of independence from the European teams. As the organisation grows, the scope of the role will grow with it.

You own delivery. You will make important cross-team initiatives land: defining scope, aligning owners, exposing risks, driving decisions, tracking dependencies, and making sure we ship useful outcomes instead of half-finished initiatives. The job is not done when the technical pieces exist. It is done when engineers trust the tool, the NOC actually uses the workflow, alerts are actionable, runbooks are real, and the new way becomes the default way.

You stay technical. You don't need to be the deepest expert in every area, but you should be technical enough to understand real trade-offs: why rollback is not optional, why "just automate it" can create a bigger blast radius, why SLOs without ownership are decoration, and why network device CI/CD is very different from deploying a stateless service. You can read a design doc, challenge missing assumptions, notice unclear failure modes, and help the team turn a vague but important problem into an executable plan.

This is a high-leverage role in an early-stage and fast-scaling network infrastructure organisation. Many important systems are being built now: automation, observability, reliability standards, provisioning flows, operational safety, and cross-site consistency. You won't be maintaining a mature machine from the sidelines. You'll help shape how the machine works.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Set the engineering bar: code quality, design review, on-call and incident management practices, and operational standards

- Own end-to-end delivery of cross-team network infrastructure initiatives in APAC, from a vague problem statement to an executable plan to adoption

- Define scope and success criteria, align owners across SRE, SWE, network, security, platform and data center teams, and drive decisions to closure

- Review designs and technical proposals, challenge missing assumptions, and surface failure modes, dependencies and risks early

- Stay hands-on where it matters: step into incidents, write code or automation, and unblock the team

- Drive adoption: make sure tools and workflows become the default way of working, with real documentation, runbooks and feedback loops

- Keep stakeholders, including the European teams, informed with clear, honest status and coordinate across time zones

- Turn operational pain and engineering input into a clear, prioritized backlog

We expect you to have:

- 7+ years of experience in software, SRE, network or infrastructure engineering, including experience leading cross-team technical initiatives

- A real engineering background: you have built and operated production systems and can earn the trust of deeply technical teams

- Ability to read design docs and technical proposals, understand trade-offs, and ask sharp questions about reliability, rollback, blast radius and failure modes

- Strong understanding of infrastructure fundamentals (Linux, networking, automation, CI/CD) at the level needed to hold your own in technical discussions

- Proven ability to drive decisions and create clarity in ambiguous, fast-changing environments

We're looking for an Engineering Manager for Network Infrastructure to own delivery of network infrastructure initiatives in the US. This is not a role for someone who only coordinates tickets and status. It is a role for someone with an engineering skeleton: a person who has built, operated, broken and recovered things, and can earn the trust of SREs, SWEs, network engineers, and security and platform teams. As the organization grows, the scope of the role will grow with it.

You own delivery. You will make important cross-team initiatives land: defining scope, aligning owners, exposing risks, driving decisions, tracking dependencies, and making sure we ship useful outcomes instead of half-finished initiatives. The job is not done when the technical pieces exist. postings.title: Field CTO, Financial Services AI Infrastructure
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role:

Nebius is building the AI infrastructure that financial institutions will run AI on in production, from quantitative research and real-time risk to agentic workflows in banks and insurers.

The Field CTO for Financial Services is a senior technical leadership role at the intersection of production GPU infrastructure and the regulated business of financial services. You will lead the technical side of the vertical: the architecture conversation with CTOs and heads of research infrastructure, the technical content of regulated-buyer diligence, the reference architectures for financial workloads, and the product requirements that come out of the field.

Financial institutions buy AI infrastructure differently from most customers. Quantitative funds and AI-native fintechs buy GPU capacity directly and judge it on price-performance, availability, and how the cluster behaves under their own workloads. Banks and insurers add a second review: security, third-party risk, data residency, and exit planning are assessed before a deal reaches architecture discussions. You will earn the trust of both kinds of buyer and help make Nebius an approved supplier to financial institutions.

You will work alongside the Head of Financial Services, Sales, Security and GRC, Product, and Engineering. The role begins as a hands-on individual contributor, with a clear path to building and leading forward deployed engineers as the vertical scales.

This is a ground-floor opportunity to define how financial institutions run AI in production on a specialized AI cloud.

You are welcome to work remotely from the United States (New York City preferred). Travel expectations are 10% to 20% for customer visits, executive meetings, and key industry events.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Executive Technical Leadership: Serve as the technical face of Nebius to financial services customers, partners, and ecosystem stakeholders. Lead architecture workshops and technical discovery with CTOs, heads of quant and ML platforms, and CIOs, showing technical buyers how Nebius performs on their own workloads and institutions how the architecture fits their control framework.

- Lighthouse Deal Support: Partner with Sales leadership on strategic financial services deals, including workload-level cost comparisons against on-premises and hyperscaler options.

- Regulated-Buyer Diligence: Work with Security, GRC, and Legal to turn our SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications, and our alignment with frameworks such as DORA, into answers that third-party risk teams accept. Cover data residency, tenant isolation, key management, audit logging, resilience evidence, concentration risk, and exit and portability plans. Flag gaps early and bring them to Product as requirements.

- Architectural Guidance: Define reference architectures for financial workloads: quantitative research and backtesting, real-time risk and fraud inference, LLM and agentic workflows in KYC, AML, and document processing, and fine-tuning on sensitive proprietary data.

- Technical Product Strategy: Translate what you learn in accounts into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for Product, Engineering, and Infrastructure teams, and keep a structured feedback loop so R&D can act on them.

- Field Enablement: Act as a force multiplier for the sales organization by creating the technical narrative, reference architectures, and training materials that help Field SAs and sellers engage financial services buyers credibly.

- Ecosystem & M&A: Partner with ecosystem vendors (market and reference data providers, model risk and AI governance tooling, trading and risk platforms, systems integrators) to identify integration opportunities and evaluate potential technical M&A targets.

- Team Building: Build and lead forward deployed engineers as the vertical grows, setting how they scope, deliver, and hand learnings back to Product.

We expect you to have:

- 10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, platform engineering, distributed systems, or a closely related technical domain, including 5+ years in AI, ML, or MLOps with exposure to production or large-scale systems.

- Prior experience in a senior technical leadership role, for example Field CTO, CTO or technical co-founder of a fintech or AI-native company, head of quant or ML platform, or principal-level architect on a cloud vendor financial services team.

- Dual Competency: You can draw a distributed system on a whiteboard for engineers and explain its value and risk profile to a CIO or a Chief Risk Officer.

- GTM Fluency: Experience partnering with Sales to close large enterprise deals and enabling field teams with technical assets.

- Product-Minded Leadership: You have defined requirements from field evidence and shaped platform strategy. You are comfortable telling a customer no when a request would create technical debt, and proposing a better alternative.

- Mastery of the Stack: Expert-level, production-grade knowledge of GPU architectures, Kubernetes and Slurm orchestration including Soperator, high-performance and parallel file systems, and networking constraints (InfiniBand and Ethernet).

- Inference Optimization: You understand the nuances of model serving, including batch sizes, quantization, KV caching, and latency tradeoffs, and can architect for both massive throughput and latency-sensitive demands such as real-time risk and fraud scoring.

- Financial Services Fluency: First-hand experience in at least one of capital markets and quant research infrastructure, bank or insurer AI platforms, AI-native fintech, or an FSI technical role at a cloud or GPU provider, plus working knowledge of how regulated buyers review vendors: data residency, third-party and concentration risk, and model risk management expectations (for example SR 11-7 in the US).

- Builder Mentality: You arrive with your own point of view on where financial institutions are heading with AI infrastructure and pursue it without waiting to be directed. You are comfortable starting as a hands-on individual contributor and growing into a team.

- Public Technical Voice: Conference talks, writing, or open-source work that shows credibility with engineering and executive audiences.

- Communication: Strong executive presence, capable of influencing product teams and leadership through clarity and credibility.

- Comfort in Ambiguity: Experience operating in fast-moving environments (hyperscalers, cloud platforms, or advanced AI startups) where requirements are evolving.

 Preferred Qualifications:

- Hands-on experience with quantitative research infrastructure, low-latency trading systems, or model risk management in a regulated institution.

- Familiarity with the hybrid and on-premises GPU environments financial institutions run.

- Strategic Empathy: The ability to distinguish customers who need raw cluster access from those who need managed endpoints, and the judgment to prescribe the right path.

Why Nebius:

- Build Solutions: You will shape how financial institutions run AI in production on a specialized AI cloud.

- Scale: Opportunity to help build the Financial Services vertical from the ground up.

- Frontier Technology: Work at the frontier of AI infrastructure, agentic workflows, and financial intelligence alongside leading customers and partners.

- Strategic Impact: Real influence over product direction, platform strategy, and ecosystem development.

- Ownership: Join a team that values technical depth, ownership, and speed of execution.

- Mission: Help define how intelligence moves from the data center into trading desks, risk engines, and the operations of banks and insurers.

We give you the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technologies in data operations, cloud computing and infrastructure management. As global data center operations grow, there will be ample opportunities for career progression. As a Field Delivery Engineer, you will be leading the on-site delivery and deployment of hardware in new locations.You will plan, coordinate, and supervise activities from rack acceptance tests through full operational readiness, ensuring that servers, storage, networking, and supporting systems are installed and functioning according to specifications.

Planning & Coordination

- 

Own the hardware deployment plan for new sites, aligning timelines, scope, and resources with project stakeholders.

- 

Coordinate with logistics, supply chain, data center construction, and network teams to prepare GPU servers for delivery to customers.

- 

Verify all pre-deployment requirements (racks, power, cooling, connectivity) are met.

On-Site Delivery & Installation

- Supervise racking, cabling, and powering of hardware equipment.

- Ensure configuration, firmware upgrades, and integration with management systems follow standards.

- Work closely with vendors, contractors, and local staff during the installation phase.

Quality & Readiness

- Conduct functional checks, acceptance tests, and troubleshooting to confirm all systems operate correctly.

- Document installation steps, asset data, and lessons learned for future rollouts.

- Establish and maintain best practices for safe, efficient hardware deployment.

Collaboration & Reporting

- Act as the single point of contact on site for deployment activities, providing clear updates to project managers and leadership.

- Support transition of deployed hardware to operations teams for steady-state management.

- Contribute feedback to improve hardware design and deployment playbooks.

We expect you to have: 

- 

3+ years' experience in data center, hardware, or IT field delivery roles.

- 

Strong knowledge of server, storage, and network installation practices (racking, cabling, power, cooling).

- 

Strong hands-on experience working on datacenter floors with server hardware and Linux troubleshooting.

- 

Proven track record coordinating deployments across multiple stakeholders and vendors.

- 

Ability to read and interpret technical documentation, layouts, and wiring diagrams.

- 

Ability to perform deep diagnostics across hardware, firmware (BIOS/BMC), and Linux (logs, drivers, storage stack basics, performance triage).

- 

Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

- 

Willingness to travel frequently (sometimes at short notice).

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- 

Strong familiarity with GPU server platforms and tooling (for example: nvidia-smi, dcgmi, GPU and system logs correlation).

- 

Experience with Redfish and BMC tooling (ipmitool/Redfish), firmware lifecycle, and staged rollouts.

- 

Scripting skills (bash and basic Python) for log collection, triage automation, and simple reliability analysis.

- 

Exposure to OCP-based platforms and ODM manufacturing ecosystems.

- 

Familiarity with change management, asset tracking, and quality-assurance processes.

- 

Understanding of health, safety, and environmental standards in datacenter or industrial settings.

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

The role 

The Field Structured Cabling Senior Technician is responsible for managing and controlling structured cabling activities on-site, ensuring installations are completed according to approved designs, specifications, and project schedules. This role serves as the main field interface between the design team, project managers, contractors, logistics, and vendors.

The position is field-focused and plays a key role in translating design drawings into accurate, well-executed cabling installations while maintaining proper change control and documentation.

You’re also welcome to work on-site at our office in Amsterdam, the Netherlands. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- 

Coordinate and control structured cabling activities from early project stages through deployment completion.

- 

Supervise and direct external contractors, including planning and controlling cable pull schedules in alignment with Project Managers and other infrastructure teams.

- 

Ensure cabling installations follow approved DWG drawings, specifications, cable routes, and quantities.

- 

Track cable pulls, routes, and completion status; document progress and any deviations.

- 

Apply minor layout updates directly in DWG files when required; escalate major design changes to the Structured Cabling Design team.

- 

Oversee installation of cable tray and containment systems based on project timelines and priorities.

- 

Maintain accurate field documentation and update tracking spreadsheets or deployment systems.

- 

Support as-built documentation by ensuring all field changes are captured.

- 

Coordinate with logistics teams and vendors to ensure timely delivery, handling, and staging of cabling materials, including large palletized deliveries.

- 

Act as the on-site point of contact for structured cabling-related coordination and issue resolution.

We expect you to have: 

- 

2–3+ years of relevant field experience in structured cabling or telecommunications.

- 

Proven hands-on experience with structured cabling deployment (fiber and copper).

- 

Strong knowledge of fiber-optic infrastructure, including:

- 

Fiber patch panels

- 

Enclosures and fiber management systems

- 

Cassettes and distribution frames

- 

Ability to read, interpret, and apply AutoCAD / DWG drawings in the field.

- 

Experience supervising or coordinating contractors and field teams.

- 

Solid understanding of cable pathways, tray systems, and routing best practices.

- 

Experience with field documentation, cable tracking, and change control.

- 

Strong communication and coordination skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- 

Participation in large-scale structured cabling projects, preferably in data center environments.

- 

Understanding of and hands-on experience working in data center environments, including operational, safety, and access requirements.

- 

Basic knowledge of network topologies and how structured cabling supports network and IT infrastructure.

- 

Hands-on experience working as part of a cable pulling team.

- 

Experience with high-density fiber environments and large cable volumes.

- 

Familiarity with structured cabling standards (TIA, ISO, BICSI).

Knowledge of or exposure to fiber fusion splicing.

postings.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Physical AI Infrastructure
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Nebius is hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to work alongside Physical AI customers, shape our core infrastructure products, and test ideas for what we should build next.
You will work with enterprises, ISVs, and digital-native companies running training, simulation, synthetic data, evaluation, and model serving workloads. By understanding their systems and helping them reach production, you will uncover requirements that inform our Cloud, Serverless, and Token Factory teams. The goal is to connect needs across Physical AI industries with product decisions, including improvements that benefit enterprise customers more broadly.
You will also investigate opportunities for new Nebius products. You will develop hypotheses about unmet needs, examine demand and existing alternatives, and build prototypes to test with customers. Your findings will help determine which opportunities deserve investment and what an initial product should deliver.
The work is hands-on. You will write code, deploy and benchmark models, build agents, and troubleshoot infrastructure alongside customer engineers.

The position is part of the Physical AI go-to-market team, with close collaboration across customers, NVIDIA, Product, and Engineering.

What you will do

- Work with customer engineers to understand their workloads, infrastructure constraints, and production requirements.

- Translate Physical AI use cases into requirements that Cloud, Serverless, and Token Factory teams can use, backed by measurements and customer evidence.

- Identify enterprise adoption barriers and common needs across industries. Work with Product and Engineering to assess gaps and test improvements with customers.

- Build agents that set up, run, and debug Physical AI workloads, connecting them to clusters, schedulers, storage, and model servers.

- Deploy and benchmark open-weight models with serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, then tune them for customer workloads.

- Build prototypes and run technical evaluations to answer specific questions about performance, reliability, and product fit.

- Assess demand and existing alternatives for opportunities outside current product teams’ scope, then build where there is a clear market.

- Debug across Python, agents, model servers, Kubernetes, GPUs, networking, and storage. Turn successful setups into reusable scripts, deployments, and short guides.

What we are looking for

- Three or more years in software engineering, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, ML infrastructure, or similar, including ownership of a production service, cluster, or platform.

- Experience working directly with customers or external engineers to scope problems, run evaluations, and explain technical tradeoffs.

- Ability to turn an unfamiliar customer problem into concrete infrastructure requirements.

- Practical experience building with LLMs or agents, at work or independently, with an understanding of their internals (e.g., transformers, KV caching, or tool calling) and how to evaluate their outputs.

- Familiarity with enterprise infrastructure requirements, including identity and access management, network isolation, security, monitoring, and reliability.

- Strong Python and Linux skills: you can read unfamiliar code, automate a setup, and debug from logs and metrics.

- Practical experience with containers and Kubernetes, including configuration, networking, storage, and scheduling.

- A record of getting useful software working with incomplete requirements, measuring results, and following through with the people using it.

Helpful experience

- Enterprise customer engineering, solutions architecture, consulting, or taking a new product from an initial customer problem to adoption.

- Distributed compute such as Ray, Slurm, Spark, or multi-GPU jobs.

- NVIDIA GPU workloads, including memory management, drivers, CUDA, NCCL, and monitoring.

- Model serving with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or TGI.

- Robotics, simulation, synthetic data, reinforcement learning, world models, or tools such as Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Omniverse, and Cosmos.

- Infrastructure automation and enterprise integrations, including Terraform, CI/CD, private connectivity, and identity federation.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

- Define KPIs and continuously improve fraud detection, investigation, and response processes. 

- Drive awareness programs to educate employees and executives on phishing, social engineering, executive fraud, and insider threat risks.

- 5+ years of experience in cyber security, fraud investigations, digital investigations, cyber intelligence, or incident response.

The role

We are seeking a General Manager, Data Center to lead the organizational build-out, hardware deployment, operational readiness, and ongoing performance of our gigawatt-scale data center campus in Independence, Missouri. This is an on-site leadership role with responsibility for the Independence campus.

You will have autonomy to design the campus organization, select your leadership team, define reporting lines, and establish the operating model within agreed budgets and company standards. You will own operational readiness and campus performance across critical facilities and IT infrastructure, aligning people, systems, and service partners to deliver reliable customer capacity.

The facility is currently under construction. You will partner with construction, engineering, and critical facilities teams to align facility completion, commissioning, and handover with hardware deployment and operational readiness. You will establish the operating team and coordinate GPU, server, network, and storage installation, integration, acceptance testing, and cloud readiness with the responsible technical teams and service providers.

This role offers the opportunity to shape the operating practices that support Nebius as its AI infrastructure business grows.

Your responsibilities will include:

Organization Design and Leadership

- Design and build the campus organization, including functional leadership, building and shift coverage, reporting lines, and clear decision authority.

- Hire, lead, and develop directors, data center managers, and operations teams in partnership with Talent Acquisition and HR.

- Own the phased workforce plan, aligning recruitment, training, contractor support, and leadership coverage with hardware deployment, acceptance testing, and production milestones.

- Establish performance expectations, consistent technical competency standards, and succession plans that support reliable campus operations and sustained performance.

Operational Deployment and Readiness

- Own the integrated operational readiness plan connecting facility completion and handover milestones, equipment delivery, hardware installation, network and storage integration, staffing, and customer service readiness.

- Coordinate with construction and facilities teams to verify power, cooling, and space readiness before deployment; manage dependencies and escalate gaps that could delay bringing capacity into service.

- Define operational acceptance criteria for the campus and deployed infrastructure, coordinate readiness and acceptance testing with technical owners, and accept or withhold operational handover against agreed requirements.

- Ensure trained teams, tested procedures, critical spares, asset records, monitoring, and vendor support are in place before production operations begin.

- Coordinate GPU, server, network fabric, storage, and cloud readiness with technical owners, and jointly confirm that released capacity can support customer workloads.

- Sequence hardware installation, integration, and production changes to protect live environments as additional compute capacity comes online.

Campus Operations and Reliability

- Own end-to-end campus operations across critical facilities and IT infrastructure, delivering agreed uptime, performance, and service levels.

- Establish 24/7 coverage, maintenance governance, change control, incident command, root-cause analysis, and business continuity practices.

- Ensure clear responsibility across power, liquid cooling, controls, hardware, networking, and cloud interfaces; hold owners accountable for corrective actions.

- Use monitoring, automation, and performance reporting to improve deployment throughput, repair turnaround, reliability, and operating efficiency.

- Own campus operating budgets, workforce costs, vendor expenditure, and forecasts within delegated authority; contribute to capital planning and investment priorities.

- Align power, cooling, rack space, equipment, and staffing capacity with deployment plans, and address constraints affecting customer commitments.

- Establish asset inventory, receiving, logistics, critical spares, repair, warranty-return, and secure disposition processes.

- Track budget variance, rework, delayed capacity, and operational losses; drive corrective actions and report financial impacts clearly.

- Build leadership succession and delegation practices that sustain reliable operations and develop future infrastructure leaders.

- A track record of building and scaling organizations and leading managers across multiple technical and operational functions.

postings.description:

About the Role 

We are looking for an experienced Global Power Procurement and Strategy Manager to lead the end-to-end procurement and commercial management of electricity across the company’s global sites. 

This role owns the complete power procurement lifecycle, from collecting and validating consumption data, forecasting demand and analyzing energy markets, through developing sourcing strategies, conducting competitive procurement processes, negotiating agreements and managing the resulting power portfolio. 

The successful candidate will combine strong knowledge of electricity markets with commercial, analytical and procurement capabilities and will work closely with Data Center Operations, Infrastructure, Engineering, Finance, Treasury, Legal, Tax and Sustainability teams. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Own the global electricity procurement strategy (including PPAs) for the company’s data centers, offices and other operational sites.

- Establish and maintain a consolidated view of electricity consumption, demand forecasts, costs, tariffs, suppliers, contractual commitments and renewal dates across all locations.

- Develop short-, medium- and long-term power procurement strategies tailored to the regulatory, operational and commercial conditions of each market.

- Monitor electricity markets, pricing trends, regulatory developments, grid conditions and relevant geopolitical and supply risks.

- Evaluate available procurement structures, including utility supply agreements, fixed and indexed pricing, spot-market exposure, Power Purchase Agreements and renewable energy solutions.

- Develop financial models, market comparisons, sourcing scenarios and business cases to support management decisions.

- Translate complex market, technical and regulatory information into clear commercial recommendations.

- Lead RFI and RFP processes, including market engagement, proposal evaluation, supplier selection and award recommendations.

- Lead commercial negotiations with utilities, electricity suppliers, energy producers, aggregators, advisors and renewable energy providers.

- Manage the contracting process from commercial alignment through internal approvals, negotiation and execution.

- Partner with Legal, Finance, Treasury, Tax and Sustainability teams to assess contractual, financial, accounting, regulatory and risk implications.

- Manage electricity supply contracts throughout their lifecycle, including renewals, pricing mechanisms, volume commitments, guarantees, indexation and termination provisions.

- Monitor contracted versus actual consumption, expenditure, supplier performance and exposure to market prices.

- Support the review and validation of electricity invoices, tariffs, grid charges and other energy-related costs.

- Identify cost-saving, cost-avoidance and risk-reduction opportunities across the global power portfolio.

- Develop dashboards and management reporting covering consumption, expenditure, forecast accuracy, market exposure, contract status, savings and key risks.

- Support the company’s sustainability and renewable energy objectives, including the evaluation and procurement of Guarantees of Origin, Renewable Energy Certificates and equivalent local instruments.

- Establish global policies, governance standards, procurement processes and contracting principles for electricity sourcing.

- Coordinate external energy advisors and consultants where specialized local-market support is required.

Required Qualifications 

- Bachelor’s degree in Energy, Engineering, Economics, Finance, Business, Supply Chain Management or a related field.

- At least 7 years of relevant experience in electricity markets, energy procurement, utilities, energy trading, commercial energy advisory or strategic sourcing.

- Demonstrated experience managing electricity sourcing or supply agreements for large commercial or industrial consumers.

- Strong understanding of electricity market structures, utility tariffs, wholesale pricing, grid charges and regulatory frameworks.

- Experience with electricity purchasing models such as fixed-price, indexed, spot-market and long-term power supply agreements.

- Proven experience leading complex sourcing processes and negotiating high-value, multi-year commercial agreements.

- Strong financial and quantitative capabilities, including cost modelling, forecasting, scenario analysis and business-case development.

- Ability to interpret consumption data and convert market information into actionable sourcing recommendations.

- Strong contract, stakeholder and project management capabilities.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

- Ability to work independently and manage multiple markets, projects and decision timelines simultaneously.

Preferred Qualifications 

- Experience supporting data centers, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications or other energy-intensive operations.

- Experience with Power Purchase Agreements and renewable energy procurement.

- Knowledge of European and US electricity markets and regulatory environments (Preferably including additional markets).

- Familiarity with energy-risk management, hedging principles, balancing arrangements and volume-risk mechanisms.

- Experience working with Treasury, Finance, Sustainability, Engineering and Data Center Operations teams.

- Experience establishing global energy-data management and reporting processes.

- Experience working within a rapidly growing international technology organization.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. The role 

We are seeking a GPU Cluster Architect to drive the design of our next-generation AI infrastructure. In this high-impact, hands-on role, you will make end-to-end architectural decisions across compute, networking, and storage — ensuring our platforms can meet the massive scale, performance, and reliability requirements of modern AI workloads.

This is a high-impact, hands-on architecture role where you’ll define how tens of thousands of GPUs are interconnected, cooled down, powered, and optimized across multiple data center sites.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Cluster Design: Architect scalable GPU cluster topologies including compute nodes, interconnect (InfiniBand, Ethernet), storage, and control planes.

- Performance Modeling: Analyze AI/ML workloads (e.g. LLM training, inference) to inform design tradeoffs across latency, bandwidth, and GPU density.

- Network Architecture: Align with network architect relevant design and validate low-latency, high-throughput interconnects (e.g., InfiniBand HDR/NDR, RoCEv2) at POD and DC scale.

- Storage Integration: Work with storage teams to optimize performance for training datasets, checkpointing, and others.

- Reliability & Monitoring: Understand and analyze signal from monitoring systems to the detect flows in design

- Collaboration: Partner with site reliability, networking, storage, and DC engineering teams to operationalize and scale your architecture.

We expect you to have: 

- 5+ years of experience designing clusters.

- Deep understanding of modern GPU architecture (NVIDIA, AMD, etc.).

- Experience with HPC interconnects (InfiniBand & RoCE).

- Solid background in systems architecture, networking, and hardware reliability.

- Experience in scripting for automation and telemetry pipelines (Python, Go, etc.)

- Hold regular 1:1s, provide feedback, set expectations, and support engineers in their development.

- Assign responsibilities and make sure engineers have clear ownership during deployments.

- Identify skill gaps and build technical depth within the team.

- Support hiring, onboarding, and performance management as the team grows.

- Remove blockers for engineers and escalate organizational or technical issues when necessary.

Own deployment engineering planning

- Represent Deployment Engineering in project planning and synchronization meetings for new data center launches.

- Understand upcoming deployment milestones and translate them into engineering resource requirements.

- Plan engineer allocation across multiple parallel projects and deployment phases.

- Make sure the right technical expertise is available for hardware bring-up, testing, troubleshooting, and acceptance.

- Identify resource conflicts and delivery risks early rather than reacting to them during deployment.

- Maintain a clear view of team capacity, project priorities, travel requirements, and upcoming workload.

Drive technical execution

- Ensure deployment testing and hardware bring-up are executed consistently and to the required quality level.

- Support engineers with complex hardware, firmware, Linux, and systems troubleshooting.

- Step into critical technical issues when deeper investigation or coordination is required.

- Drive problems toward a clearly identified failure domain, root cause, or actionable escalation.

- Coordinate with R&D, DC Operations, vendors, ODMs, and other engineering teams when issues cross organizational boundaries.

- Make sure deployment findings result in fixes, documentation, tooling, or process improvements rather than remaining one-off solutions.

Improve how we deploy infrastructure

- Build repeatable deployment processes, standards, checklists, and troubleshooting practices.

- Improve the quality and predictability of hardware testing and acceptance.

- Identify recurring deployment problems and drive systemic fixes upstream into factory, hardware, firmware, tooling, or operational processes.

- Improve handover from Deployment Engineering to steady-state operations.

- Help develop automation and tooling that reduce manual work and increase deployment scale.

We expect you to have: 

- Strong experience with server hardware, data center infrastructure, or large-scale systems deployment.

- Experience leading engineers, either as a formal people manager or as a strong technical/team lead with clear ownership for other engineers.

- Ability to plan resources and coordinate engineering work across several projects running in parallel.

- Strong ownership mindset and the ability to operate in environments where procedures are incomplete and problems are not yet well understood.

- Ability to challenge assumptions, investigate beyond the immediate symptom, and drive issues to resolution.

- Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively with project managers, engineering teams, operations, and external vendors.

- Comfortable working directly in data centers and traveling across EMEA when required.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Linux troubleshooting skills and a solid understanding of modern server architecture.

- Experience diagnosing hardware and infrastructure problems across components such as CPU, memory, NVMe, PCIe, NICs, BMC, BIOS, and firmware.

- Experience deploying GPU or AI infrastructure at scale.

- Experience with large server fleets or hyper-scale environments.

- Experience working with ODMs or server vendors during production, deployment, or failure investigation.

- Experience with automated hardware validation or fleet-level testing.

- Experience building a deployment, infrastructure, SRE, hardware reliability, or similar engineering team.

What success looks like

You will not be measured by how many individual servers you personally troubleshoot or deploy.

Success means that Deployment Engineering operates as a reliable function: projects know when and how to engage the team, engineers are assigned to the right work, technical problems are driven to resolution, deployment risks are visible early, engineers are developing, and new infrastructure can move from delivery to operational readiness predictably.

You will be the person the Head of Hardware Delivery and Deployment can rely on to run the EMEA Deployment Engineering function day to day, while also continuously improving how the team operates and scales.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
Role Overview

This is a leadership role spearheading Nebius’s communications across Europe and the Middle East: you will develop strong regional narratives, provide senior counsel, manage and develop the team, and lead consequential communications and stakeholder situations.

Reporting to the global Head of Communications, you will translate business priorities into compelling stories and a practical regional strategy. You will connect local developments to the company narrative and adapt them to the audiences and circumstances of each market.

We need an outstanding storyteller with the gravitas, experience and judgment to personally lead high-stakes situations involving multiple stakeholders. You will know when to shape the narrative, handle a difficult relationship or lead a response yourself, and when to give colleagues the authority and support to deliver.

What success looks like

The region has clear priorities, strong narratives, credible stories and trusted stakeholder relationships. Important situations receive the right senior attention. Colleagues understand their responsibilities, exercise sound judgment and develop under your leadership. Global colleagues have early visibility of consequential regional developments.

Key Responsibilities

Shape regional narratives and strategy

- Develop communications strategy and strong narratives for priority European and Middle Eastern markets, linked to business priorities and the wider company story.

- Identify compelling stories and the evidence behind them. Make clear choices about audiences, markets and investment; adapt narratives locally while keeping core facts consistent.

- Advise senior leaders on positioning, communications opportunities and reputation risks. Define measurable objectives and use evidence to improve the programme.

Lead communications and consequential stakeholder situations

- Build trusted relationships with regional business leaders, partners and relevant business, technology, infrastructure and local media. Create a sustained pipeline of credible stories.

- Shape and deliver the narratives, writing, executive counsel and stakeholder engagement that need your senior experience. Delegate other work with clear briefs, authority and quality standards.

- Lead regional communications for customer, partner, product and infrastructure developments.

- Partner with country managers and public affairs colleagues on communications and local engagement around physical infrastructure builds.

Manage people and regional resources

- Set team priorities and responsibilities, coach colleagues, manage performance and support their development. Build the capability and confidence to make sound decisions.

- Balance workloads and recommend where additional skills or capacity are needed. Recruit and onboard approved hires.

- Direct agencies and partners through clear briefs, budgets and performance reviews. Judge what to own personally, what to delegate and when to intervene; retain accountability for quality and outcomes.

Coordinate across the business

- Work closely with stakeholders across Nebius – GTM country leads, Marketing, Business Diplomacy, Product, Research, Technology, subject experts and other colleagues – to coordinate on issues including regional priorities, policy, local engagement and reputation management.

- Coordinate with US, APAC and global communications leaders on announcements, issues and executive visibility. Maintain early visibility of consequential developments within appropriate confidentiality controls.

Key Qualifications and Experience

What we need

- A strong record of senior communications leadership in Europe and the Middle East, with substantial in-house technology-company experience and the ability to operate credibly across the region.

- Outstanding storytelling and narrative-development skills: translating complex business and technology priorities into compelling, credible stories for different audiences and markets.

- Demonstrated people-management experience: setting goals, coaching, managing performance and developing capable colleagues.

- Gravitas and senior experience to personally lead high-stakes, multi-stakeholder situations, advise business leaders and navigate competing interests with sound judgment.

- Evidence of judging when personal involvement is essential and when to delegate, alongside strong media relationships and experience directing agencies and regional resources.

- Outstanding English writing, editing and spoken communication, with the curiosity and rigor to understand complex technology and build accurate narratives.

Helpful experience

- AI, cloud infrastructure, enterprise technology or another complex B2B sector; regional expansion, infrastructure investment or a publicly listed company.

- Substantial Middle East communications work, relevant media relationships and additional regional language skills.

- Agency experience is valuable alongside substantial in-house experience; an agency-only background does not meet the role’s requirements. Journalism experience can be beneficial.

Competencies and Behavioural Traits

Strong narrative judgment, senior presence, clear prioritisation and calm leadership. A capable people manager who develops others, gives direct feedback and delegates with purpose. Takes personal ownership where the stakes or complexity require senior experience, while keeping regional and global colleagues aligned. Comfortable with ambiguity, iteration, course-correction, experimentation and (occasionally) failure.

What We Offer

A senior communications leadership role shaping narratives and stakeholder relationships across Europe and the Middle East, working closely with business and global communications leaders and developing the regional team.

The Role

The Head of Employee Relations will define and lead our global approach to employee relations and performance management. Combining strategic leadership with operational expertise, the role will ensure employee matters are handled consistently, fairly and within applicable legal requirements. The role will build effective relationships with works councils and other employee representative bodies and partner closely with senior leaders, People teams and employment lawyers. 

Responsibilities 

Employee Relations and Performance Management strategy and governance 

- Define and implement the organisation’s employee relations and performance management strategy, principles and operating model.

- Define the organisation’s approach to performance management, including the effective management of underperformance.

- Establish clear, practical policies, processes and templates for performance concerns, grievances, disciplinary matters and other employee relations cases.

- Provide senior oversight and advice on complex, sensitive or high-risk cases.

- Help managers address concerns early, set clear expectations and reach fair, proportionate outcomes.

- Ensure practices are applied consistently while accommodating local legal requirements.

- Identify recurring themes and recommend preventative or organisation-wide action.

- Partner with relevant People teams to align employee relations and performance practices with the broader talent and reward strategy. 

Works Council and employee representation 

- Build constructive relationships with works councils, employee forums and other representative bodies.

- Define the organisation’s approach to engaging, informing and consulting with employee representatives.

- Advise leaders on consultation requirements, timelines and communications, particularly during organisational change.

- Support consultation and negotiation processes and ensure agreed actions are implemented.

- Build internal capability so that leaders and People teams engage with representative bodies confidently and consistently. 

Legal and risk management 

- Partner with in-house and external employment lawyers to ensure decisions and processes operate within applicable legal thresholds.

- Translate legal advice into clear and commercially practical recommendations.

- Monitor relevant employment law developments and update organisational practices where required.

- Identify and manage the legal, financial and reputational risks associated with employee matters. 

Leadership and capability 

- Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, People partners and Legal.

- Build manager and People-team capability through clear guidance, training and coaching.

- Establish appropriate case-management, governance and reporting standards.

- Use case data and employee insights to identify trends, risks and areas for improvement. 

What you bring

- Significant senior-level experience in employee relations, employment law, HR or a related discipline.

- Experience defining and implementing an employee relations strategy or operating model.

- Strong knowledge of performance management, investigations, disciplinary and grievance processes, organisational change and dispute resolution.

- Experience working with works councils, employee representatives or trade unions, ideally across multiple jurisdictions.

- Strong employment law knowledge and experience working with internal or external legal counsel.

- Sound judgement and the ability to balance legal risk, employee experience, organisational values and commercial priorities.

- Strong influencing, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills.

- Comfortable working both strategically and hands-on with complex cases.

- Experience leading a team or specialist function is desirable. 

What success looks like

- Employee relations and performance matters are handled consistently, fairly and efficiently.

- Managers and People teams have clear, practical guidance and tools.

- Works council and employee representative relationships are constructive and well managed.

- Legal and organisational risks are identified early and managed appropriately.

- Employee relations insights lead to meaningful improvements across the organisation.
