Nebius is an AI-centric purpose-built for intensive GPU using company. As our global footprint accelerates toward multiple gigawatts of capacity, we are establishing our regional network engineering presence in the Asia-Pacific region.

We are looking for a hands-on, high-autonomy Network Engineer / Senior Network Engineer to drive the build-out, connectivity, and continuous production operations of our regional data centers, PoPs, and transport fabrics across APAC, with connectivity to EU/the US region and IP transit/PNI services.

In this role, you will be the boots-on-the-ground technical authority in the region. You will bridge low-level physical bringing-up with modern CLOS fabrics, collaborating closely with our core engineering teams in the EU (Amsterdam HQ) and the US within a global follow-the-sun operational model.

This position is fully remote within the APAC region (preferred hubs: Singapore, India), with periodic domestic/regional site visits and occasional sync trips to our engineering headquarters in Amsterdam.

Your Responsibilities Will Include:

- End-to-End Infrastructure Ownership: Take complete operational and deployment ownership of the network stack across APAC sites—ranging from Day-0 Out-of-Band (OOB) part of network as seed , console setups, and management L2 switches to high-scale leaf-spine frontend fabrics (EVPN/VXLAN) 400g/800g/1,6T ready and regional DCI/Backbone boundaries (BGP/MPLS/SRv6).

- High-Autonomy Site Bring-up & Operations: Act independently to triage, debug, and deliver connectivity in fast-moving, greenfield colocation environments. Make sound architectural and operational calls on short notice when counter parts oversight is offline.

- Global Collaboration & Follow-the-Sun Alignment: Partner tightly with core architecture, backbone, and platform teams in the EU and US. Own regional operational handoffs, participate in global on-call rotations, and conduct changes in coordinated regional maintenance windows.

- Team Scaling & Knowledge Offloading: As the APAC team expands, actively onboard new engineers, write rigorous runbooks, and offload operational pipelines to incoming peers to keep the team scalable.

- Dynamic Execution: Operate effectively in a high-velocity environment where quarterly business priorities, cluster locations, and deployment schedules adjust dynamically to customer demand.

We Expect You to Have:

- Proven Production Routing & Switching Depth: Solid hands-on experience operating Service Provider or Scale Data Center networks. Deep working knowledge of BGP, IS-IS (or OSPF), EVPN/VXLAN, SR-MPLS/SRv6, ECMP load balancing, and L3VPN architectures.

- CLOS Fabric & L2–L4 Diagnostics: Strong diagnostic instincts in multi-tier Clos fabrics. Practical mastery of TCP/IP, IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack environments, packet analysis (tcpdump, Wireshark), interface error rates, and QoS queue behavior.

- Full-Stack Network Mindset: Comfort with the entire operational pipeline: you are equally willing to console into an unconfigured management switch/OOB router at an unpolished greenfield site and tune BGP policy on multi-terabit edge borders (Juniper preferred, or relevant cisco/nokia).

- Vendor Agility: Practical configuration and troubleshooting experience across modern network operating systems (Juniper Junos, Cisco IOS-XR, Arista EOS, or NVIDIA/Cumulus).

- Startup Agility & Timezone Flexibility: Proven ability to self-direct, prioritize backlogs under ambiguous requirements, and maintain effective working overlap with European (CEST) and US (EST/PST) teams when critical milestones hit.

- Communication: Professional working proficiency in English, with the ability to document complex systems clearly and communicate concisely under Sev-1 pressure.

- Practical scripting and network programmability skills (Python or Go, Git, NetBox, telemetry pipelines).

- Practical exposure to high-performance AI networking: RoCEv2 (PFC, ECN/DCQCN, MCR) fabrics.

- Experience interfacing directly with regional APAC telecom carriers, dark fiber providers, subsea consortiums, and local Internet Exchanges (e.g., Equinix IX, JPIX, SGIX).

Offensive security

The internal offensive security team is responsible for the penetration testing program, red team engagements, and offensive research aimed at uncovering sophisticated attack scenarios targeting high-value assets across the Nebius Cloud stack.

The Role

We're hiring an Offensive Security Engineer to join us at Nebius. You'll design and execute adversarial simulation across our cloud platform - attacking the same infrastructure our customers depend on - and translate findings into measurable security improvements.

This is a hands-on engineering role within Product Security Team. You will be part of an internal red team, establish a penetration testing program, and conduct research to uncover sophisticated attack scenarios targeting high-value assets across the Nebius tech stack.

What you’ll do

- Validate and extend early-stage Secure SDLC threat models via continuous penetration testing, assessing threat severity and mitigation status while challenging assumptions made during threat modeling and system development. Automate routine validations to keep pace with increasing feature flow, reserving manual analysis for genuinely complex cases.

- Plan and execute full-scoped red team engagements against Nebius cloud platform - including compute, storage, inference, networking, orchestration layers, and internal tooling. Identify threats, which are able to impact an organization's operations. Work closely with Detection & Response and other security engineering teams to run purple team exercises, validate detection coverage, and close gaps collaboratively.

- Research novel attacks against GPU infrastructure (e.g., closed-source firmware and vendor driver binaries, device passthrough exploits, SR-IOV/IOMMU misconfigurations, RDMA/InfiniBand fabric attacks, etc.), the inference stack (e.g., vLLM, TRT-LLM), and AI platform managed services (e.g., managed Slurm). Assess tenant-isolation boundaries and how they can be broken at the low-level stack

- Conduct targeted assessments of new products and infrastructure changes before they ship.

- Deliver clear, actionable reports for both technical audiences and leadership - with prioritized findings and remediation guidance.

- Establish red team processes, tooling, and a methodology that scales as the platform grows.

What we’re looking for 

- 6+ years in offensive security - penetration testing, red teaming, or adversary simulation 

- Deep experience attacking cloud-native environments: Kubernetes privilege escalation, cloud IAM abuse, virtualization and container escapes.

- Strong fundamentals across the attack lifecycle: initial access, persistence, lateral movement, data exfiltration.

- Proficiency developing custom tooling and post-exploitation capabilities (Python, Go, or similar).

- Experience running purple team exercises and working constructively with blue teams.

- Ability to write clear, senior-level reports with business-contextualized risk (not just raw findings) that engineers can easily use.

Nice to have

- Experience attacking ML infrastructure, model serving pipelines, or GPU clusters.

- Reverse engineering and exploits development experience

- Application security experience

- Familiarity with eBPF bypass techniques or kernel-level exploitation.

- Background in vulnerability research or CVE discovery.

- Experience with cloud provider internals (hypervisor/networking layers).

- Presenting your security research at conferences like BlackHat/DefCon, etc.

Why this role at Nebius

- Attack surface that's genuinely novel - GPU clusters, AI platforms, multi-tenant cloud at scale.

- Work alongside world-class engineers on infrastructure that powers frontier AI.

- Competitive compensation with equity upside in a Nasdaq-listed, high-growth company.

- Flexible, remote-first culture

Hiring process

- Recruiter's chat (30mins)

- Live-coding interview (60mins) to asses basic coding skills 

- Security interview (60mins) to asses domain expertise

- Security System Design interview (90mins) to assess practical experience

- (Optional) Technical deep dive (90mins) to present a complex and impact project. 

- Final interview to close the hiring process (45mins)

postings.title: Principal ML Solutions Architect - Token Factory
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

This position sits within Nebius Token Factory, our serverless platform for running and customizing open-source LLMs in production. Token Factory allows for serverless inference and fine-tuning (LoRA, full FT, RFT) backed by in-house optimizations like custom speculative decoding, quantization, cache-aware routing and dedicated endpoints. Customers come to us to move from prototype to scaled production without the cost and complexity of building and tuning their own inference stack.

We're looking for a Principal ML Solutions Architect to act as the most senior technical authority for customers leveraging Token Factory's serverless inference and fine-tuning platforms. Beyond designing and implementing optimized inference and fine-tuning workflows, you will set technical direction across our largest and most strategic accounts, own the hardest performance and quality problems end to end, mentor other Solutions Architects, and serve as a primary technical voice shaping the platform roadmap with backend, product, and research teams.

You’re welcome to work remotely from the United States.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Own the most complex, highest-stakes customer engagements from architecture through production across multiple modalities, driving measurable business value

- Optimize LLM inference at the framework and hardware level and codify the resulting best practices into reusable playbooks for the team

- Lead supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning efforts to maximize model quality

- Design and implement production-ready LLM solutions using Token Factory's inference services

- Provide deep technical expertise in prompt engineering, RAG architectures, model selection, and cost/performance trade-offs at scale

- Partner closely with product, engineering and research to surface customer needs, prototype platform features, and directly influence the roadmap

- Guide customers from PoC to production with a focus on performance, reliability, and cost efficiency — and define the standards by which the team does so

- Mentor Senior and mid-level Solutions Architects; raise the technical bar of the team through review, enablement, and knowledge sharing

- Represent Token Factory externally through talks, blog posts, and conferences

We expect you to have: 

- 8+ years of experience in ML/AI systems, with at least 4 years focused on LLMs and generative AI

- Demonstrated technical leadership: owning ambiguous, high-impact problems end to end and influencing decisions across teams and customers

- Expert knowledge of the LLM ecosystem: model architectures, fine-tuning approaches, and inference internals

- Deep, hands-on command of inference optimization: quantization, KV-cache management, batching, routing, etc.

- Hands-on experience with:

- Running LLMs in production at scale: deploying, operating, and debugging inference workloads down to the framework level

- LLM fine-tuning, including SFT/LoRA and data preparation/curation; experience with RL-based fine-tuning

- LLM evaluation: building task-specific benchmarks and offline/online eval pipelines, including LLM-as-a-judge setups

- Inference frameworks and libraries (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM), including the ability to read, modify, and contribute to their internals

- Deploying LLM-powered applications using APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-source models

- Strong Python programming skills

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts to diverse audiences, from engineers to executives

It would be an added bonus if you have: 

- Contributions or maintainership in major OSS inference/ML projects (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM)

- Published research, conference talks, or widely-read technical writing in the LLM/serving space

- Deep work with multimodal AI models (vision-language, speech)

- Proficiency with DevOps tooling (Docker, Kubernetes) and infrastructure-as-code

- Experience building or owning internal tooling/automation for ML workflows at scale

Preferred technical stack:

- Programming Languages: Python

- ML Frameworks and Libraries: vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang, Transformers, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs

- MLOps and DevOps tools: Kubernetes (K8s), Docker, Git

- Cloud Platforms: AWS (SageMaker, Bedrock), GCP (Vertex AI), Azure (Azure ML)

The role

Nebius is looking for a Principal Product Marketing Manager to set the direction for our enterprise story: the narrative, messaging, and go-to-market strategy that turn Nebius’s full-stack differentiation into pipeline and revenue with mid-market and enterprise buyers.

You’re welcome to work remotely in the United States.

This is a role for a recognized enterprise product marketing leader from B2B cloud or AI infrastructure who has shaped category narratives and led complex go-to-market motions, and can prove it through the messaging they built, the programs they orchestrated, and the revenue outcomes behind them. You understand the AI cloud stack well enough to earn credibility with engineering leaders, and you know what it takes to move a complex enterprise buying committee (CIOs, CTOs, Chief Data/AI Officers, CISOs, VPs of Infrastructure, security and procurement teams) through a 6–18-month cycle. You set the strategy and frameworks that others execute against, and you measure your impact in win rates, pipeline influenced, and field adoption, not assets shipped.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Product Marketing, you will be the senior voice for how Nebius positions itself to the enterprise and a force multiplier for the organization: setting the enterprise go-to-market strategy across product lines, guiding and mentoring other product marketers, and equipping sales, solutions architecture, and partnerships to carry the story into the field. You will work directly with senior leaders across product, engineering, sales, and executive leadership as a trusted strategic partner.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Set the enterprise narrative and positioning strategy. Own the enterprise layer of the Nebius story end to end, from our “ultimate AI cloud” positioning down to persona-specific messaging, and define the frameworks and standards that other product marketers and content teams build on. Translate our differentiators and each layer of the cloud stack (custom GPU servers, AI orchestration and MLOps tooling, Token Factory, and our agentic layer) into credible messaging that resonates with technical and business decision-makers alike.

- Lead enterprise go-to-market strategy across products and launches. Define the enterprise go-to-market plan across the Nebius portfolio, set priorities and sequencing for major launches, and drive alignment across product, sales, solutions architecture, partnerships, and marketing. Make the trade-offs on where to focus and invest, and hold cross-functional teams accountable to shared outcomes.

- Design and own the enterprise customer journey. Own the logic and strategy of the 6–18-month enterprise buying cycle, defining what moves a buyer at each stage from awareness to evaluation, decision, and expansion. Set the plays, content, and touchpoints for each stage and partner with digital/ABX and field marketing leaders to sequence and target them by account, using ABM platforms such as 6sense or Demandbase.

- Build the enterprise business case. Develop the messaging, proof, and business case around what enterprises actually evaluate: total cost of ownership, reliability and SLAs, security and compliance, data sovereignty and residency, migration risk, and vendor lock-in. Equip Nebius to win through security review, procurement, and the CFO’s office, and engage directly with senior executives on strategic deals.

- Drive enablement strategy and field adoption. Set the enablement strategy for sales, solutions, and partner teams, and ensure they can articulate Nebius’s value to every persona on the buying committee: first-call decks, battlecards, discovery guides, ROI/TCO tools, objection handling, and competitive positioning against hyperscalers and neoclouds. Lead enablement programs and measure adoption, win rates, and deals influenced.

- Own competitive and category positioning. Maintain a sharp, evidence-based view of the AI enterprise infrastructure landscape and help shape how the category is defined. Turn market and competitive intelligence into positioning the field can defend and campaigns can lead with, and keep Nebius’s differentiation current as the market moves.

- Lead the enterprise content and proof strategy. Define the enterprise asset strategy and own quality across the library: solution briefs, white papers, reference architectures, case studies, web pages, webinars, and videos. Personally produce the most strategic pieces and set the bar for the rest.

- Elevate communications, analyst, and investor narratives. Shape the enterprise narrative for press moments, site launches, analyst briefings, and investor materials, in close coordination with comms, legal, and executive leadership. Serve as a spokesperson and subject matter expert for the enterprise story in analyst, customer, and industry settings.

- Champion the voice of the customer. Partner with sales and customer marketing to build a pipeline of references, case studies, and proof points, and bring enterprise pain points and wins back into product strategy and messaging.

- Mentor and multiply. Coach and guide other product marketers and cross-functional contributors, establish best practices, messaging methodologies, and workshop frameworks (such as SCIPAB), and raise the quality and consistency of product marketing across the organization.

- Contribute strategically at the leadership table. Bring ideas, challenge assumptions, and help shape how we position Nebius in a fast-moving AI infrastructure market. Act as a trusted partner to product, engineering, sales, and partnerships leaders, with a seat at the table, not just as a content source.

We expect you to have: 

- 8+ years in product marketing, with a strong track record leading enterprise go-to-market in cloud infrastructure or AI infrastructure (ideally the AI cloud market) at a growing, modern company.

- Proven ownership of the enterprise segment across the marketing lifecycle, with the ability to speak to win rates, pipeline data, and revenue impact on significant enterprise deals.

- Demonstrated experience setting go-to-market strategy and leading cross-functional launches across multiple products or product lines, influencing leaders without direct authority.

- Hands-on experience designing and orchestrating multi-stage enterprise customer journeys across long (6–18 month) buying cycles, and running account-based programs on ABM platforms such as 6sense or Demandbase in partnership with digital/ABX teams, with clear, measurable outcomes.

- Strong technical understanding of AI/ML workflows and the AI cloud infrastructure stack: GPU platforms and the NVIDIA ecosystem, networking, storage, IaaS, inference, and ML tools (e.g., PyTorch, Ray, Slurm, MLflow, Kubernetes, inference and agentic platforms), with the ability to go deep with engineers and translate up for executives and business buyers.

postings.title: Product Manager - Anti Fraud
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

We run a large-scale GPU cloud and AI infrastructure platform. Fraud and abuse — stolen payment cards, fake sign-ups, compute mining, credential abuse, and coordinated free-tier exploitation — directly threaten platform economics, capacity availability for legitimate customers, and our standing with payment providers and cloud partners. 

As Product Manager, Anti-Fraud, you own the product roadmap for the systems that detect, prevent, and respond to fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle — from onboarding and payment through to ongoing consumption. You sit at the intersection of Trust & Safety, Payments/Billing, Risk, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and you balance two goals in constant tension: stop bad actors and keep friction near zero for real customers. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Own the end-to-end anti-fraud product roadmap: signup/KYC checks, payment fraud detection, account takeover protection, and compute-abuse (e.g., crypto mining, resource reselling) prevention. 

- Own the rules and risk-scoring surfaces — the tooling that lets analysts and data scientists define, test, and deploy detection rules and ML models with clear guardrails and audit trails. 

- Own the manual review and case-management experience for the Trust & Safety operations team, including queues, evidence views, and action workflows (block, limit, step-up verification, release). 

- Own customer-facing friction points — verification flows, step-up challenges, and appeals — designed to minimize false positives and protect the legitimate user experience. 

- Identify fraud and abuse incidents early — define the signals, alerts, and thresholds that surface incidents before they scale, and own the detection surface that flags them. 

- Participate in incident reviews and post-mortems, capturing root causes and turning each finding into concrete improvements to detection rules, models, and the roadmap. 

- Ensure timely response to active incidents — drive fast triage, clear ownership, and mitigation, working alongside Trust & Safety, Engineering, and Data Science to contain impact. 

- Write clear PRDs and specs that translate fuzzy risk problems into shippable engineering and data-science work. 

- Partner with Analytics team on detection models — defining the problem, labels, and success criteria, and deciding where rules vs. ML are the right tool. 

- Run experiments and monitor rollouts, watching both fraud-catch metrics and false-positive / customer-friction impact. 

- Work with Legal/Compliance to keep detection and enforcement aligned with payment-network rules, KYC/AML expectations, and data-privacy requirements. 

- Track and report on fraud loss, chargeback rate, false-positive rate, review throughput, and time-to-detection. 

We expect you to have: 

- Proven product management experience in fraud, risk, trust & safety, or payments. 

- Strong analytical skills — comfortable with data, SQL or equivalent, and reasoning about precision/recall trade-offs and metrics. 

- Ability to make decisions under ambiguity and to balance security, business, and customer-experience priorities. 

- Solid collaboration with engineering and data science; you can hold a technical conversation about signals, features, and model behavior. 

- Exposure to cloud, SaaS, marketplace, fintech, or infrastructure products. 

- Understanding payment fraud, chargebacks, KYC/AML, or device/network signals (fingerprinting, velocity, IP reputation). 

It would be an added bonus if you have: 

- Familiarity with ML-based detection systems and their operational lifecycle (drift, retraining, monitoring). 

- Experience with abuse patterns specific to compute or GPU platforms (mining, credential stuffing, free-tier farming). 

Benefits & Perks:

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group secures the land, power, and data center capacity that enables the Nebius AI Cloud. We identify where Nebius should grow next, structure the commercial agreements that make that growth possible, and partner across engineering, energy, finance, legal, and development to bring new AI infrastructure online.

We're a small, founding team building this function from the ground up across the Americas, leading the acquisition of colocation, build-to-suit, powered land, and other strategic infrastructure opportunities as one of the world's fastest-growing AI cloud platforms scales.

Transform acquisitions into data center-ready projects. A signed agreement is only the beginning. You'll lead development planning, utility coordination, permitting, consultant management, and infrastructure planning to prepare projects for successful delivery.

Build a repeatable development program. Help establish the standards, development governance, readiness gates, and project controls that will support AI infrastructure development across the Americas.

As a Development Manager, you'll lead the development of AI infrastructure projects across the Americas from executed agreement through construction readiness. Working within the Infrastructure Acquisition Group, you'll partner with Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Engineering, Energy, Finance, Legal, and Delivery to transform acquisitions into fully defined, development-ready projects.

This is a build-phase role on a build-phase team. Many of the development standards, governance processes, readiness gates, and project controls you'll use are still being written—in some cases, you'll help write them. We're looking for someone who can independently lead complex infrastructure developments while helping build the systems that make every future project faster, more predictable, and more scalable.

What You'll Own

- Lead the development of AI infrastructure projects from executed agreement through construction readiness.

- Own integrated development roadmaps, schedules, budgets, milestones, and the pre-construction risk register.

- Coordinate permitting, entitlement, utility planning, infrastructure planning, and owner obligations.

- Recommend Go / No-Go decisions as projects advance through key development milestones.

- Deliver development-ready projects to the Delivery organization with complete documentation and minimized risk.

Development Planning & Governance

- Lead development activities from executed agreement through construction readiness.

- Develop and manage integrated development roadmaps, schedules, budgets, and key milestones.

- Own the development budget, schedule, assumptions, and risk register throughout the pre-construction lifecycle.

- Lead weekly development reviews and executive readiness meetings, and recommend Go / No-Go decisions as projects advance through key milestones.

Infrastructure & Utility Coordination

- Coordinate infrastructure planning for electrical service, substations, fiber, water, sewer, stormwater, and transportation access.

- Coordinate permitting, utility planning, entitlement activities, infrastructure planning, and owner obligations.

- Partner with utility providers, municipalities, engineering teams, and consultants to validate executable development plans.

- Ensure infrastructure assumptions are fully integrated into project budgets and schedules.

Construction Readiness

- Establish development readiness criteria and project handoff standards.

- Verify permits, utility agreements, infrastructure planning, owner deliverables, and development obligations are complete before turnover.

- Deliver projects to the Delivery organization with complete documentation, defined scope, and minimized development risk.

- Identify and resolve development risks before they impact construction.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Serve as the primary development interface across Site Selection, Technical Due Diligence, Engineering, Energy, Finance, Legal, and Delivery.

- Coordinate architects, civil engineers, environmental consultants, surveyors, permitting specialists, and other external partners.

- Align internal stakeholders and external consultants to prevent scope, schedule, and cost drift throughout development.

What Success Looks Like

- Transform acquisitions into data center-ready development projects.

- Deliver predictable development schedules, budgets, and readiness milestones.

- Identify and resolve development risks before they impact construction.

- Build trusted relationships with utilities, municipalities, consultants, and development partners.

- Help build the standards and processes the Infrastructure Acquisition Group runs on as it scales.

What You'll Bring

- You're comfortable operating in ambiguity and building processes where none exist. You know how to independently lead complex infrastructure developments while helping define how future projects should be executed.

- 8+ years of experience in data center development, industrial development, infrastructure development, land development, or mission-critical projects.

- Experience managing permitting, entitlement, utility coordination, consultant management, and development planning activities.

- Strong understanding of infrastructure development, owner's budgeting, development scheduling, risk management, and pre-construction planning.

- Experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams across engineering, utilities, design, legal, and construction.

- Excellent communication and executive presentation skills.

- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Real Estate Development, Urban Planning, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience supporting hyperscale data center or AI infrastructure development.

- Experience with utility coordination, entitlement strategy, infrastructure planning, and owner's representation.

- Experience with self-development or joint venture delivery models.

- Professional Engineer (PE), PMP, or similar professional certification.

Why Join Nebius

The infrastructure supporting AI is being built now. This is an opportunity to help define how Nebius transforms acquisitions into development-ready AI infrastructure while helping build the function itself—the governance, development standards, readiness framework, and operating model that will support infrastructure investments across the Americas. You'll work on some of the industry's largest and most complex AI infrastructure developments while helping shape the physical foundation of the global AI economy.

Nebius is building the infrastructure that powers the next generation of AI — and we're scaling fast. In line with our values, we're committed to an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive, and we're looking for an experienced Environmental, Health & Safety Manager to set the direction, standards and capability that keep our expanding operations safe, compliant and sustainable. 

This is no ordinary role. We need a decisive, credible leader who owns the regional EHS agenda — someone who can set strategy, build a high-performing team, and act as the trusted voice of EHS at leadership level, while staying close enough to the detail to guide, challenge and support when it matters most. 

This is a genuine opportunity to shape how EHS operates as Nebius scales. You'll have real autonomy to set priorities, build capability across your team and sites, and influence decisions at a regional and business level — backed by strong support from senior stakeholders and a growing global EHS function. 

You'll be accountable for the performance, maturity and culture of EHS across your region — leading through others, setting the standards your team and sites work to, and stepping in personally when situations demand calm, experienced judgement under pressure. Above all, you'll help make sound EHS practice a source of competitive advantage for Nebius, not a compliance exercise. 

What you'll do 

- Set and own the regional EHS plan, turning policy and legislation into clear priorities and controls for your sites.

- Translate the global EHS strategy into everyday practice across your region, making sure teams are well supported and equipped with the toolkit to advance site EHS performance.

- Lead, manage and develop local teams — setting objectives, building capability, and owning outcomes.

- Act as the senior EHS voice with regional and site leadership — advising on risk and holding the business to account.

- Own regional governance and assurance — audits, inspections, and the quality of your team's risk assessments and controls.

- Take personal command of major incidents and crises — leading investigations, building a learning culture, and reporting to executive level with composure under pressure.

- Set the standard for construction, commissioning, operations and other high-risk activity, equipping specialists to manage risk on the ground.

- Own the regional EHS performance narrative — turning data into insight that drives decisions and accountable action plans.

- Review EHS data and performance metrics regularly, acting on trends and insights to drive continuous improvement across the region.

- Support the wider environmental and sustainability agenda, partnering with teams to embed it across your region.

- Represent Nebius with regulators, industry bodies and partners, protecting its credibility on EHS.

- Champion Nebius's culture and values, embedding EHS as core to how the business operates. 

What we're looking for

- Partner with Sales, Legal, Finance, and Customer Success teams to facilitate seamless contract execution and customer onboarding.

- Ensure customer contracts and commercial terms are accurately reflected across internal systems and operational workflows.

- Handle both routine and non-standard operational cases, providing solutions and escalating issues when needed.

Billing Operations & Revenue Support

- Support billing processes including mechanics, configurations, and tool management to ensure accurate invoicing.

- Review and validate sales requests to make sure contractual terms and billing details are correctly reflected in internal systems.

- Coordinate with Finance regarding invoice or payment discrepancies.

- Participate in the NBA Ops Channel on-call rotation under supervision, handling routine cases.

- Support preparation of standard payment and operations reports.

- Ensure proper documentation and smooth communication across teams.

- Ensure adherence to pricing guidelines and margin policies when processing sales requests and contracts.

- Identify operational gaps or blockers in deal execution and escalate proactively

- Partner closely with Sales teams to ensure operational readiness and smooth deal execution.

We expect you to have: 

- 1–3 years of experience in Sales Operations, Commercial Operations, Revenue Operations, Billing Operations, Finance Operations, or a related analytical role.

- Experienced with billing or CRM & ERP tools (e.g., Net.Suite, Salesforse, Hubspot)

- Understands the commercial impact of operational decisions, including pricing and margin considerations.

- Strong attention to detail and willingness to learn.

- Good organizational and communication skills.

- Good communication skills in English

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Experience in SaaS or technology companies.

- Exposure to contracts, invoices, or payments processes.

Cybersecurity Architecture

- Define and maintain the organization’s cybersecurity architecture, reference architectures, security standards, and design principles.

- Lead security architecture reviews for new systems, applications, infrastructure, and technology initiatives.

- Establish security-by-design principles across cloud, infrastructure, application, and platform architectures.

- Identify architectural security gaps and drive remediation roadmaps.

Kubernetes and Cloud-Native Security

- Design and implement security architectures for Kubernetes-based environments and cloud-native platforms.

- Secure Kubernetes clusters, control planes, worker nodes, namespaces, workloads, and cluster-to-cluster communications.

- Secure container images and registries, including image scanning, provenance, signing, and supply chain integrity.

- Implement runtime security, workload isolation, threat detection, and monitoring for containerized environments.

- Secure Kubernetes ingress, service-to-service communications, APIs, and service mesh architectures where applicable.

- Establish security controls for container orchestration platforms across development, testing, and production environments.

- Evaluate and manage Kubernetes security risks, misconfigurations, excessive privileges, exposed services, and vulnerable workloads.

- Lead security architecture across AWS and/or Microsoft Azure, including cloud-native and hybrid environments.

- Define secure cloud landing zones, identity and access management, network segmentation, encryption, logging, and key management.

- Implement preventive and detective security controls using cloud-native security services and centralized policy enforcement.

- Drive cloud security posture management and remediation using CSPM, CNAPP, and related technologies.

- Ensure alignment with organizational security requirements and relevant industry standards.

- Integrate security throughout the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), from design and coding to deployment and production operations.

- Partner with R&D, DevOps, and Platform Engineering teams to embed security into CI/CD pipelines.

- Define and implement automated security controls, including SAST, DAST, Software Composition Analysis (SCA), secrets detection, and container image scanning.

- Establish secure coding standards, threat modeling practices, API security requirements, and secure software supply chain controls.

- Promote developer-friendly security tooling and reusable security patterns that minimize friction and accelerate delivery.

- Drive remediation of vulnerabilities and architectural weaknesses in collaboration with engineering teams.

Security Engineering and Risk Management

- Develop technical security standards, architecture patterns, and security control baselines.

- Conduct threat modeling, attack-path analysis, architecture risk assessments, and security design reviews.

- Define security requirements for identity, access, data protection, network security, workload isolation, and observability.

- Collaborate with Security Operations to improve security telemetry, detection capabilities, and incident readiness.

- Evaluate emerging security technologies and recommend solutions based on risk reduction, operational effectiveness, and architectural fit.

- Track security findings and drive measurable improvements in the organization’s security posture.

We are seeking a Security Solutions Engineer with a strong background in strategic solution evaluation, vendor assessment, and hands-on Proof-of-Concept (PoC) validation. This role is a crucial bridge between identifying customer security requirements and implementing best-in-class, enterprise-grade solutions. You will be responsible for defining the criteria, researching the market, and executing technical validation for all major security tooling and services adopted by the company. 

Key responsibilities: 

1. Strategic Research & Requirement Definition 

- Threat-to-Solution Mapping: Proactively analyze customer expectations, regulatory/compliance drivers, and threat models to define precise functional and non-functional requirements for new security solutions. 

- Market Analysis & Scouting: Conduct thorough market scans to identify cutting-edge security products, platforms, and vendors across key domains (e.g., CSPM/CNAPP, DLP, IAM/IGA, EDR/XDR, data security, Kubernetes security, and AI/ML security). 

- Vendor Due Diligence: Evaluate potential vendors based on technical capability, security posture, integration requirements, roadmap, data residency/compliance, and support quality, and shortlist candidates for the PoC phase. 

2. Technical Validation & Proof-of-Concept (PoC) Leadership 

- PoC Planning & Design: Develop detailed, objective, and threat-aligned test plans and success criteria for all security solution Proof-of-Concepts (PoCs), including quantitative success metrics, coverage of key attack scenarios, and opportunities for automation. 

- Hands-on Environment Setup: Independently architect and deploy isolated PoC environments that accurately simulate our production infrastructure (e.g., setting up cloud VPCs, Kubernetes clusters, integrating with test data via IaC, and mimicking typical workloads).

AI is moving faster than any single product team can track. Nebius is expanding across serverless, databases, MLflow, MLOps, Physical AI, and HCLS — and customers arriving with complex, real-world ML workloads need more than documentation. This role exists to close that gap: someone who can prototype what's possible, accelerate customers through their first 90 days, and feed hard-won field insight back into the product roadmap.
This role sits at the intersection of deep ML engineering and product impact. You'll spend roughly half your time in the field — helping new customers move from POC to production, running technical onboarding, and working hands-on through their ML stack. The other half you'll spend building — prototyping applied AI use cases that show what's possible on the platform, going deep on emerging techniques before they're mainstream, and turning that expertise into concrete product direction.
This is not a presales role. You get your hands dirty every day.

What success looks like in 12 months

- The product and sales teams have a library of working, polished demos they reach for on calls

- Enterprise customers you've touched have meaningfully faster time-to-value than those you haven't

- At least 2–3 product changes were shipped because of feedback you originated

- The team understands where applied AI is heading 6–12 months from now, partly because you told them

Your responsibilities will include:

- Build prototypes and demos across the product portfolio — serverless inference, databases, MLflow, MLOps, and vertical use cases in Physical AI and HCLS — that become assets for sales, product, and engineering teams

- Support new customers hands-on through POC design, technical onboarding, and validation; act as the bridge between their ML team and the platform during the critical first months

- Go deep on emerging applied AI — new training techniques, inference optimizations, agentic architectures, new frameworks — and turn findings into working prototypes, writeups, and product recommendations

- Feed the product roadmap with specific, grounded feedback; be the voice of "here's what broke in three customer POCs last month and here's what needs to change"

- Develop reusable technical assets — notebooks, reference architectures, benchmark results — that reduce onboarding friction at scale

- You've worked with enterprise ML teams — whether as a solutions engineer, customer engineer, or an ML engineer who collaborated closely with customers

- You communicate with calibration: you can explain activation checkpointing tradeoffs to an ML engineer in the morning and the cost implication to a CTO in the afternoon

- Experience in any of our vertical domains: Physical AI / robotics / simulation, HCLS (drug discovery, medical imaging, clinical NLP), or enterprise AI application development

postings.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Efficient LLM Inference & Model Optimization
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on.

Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production.

Your responsibilities

- Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff.

- Develop and evaluate methods spanning quantization, quantization-aware training (QAT), distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, KV-cache compression, long-context inference, MoE routing, and model/runtime co-optimization.

- Build prototypes using PyTorch, Triton, CUDA-adjacent tooling, or inference-serving frameworks, and collaborate with MLEs and platform engineers to turn them into production components.

- Research LLM request routing and scheduling strategies, including cache-aware load balancing and prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD). Evaluate how queueing, KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and prefill/decode capacity allocation affect latency, throughput, and serving cost.

- Investigate multi-node inference for dense and mixture-of-experts models, including wide expert parallelism (WideEP). Study expert placement, load imbalance, and computation/communication trade-offs, and use the findings to guide model and system architecture choices.

- Develop rigorous evaluations covering quality, latency, throughput, numerical stability, memory footprint, tail latency, and cost per token. Compare serving architectures under consistent workload conditions and GPU budgets.

- Work with MLE, GPU kernel, backend infrastructure, product, and customer teams to select research priorities with measurable production impact.

- Share results through internal reports, technical blogs, papers, and open-source artifacts, and mentor engineers and scientists on experimental design, scientific rigor, and model/system trade-offs.

Must-haves

- A PhD in computer science, machine learning, ML systems, computer systems, computer architecture, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.

- A strong publication record or equivalent research artifacts in ML, ML systems, efficient inference, model compression, quantization, distillation, serving systems, or related areas.

- Strong Python and PyTorch implementation skills, with the ability to turn ideas into experiments and working prototypes.

- Deep knowledge of LLMs, VLMs, transformer inference, decoding algorithms, model compression, quantization, and production-serving trade-offs.

- Strong experimental design skills covering ablations, baselines, metrics, statistical reasoning, and failure analysis.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-haves

- First-author publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP, ASPLOS, OSDI, SOSP, ISCA, or HPCA.

- Experience deploying ML models or inference optimizations in production.

- Experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUDA, or PyTorch internals.

- Experience applying post-training, SFT, DPO, RLHF, RLAIF, preference optimization, or synthetic data generation to inference quality or efficiency.

- Open-source research artifacts, widely used benchmarks, technical blogs, or invited talks demonstrating contributions to efficient AI systems.

- Research or implementation experience in one or more areas of distributed inference system architecture, such as LLM request routing, PDD, multi-node serving, or MoE expert parallelism, including WideEP.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

postings.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Efficient LLM Inference & Model Optimization
postings.location: Amsterdam, Netherlands; Berlin, Germany; London, United Kingdom; Poland; Prague, Czech Republic; Tel Aviv, Israel; Zurich, Switzerland
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Nebius Token Factory is looking for scientists who can turn frontier LLM and VLM inference bottlenecks into research questions, conduct rigorous experiments, and translate their findings into production capabilities. You will own focused research and optimization projects, write strong code, and produce prototypes, publications, and technical artifacts that engineers can build on.

Your research will span quantization, distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, and model/runtime co-optimization, alongside inference engines and distributed inference architectures. You will investigate how these approaches interact, evaluate their trade-offs across model quality, latency, throughput, memory footprint, and cost per token, and work with engineering teams to bring promising results into production.

Your responsibilities

- Lead research projects in efficient LLM and VLM inference, from hypotheses and experiments through ablations, prototypes, and production handoff.

- Develop and evaluate methods spanning quantization, quantization-aware training (QAT), distillation, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, KV-cache compression, long-context inference, MoE routing, and model/runtime co-optimization.

- Build prototypes using PyTorch, Triton, CUDA-adjacent tooling, or inference-serving frameworks, and collaborate with MLEs and platform engineers to turn them into production components.

- Research LLM request routing and scheduling strategies, including cache-aware load balancing and prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD). Evaluate how queueing, KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and prefill/decode capacity allocation affect latency, throughput, and serving cost.

- Investigate multi-node inference for dense and mixture-of-experts models, including wide expert parallelism (WideEP). Study expert placement, load imbalance, and computation/communication trade-offs, and use the findings to guide model and system architecture choices.

- Develop rigorous evaluations covering quality, latency, throughput, numerical stability, memory footprint, tail latency, and cost per token. Compare serving architectures under consistent workload conditions and GPU budgets.

- Work with MLE, GPU kernel, backend infrastructure, product, and customer teams to select research priorities with measurable production impact.

- Share results through internal reports, technical blogs, papers, and open-source artifacts, and mentor engineers and scientists on experimental design, scientific rigor, and model/system trade-offs.

Must-haves

- A PhD in computer science, machine learning, ML systems, computer systems, computer architecture, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, or a closely related discipline.

- A strong publication record or equivalent research artifacts in ML, ML systems, efficient inference, model compression, quantization, distillation, serving systems, or related areas.

- Strong Python and PyTorch implementation skills, with the ability to turn ideas into experiments and working prototypes.

- Deep knowledge of LLMs, VLMs, transformer inference, decoding algorithms, model compression, quantization, and production-serving trade-offs.

- Strong experimental design skills covering ablations, baselines, metrics, statistical reasoning, and failure analysis.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-haves

- First-author publications at venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys, ACL, EMNLP, ASPLOS, OSDI, SOSP, ISCA, or HPCA.

- Experience deploying ML models or inference optimizations in production.

- Experience with vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, FlashAttention, FlashInfer, Triton, CUDA, or PyTorch internals.

- Experience applying post-training, SFT, DPO, RLHF, RLAIF, preference optimization, or synthetic data generation to inference quality or efficiency.

- Open-source research artifacts, widely used benchmarks, technical blogs, or invited talks demonstrating contributions to efficient AI systems.

- Research or implementation experience in one or more areas of distributed inference system architecture, such as LLM request routing, PDD, multi-node serving, or MoE expert parallelism, including WideEP.

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

About Tavily (Acquired by Nebius)

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.

Tavily provides the search and intelligence layer that powers AI agents and retrieval systems with trustworthy, real-time information. We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI, from fast-growing startups to global enterprises, helping them build agents that are not only intelligent, but informed.

The role

We're looking for a Business Analyst to partner closely with our Finance and Sales teams and turn data into decisions. You'll be the owner of the company's most important metrics: revenue (ARR/MRR), bookings, pipeline, conversion, net revenue retention, gross margin and more. You will need to work independently, manage competing priorities, and bring structure to complex situations.

This remote position will require travel between Data Centers.

Provider commercial management 

- Own the coordination of commercial matters with colocation providers, data center developers, and power infrastructure partners.

- Review provider requests for completeness, supporting documentation, contractual basis, and alignment with agreed scope and milestones.

- Drive funding requests, milestone payments, deposits, and prepayments through internal review and approval.

- Maintain a consolidated view of requested, approved, committed, and paid amounts across projects.

- Reconcile revised requests, funding reallocations, and previously paid amounts with Finance and providers.

The Role 

Nebius is hiring a Senior Director of GSI and Regional SI Partnerships to build and scale our global systems integrator program from the ground up. This is an infrastructure-first alliances role: we are looking for a leader who deeply understands AI cloud, inference, and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure, and who has a proven track record of turning that infrastructure into services-led, repeatable solutions that partners sell and deliver to enterprise clients worldwide. 

The strategy is deliberately two-fold. On one side are the marquee, long-tail global systems integrators — the strategic, higher-effort relationships that compound into durable, large-scale revenue over time. On the other are the fast-moving, AI-native systems integrators and emerging AI consultancies — the short-tail, quicker-to-win partners who can source and land opportunities far faster than the traditional GSIs. We need a leader who can build and balance both motions, and who already has the relationships and instincts to activate the AI-native ecosystem quickly. 

You will own the strategy, architecture, and execution of Nebius's GSI motion globally, while building the regional structure to activate partners across AMER, EMEA, and APJ. You will combine partner strategy, solution and offering development, and hands-on execution, working shoulder-to-shoulder with sales, solution engineering, product, and marketing. This is a builder's role for someone who has operated in fast-moving, high-growth environments and can create frameworks, offerings, and playbooks where none exist. Travel is expected for executive meetings, QBRs, and key industry or partner events. 

What You'll Do 

- Build the global GSI program and team. Design and own the end-to-end partner framework — segmentation, prioritization, tiering, and engagement model — spanning both marquee global systems integrators and AI-native SIs and stand up the regional operating model to execute it consistently across priority markets. 

- Activate the AI-native SI ecosystem for speed. Identify, recruit, and mobilize fast-moving, AI-native systems integrators and emerging AI consultancies as a short-tail motion that sources and lands opportunities quickly — a deliberate complement to the longer-cycle strategic GSIs. 

- Fit Nebius into partner services — and build new ones. Map how the Nebius platform plugs into each partner's existing service portfolio, and co-build the reference architectures, accelerators, and repeatable offerings that turn it into revenue they can package, sell, and deliver at scale. 

- Develop senior and field relationships. Build durable relationships across GSI sales, cloud/infrastructure, HPC, AI/ML, and industry practices — from practice leads and architects to executive sponsors. 

- Define commercial models. Establish sell-with, resale, co-sell, and managed-service models with the governance, economics, and incentives that make each partnership commercially successful for both sides. 

- Drive joint pipeline and revenue. Map target accounts, run co-sell motions, and secure Nebius inclusion in GSI pursuits to generate material, repeatable, GSI-influenced revenue and consumption. 

- Enable partner technical and sales teams. Build the enablement, certification, and deployment blueprints that make GSI teams self-sufficient on the Nebius platform. 

- Launch joint go-to-market. Partner with marketing on campaigns, events, and thought leadership focused on AI infrastructure and AI cloud. 

- Own the numbers. Track and report GSI-influenced pipeline, revenue, and consumption, holding internal and partner stakeholders accountable to shared goals. 

What You Bring 

- AI-, infrastructure-, and technology-savvy. Deep, credible fluency across AI cloud and GPU infrastructure, IaaS/PaaS, Kubernetes, and modern AI/ML workloads — enough to earn the trust of partner architects and practice leads, see how Nebius fits into a partner's existing services, and help them build new services around it. 

- A track record building services and solutions with SIs. You've built offerings, practices, and reference solutions around an infrastructure or platform product with systems integrators — not just managed a relationship, but created what partners take to market. 

- A dual network across GSIs and AI-native SIs. You bring existing relationships with both the large strategic GSIs and the emerging, AI-native systems integrators and AI consultancies, and you understand how to work each — landing quick wins through the AI-native ecosystem while building the longer-term strategic partnerships in parallel. 

- Global programs and regional build. Experience running global GSI or alliance programs and standing up the regional structures to execute across multiple geographies, accounting for local partner dynamics, delivery models, and incentives. 

- A builder's mindset. You have created frameworks, offerings, and playbooks from scratch and thrive in early-stage, high-growth environments. Startup or 0-to-1 experience is a strong plus. 

- Product savvy. You understand how infrastructure products are built and positioned, and you can work closely with product teams to shape roadmap and packaging for partner-led motions. 

- Commercial savvy. You can design commercial models, negotiate, and build the economics of partnerships that scale into meaningful, repeatable revenue. 

- Experience. 10+ years in cloud/infrastructure partner management, GSI alliances, or consulting-led enterprise GTM, including senior program leadership. Time at a hyperscaler, GPU/AI cloud, HPC or infrastructure provider, or cloud-native ISV working closely with GSIs is highly valued. 

- Deep SI knowledge. You understand how systems integrators build and run cloud, data, and AI practices — their sales cycles, delivery models, and incentive structures. 

Why Nebius 

- Be the founding global GSI leader for a high-growth, Nasdaq-listed AI infrastructure company.

- Act as the primary legal contact for the HR team (and other HQ units), providing timely, practical, decisive and commercially balanced advice on employment and labour law and employee-relations matters, and escalating material risks appropriately.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

We’re looking for a Senior HPC Cluster Engineer to join our team and play a key role in the development of our cutting-edge hyperscaler platform. The GPU & InfiniBand team is responsible for enhancing and optimizing the core components of our Cloud platform, with a specific focus on GPU computing, InfiniBand networks, and the KVM/QEMU stack. You’ll work closely with hardware virtualization and device emulation technologies, ensuring high performance and security in multi-GPU, HPC environments. The role involves analyzing, troubleshooting, and improving infrastructure to support new hardware, fine-tuning system performance, and automating fault detection and resolution in a complex system.

In this position, you will be responsible for:

- Tuning the performance of GPU clusters and InfiniBand networks to ensure optimal operation in HPC and GPU-based environments. 

- Analyzing and troubleshooting the root cause of issues related to GPUs and InfiniBand networks, and proposing corrective actions. 

- Integrating new hardware into the existing infrastructure, including support for new GPU hardware through software stacks like Kubernetes, QEMU, and KVM. 

- Enhancing automation systems for proactive monitoring, detecting, and resolving issues in GPU and InfiniBand environments. 

- Configuring and managing GPU devices and InfiniBand fabrics, ensuring efficient and reliable operation.

We expect you to have:

- 5+ years of professional experience in system-level software development (focused on performance optimization, low-level programming). 

- 3+ years of hands-on experience with Linux systems (administration, troubleshooting, and performance tuning). 

- In-depth understanding of server architecture, including PCIe devices, NICs, Linux OS/Kernel, and high-performance computing (HPC) systems. 

- Strong proficiency in one or more performance-oriented programming languages (C/C++, Go, Python).

It would be a plus if you have:

- Experience with GPU end-to-end testing in a cluster environment using InfiniBand networking. 

- Proven track record of analyzing and optimizing the performance of HPC workloads (e.g., simulations, data analysis, AI/ML workloads). 

- Familiarity with RDMA, RoCE, and InfiniBand protocols for high-performance communication. 

- Background in Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and experience with HPC cluster networking. 

- Understanding of QEMU/KVM virtualization and managing virtualized environments. 

- Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow, and their integration with HPC systems. 

- Familiarity with collective communication libraries like MPI and NCCL for distributed computing. 

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience

- 3+years of experience with Linux

- At least 3 years of engineering experience with QEMU/KVM

- General understanding of x86-compatible systems (virtual memory, interrupts, privilege rings)

postings.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, LLM Inference Optimization
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied AI team at Nebius Token Factory, you will own model and endpoint optimization from model artifacts through production deployment. Your work will span model internals, quantization and model compression, speculative decoding, KV-cache optimization, inference engines, serving architecture, and benchmarking to improve latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, and cost per token while preserving quality and reliability.

You will work with kernel and platform engineers to investigate serving problems, compare configurations, and resolve performance and quality regressions. You will evaluate model- and engine-level optimizations together with distributed inference designs, including request routing, scheduling, prefill/decode coordination, and multi-node GPU execution. Your improvements will be validated through reproducible benchmarks and safe production rollouts under real-world workloads.

Your responsibilities

- Own optimization projects for specific model families, customer endpoints, or serving backends.

- Compare inference engines and recommend serving configurations suited to individual workloads.

- Diagnose model-quality and performance regressions during production rollouts.

- Improve LLM and VLM endpoint latency, throughput, memory efficiency, GPU utilization, quality, and cost per token.

- Deploy, configure, benchmark, and extend engines such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and NVIDIA Dynamo.

- Develop production model-compression workflows covering quantization, quantization-aware training, distillation, low-bit serving, and accuracy recovery.

- Implement or integrate speculative decoding, draft-model approaches, KV-cache optimization, prefix caching, chunked prefill, continuous batching, and disaggregated prefill/decode serving. For prefill–decode disaggregation (PDD), evaluate KV-cache transfer, worker placement, and capacity balancing to determine which workloads benefit from the architecture.

- Design and improve LLM request routers and scheduling policies that balance worker utilization, queueing, request characteristics, and KV-cache locality while meeting latency and reliability targets.

- Scale dense and mixture-of-experts inference across multiple GPU nodes. Select and tune tensor, pipeline, data, and expert parallelism—including wide expert parallelism (WideEP)—with attention to hardware topology, expert load balance, and communication overhead.

- Build reproducible benchmark harnesses measuring TTFT, TPOT, tokens per second per GPU, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory, reliability, and cost per token. Validate architecture choices under representative traffic and consistent GPU budgets.

- Collaborate with GPU kernel and platform engineers to trace bottlenecks across model code, kernels, runtime, scheduler, gateway, and cluster layers.

- Produce design documents, performance reports, rollout plans, and customer-facing technical explanations.

Must-haves

- Strong engineering skills in Python and PyTorch.

- Hands-on experience deploying or optimizing LLM, VLM, or high-throughput transformer inference.

- Practical knowledge of at least one modern inference stack, such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, NVIDIA Dynamo, Ray Serve, KServe, or an equivalent internal system.

- A strong understanding of transformer inference bottlenecks involving KV cache, attention, memory bandwidth, batching, parallelism, and long-context serving.

- Ability to quantify trade-offs among latency, throughput, quality, utilization, and cost.

- Experience designing or optimizing distributed inference system architecture, with hands-on work in one or more areas such as request routing, distributed scheduling, PDD, multi-node inference, or expert parallelism.

- Strong communication and collaboration skills across research, kernel, infrastructure, product, and customer teams.

Nice-to-haves

- Experience with quantization-aware training, post-training quantization, FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4, MXFP4, AWQ, GPTQ, or SmoothQuant.

- Experience with distillation, speculative decoding, EAGLE, Medusa, multi-token prediction, or related inference acceleration methods.

- Experience supporting agentic workloads involving tool calling, structured outputs, streaming APIs, high concurrency, and multi-step orchestration.

- Familiarity with CUDA or Triton; the role does not require kernel engineering to be the candidate’s primary specialization.

- Contributions to open-source projects such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer, LMCache, PyTorch, Triton, Ray, or KServe.

- Implementation experience with cache-aware request routing, PDD, or WideEP, including diagnosing communication bottlenecks and load imbalance.

- Familiarity with GPU communication libraries and interconnects, such as NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, or RoCE.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Experience building structured extraction over messy/unstructured domain data

We're looking for a Senior Product Analyst to drive product decisions with data. You'll research how developers and companies discover, adopt and get value from Tavily and find the drivers behind them. You'll work as a thought partner to Product, R&D and leadership and shape what we build next and why.

This is a senior, high-ownership role. You take a question from start to finish: you frame the problem, build the data you need, run the analysis or model, and come back with a clear recommendation.
You are expected to understand the need and show people results they didn't even knew they wanted or needed and be an integrational part in decision making. You'll work closely with the analysts on the team and with Product, Engineering, Growth and GTM.

• Uncover the drivers behind top-level KPIs: which behaviors, use cases, endpoints and product experiences predict activation, retention and expansion.

• Build the data you need: model raw product, usage and billing data into trusted, reusable datasets with SQL, dbt and Python and more.

• Proactively monitor key product metrics, investigate trends and anomalies, and surface insights stakeholders can act on.
