postings.title: Senior Product Manager, Search Infrastructure
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.

We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.

When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.

The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.

The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week. Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Set the quality bar and release criteria for search: what good means per use case, and what a change has to clear before it ships. Our evaluation team owns the measurement, and you work closely with them on what to measure and why.

- Own the depth, latency, and cost tradeoffs across our search products, and make them explicit and defensible.

- Shape the direction of our index: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what quality bar it has to meet.

- Build a point of view on where search infrastructure is going as agents, rather than people, become the main consumer, and turn that into a roadmap.

- Know how we compare to the alternatives customers evaluate, and drive the work that closes the gaps that matter.

- Work with customer success and directly with customers to understand where our results fall short in real workflows, and turn that into quality priorities.

- Partner with the data and vertical product owners on what our corpus needs to contain and how results should be shaped per industry.

We expect you to have: 

- 5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion spent on high-scale search or ranking systems: web search, feed ranking at a large social platform, or a large ad engine.

- A background as an engineer, ML engineer, or researcher on a production system in one of those areas. This is a requirement rather than a preference. You will be making tradeoff calls alongside senior search engineers, and you need to have built something at that scale yourself.

- Direct experience shipping a search or ranking change end to end, including how it was evaluated and what happened after it shipped.

- A strong data foundation: you can design an experiment, read eval results critically, and tell a real quality improvement from noise.

- Product judgment to match the technical depth: you can decide what to build and what to leave, and defend it to both engineers and customers.

- Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how retrieval fits into agentic workflows.

- Comfort with ambiguity, moving between strategy and execution without losing the thread.

- The ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Depth in information retrieval, NLP, or applied machine learning beyond what the role requires.

- Experience with index tiering, sharding, freshness pipelines, or cost-per-query optimisation at scale.

- Experience with hybrid retrieval, semantic and lexical search, re-ranking, or human evaluation programs.

- Experience in API-first or developer-platform businesses running both self-serve and enterprise motions.

- Experience in a high-growth technology company, especially post-acquisition or startup-within-a-larger-org environments.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

postings.title: Senior Product Manager, Search Infrastructure
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Tavily, part of Nebius, is the web access layer for AI agents. Over two million developers use us, and our customers include Fortune 500 companies running agents in production.

We build and run our own index. That means we own the hard problems directly: crawl coverage at scale, freshness, cost per query, and the quality of what comes back. This role owns that infrastructure as a product.

When an agent asks a question, the answer has to be relevant, fresh, fast, and affordable. Those four things pull against each other, and someone has to decide which one gives. That is you. You will set what good means for each use case we serve and the bar a change has to clear before it ships, working closely with our evaluation team, who own how we measure it. You will also shape where our index goes next: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what it has to be good at.

The most open part of the job is what comes next. Search is being rebuilt for a consumer that is not a person. Agents do not want one result page, they want to break a problem apart, run many retrievals, and decide what to do next. That changes what search infrastructure should look like, and part of your job is to have a view on where ours should go.

The hard part is deciding what good enough means. Perfect coverage, perfect freshness, and low cost cannot all be true at once, and the person in this seat is the one who has to make that call for each use case and defend it.

In your first year, we expect you to set a clear quality bar for our search products that the team builds against, have a real influence on where our index goes next, and bring us a point of view on where search infrastructure is heading.

This is a hands-on senior IC role with real ownership, reporting to the Director of Product. You will work day to day with our search engineering and research teams, with the evaluation team, and with customer success, who bring us quality feedback from real accounts every week. Our search engineers are deeply experienced in large-scale retrieval, and the product team is small, so you will argue your case directly with the people building it. That only works if you have built at this scale yourself.

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Set the quality bar and release criteria for search: what good means per use case, and what a change has to clear before it ships. Our evaluation team owns the measurement, and you work closely with them on what to measure and why.

- Own the depth, latency, and cost tradeoffs across our search products, and make them explicit and defensible.

- Shape the direction of our index: what it needs to cover, how fresh it needs to be, and what quality bar it has to meet.

- Build a point of view on where search infrastructure is going as agents, rather than people, become the main consumer, and turn that into a roadmap.

- Know how we compare to the alternatives customers evaluate, and drive the work that closes the gaps that matter.

- Work with customer success and directly with customers to understand where our results fall short in real workflows, and turn that into quality priorities.

- Partner with the data and vertical product owners on what our corpus needs to contain and how results should be shaped per industry.

We expect you to have: 

- 5+ years of product management experience, with a meaningful portion spent on high-scale search or ranking systems: web search, feed ranking at a large social platform, or a large ad engine.

- A background as an engineer, ML engineer, or researcher on a production system in one of those areas. This is a requirement rather than a preference. You will be making tradeoff calls alongside senior search engineers, and you need to have built something at that scale yourself.

- Direct experience shipping a search or ranking change end to end, including how it was evaluated and what happened after it shipped.

- A strong data foundation: you can design an experiment, read eval results critically, and tell a real quality improvement from noise.

- Product judgment to match the technical depth: you can decide what to build and what to leave, and defend it to both engineers and customers.

- Strong understanding of LLMs, AI agents, and how retrieval fits into agentic workflows.

- Comfort with ambiguity, moving between strategy and execution without losing the thread.

- The ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without formal authority.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Depth in information retrieval, NLP, or applied machine learning beyond what the role requires.

- Experience with index tiering, sharding, freshness pipelines, or cost-per-query optimisation at scale.

- Experience with hybrid retrieval, semantic and lexical search, re-ranking, or human evaluation programs.

- Experience in API-first or developer-platform businesses running both self-serve and enterprise motions.

- Experience in a high-growth technology company, especially post-acquisition or startup-within-a-larger-org environments.

Benefits & Perks:

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

postings.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager - Data Center and Community Engagement
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

Senior Product Marketing Manager - Data Center Infrastructure & Local Community Engagement

Nebius is looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager, focusing on Data Center & Infrastructure, to own how Nebius talks about its infrastructure layer, from data centers and racks, to power and sustainability, and engage the local communities where we build. At the core of this role, is partnering with other Nebius teams, such as public affairs, government and investor relations, to navigate local political and regulatory dynamics, and address community concerns openly. You’re welcome to work remotely in the United States.

Nebius's advantage starts in the physical world: in our data centers, our custom servers with NVIDIA GPUs and networking fabric we operate. As we build new sites across the US and beyond, we need someone who can tell that story with credibility and heart: to customers and analysts, to investors and press, and to the communities where our data centers are built. 

This role sits at the intersection of technical storytelling, infrastructure fluency, and community trust. You are as comfortable explaining a liquid-cooled GPU rack as you are sitting in a town hall, and you can move between the two without losing either audience. 

Reporting to the Product Marketing Lead, you'll work hand in hand with our engineering and product management organization, data center operations, Sustainability, Communications, and Public Affairs / Government Relations teams. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Own the infrastructure and data center narrative. Translate Nebius's vertically integrated, energy-to-API advantage: turn our custom hardware, NVIDIA GPU platforms, high-performance networking fabric, storage, power, and cooling into clear, credible messaging for technical and business audiences. Contribute to our overall Nebius core messaging, positioning and story. 

- Lead the local community engagement for new and existing data center builds. This is the heart of the role and you will need to partner with our local site, public affairs and government relations to campaign positively around new US (and global) data center initiatives. You will develop community-facing materials as required, such as fact sheets, FAQs, town-hall content, local economic-impact and jobs stories that address concerns about energy, grid, water, noise, and land honestly and proactively. 

- Enable go-to-market and field teams. Arm sales, solutions, and partner teams with the messaging and assets they need to sell the infrastructure story. From first-call decks, battlecards, discovery guides, ROI/TCO tools, objection handling, and competitive positioning against hyperscalers and neoclouds. Run enablement sessions and measure whether the field is adopting and winning with what you build. 

- Tell the efficiency and sustainability story. Turn energy efficiency, power and cooling design, heat reuse, water stewardship, renewable sourcing, and sustainability metrics into proof points that stand up to scrutiny from customers, investors, regulators, and communities alike. 

- Evangelize our GPU platform layer. Work closely with Nebius's product management, engineering teams, and our NVIDIA counterparts, to understand new GPU platforms and hardware as they arrive: what's different, why it matters, and how it performs, and translate that into launch narratives, positioning, and differentiated stories that reach the market ahead of the field. 

- Build the proof library. Create and maintain solution briefs, site fact sheets, reference architectures, white papers, customer and investor-ready presentations, videos, and web pages that make Nebius's infrastructure differentiation tangible. 

- Support communications, PR, and analyst / investor relations. Feed the data center scaling narrative into press moments, site launches, analyst briefings, and investor materials, in close coordination with comms, legal and other team. 

- Own competitive and category positioning for infrastructure. Keep a sharp, evidence-based view of the data center and AI infrastructure landscape: power availability, GPU roadmaps, cooling, network fabric, sustainability standards, and keep Nebius's differentiation current. 

- Champion the voice of the customer. Partner with sales and the customer marketing team to develop references, case studies, and proof points; bring real enterprise pain points and wins back into product and messaging. 

We expect you to have: 

- 5+ years in product marketing in data centers, cloud and/or AI infrastructure, energy, hardware, or semiconductors. 

- Demonstrated experience with community engagement, public affairs, or stakeholder communications. You've helped an organization earn local trust for a physical project, or you can clearly show how you'd do it. This is the differentiator we are looking for. 

- A genuine working understanding of AI data center infrastructure: power and cooling, racks, GPU platforms and hardware, high-performance networking, and the sustainability metrics that matter (e.g., PUE, WUE, energy sourcing). Familiarity with NVIDIA GPU platforms, high-performance networking (NVIDIA InfiniBand). 

- Excellent hands-on writing, presentation, and storytelling skills, including experience running messaging workshops and methodologies such as SCIPAB. 

- Familiarity with sustainability reporting, ESG frameworks, or environmental permitting and its stakeholders. 

- Strong ability to translate complex technical and engineering concepts into simple, audience-first narratives for very different audiences: from engineers to residents to investors. 

- Proven experience creating content across the spectrum: from technical briefs and web pages to community FAQs, event materials, and executive presentations. 

- Sound judgment and fact discipline: comfort handling sensitive topics (energy, environment, community impact) accurately and responsibly, and flagging claims that need sign-off. 

- A collaborative, cross-functional operator who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is willing to travel to sites and communities as needed. 

- Bachelor's degree in a technical, communications, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. 

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Comfort operating in public-company investor relations contexts, feeding directly into investor, analyst, and earnings-related materials. 

- Experience within the NVIDIA ecosystem and familiarity with the GPU roadmap, reference architectures, and partner programs. #LI-LT1

Key employee benefits in the US:

- Health insurance: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and families.

- 401(k) plan: Up to 4% company match with immediate vesting.

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Remote work reimbursement: Up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

- Disability & life insurance: Company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

postings.title: Senior Product & PLG Analyst (Full-Stack Data Scientist)
postings.location: New York City, New York, United States
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
About the Tavily at Nebius

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.
Tavily provides the search and intelligence layer that powers AI agents and retrieval systems with trustworthy, real-time information. We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI, from fast-growing startups to global enterprises, helping them build agents that are not only intelligent but informed.

About the Role

We're looking for a senior, full-stack analyst / data scientist to own Product and PLG analytics end-to-end. You'll own the metrics behind our self-serve motion (signup, activation, usage, conversion, expansion and retention) and find the drivers behind them. You'll work directly with our CEO and leadership as a thought partner on product and growth decisions.

This role is fully independent. When a question comes up, you take it all the way: from building the pipeline, model the data, train and deploy the model, analyze the results and come back with a clear recommendation. Nothing waits in a queue for someone else. You'll also work closely with the other analysts on the team, share methods and standards, and collaborate across Product, Engineering, Growth, Marketing and GTM.

What You'll Do

• Own Product and PLG analytics end-to-end: define, instrument and measure the self-serve funnel, from first API call through activation, conversion to paid, expansion and churn.
• Uncover the drivers behind top-level KPIs: which behaviors, use cases and product experiences predict activation, retention and monetization.
• Build what you need: data pipelines and models (SQL, dbt, Python, orchestration) that turn raw product, usage and billing data into trusted, reusable datasets.
• Build and ship predictive models (conversion propensity, churn risk, usage forecasting, lead and account scoring) and bring their outputs into product and GTM workflows.
• Design, run and evaluate experiments (A/B tests, pricing and packaging tests, onboarding changes) and apply causal inference where you can't run a clean experiment.
• Proactively monitor key business and product metrics, investigate trends and anomalies, and surface insights stakeholders can act on.

The Role
We are looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) to join the Compute Node team at Nebius AI Cloud. The Compute Node team is responsible for building and operating the cluster scheduler and node-level services that run and manage virtual machines across all cloud regions. This role focuses on Linux systems engineering, virtualization and operational reliability. You will work close to the operating system and hypervisor, shaping how reliability and observability are embedded into the Compute platform.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Ensure reliability, availability and performance of compute nodes running VMs

- Analyze and debug Linux systems across user space and kernel space, understanding capabilities, limitations and trade-offs at each layer

- Troubleshoot complex production issues involving CPU, memory, NUMA, cgroups and scheduling

- Work hands-on with virtualization and containerization, primarily using QEMU/KVM and Linux-native technologies

- Design and evolve observability as a core capability of the node layer: metrics, logs, traces, alerts, SLIs and SLOs

- Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, and postmortems, driving long-term reliability improvements

postings.location: Amsterdam, Netherlands; Israel; London, United Kingdom
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

The Product

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.

We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the web access infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on making our access to public web content reliable and efficient. You will investigate how modern websites and browsers communicate across the full request lifecycle, find the root cause when a request fails or returns something unexpected, and build the fixes into production systems operating at internet scale. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the crawling, indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

- Diagnose failed or degraded requests at the right layer: network and IP, TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, headers and session state, client-side scripts, or browser characteristics

- Analyze how websites verify and classify clients, including how client-side scripts and protocol-level behavior shape what a site serves to different clients

- Build clients and tooling that behave consistently and compatibly with standard browsers across all of these layers, using a real browser where a lightweight client is not enough

- Monitor access quality as websites change: detect regressions, find the cause, and measure success on real content rather than on status codes

- Build the tooling to do this at scale: traffic capture and comparison against real browsers, per-site and per-method success tracking, and the cost of each successful fetch

- Choose the fetch method for each host, from a lightweight HTTP client to a full browser, balancing quality against cost

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

The request lifecycle

- HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, TLS handshakes and TLS fingerprints (JA3/JA4), and header behavior

- What a server can observe at each step of a request, and what a client controls at each step

- A debugging method, not guesses: replaying captured browser traffic, comparing against a real browser on the same network path, and changing one variable at a time

Client-side analysis

- Reading and analyzing complex or obfuscated JavaScript, and observing what a script measures by hooking browser APIs

- How browser, device and network characteristics are measured (canvas, fonts, WebGL, screen and window metrics) and how consistent they are across layers

- Browser instrumentation and the Chrome DevTools Protocol, used as tools for investigation

Running it for real

- Have run this in production and can give numbers: requests per day, sites or hosts, and the success rate and how you measured it

- Strong programming in at least one of Go, Python, Rust or C++

Strong candidates may also have experience with

- Working at a web data provider, a browser or web-security company, or a company that collects data from complex sources

- Contributions to browser networking or fingerprinting-related open-source tooling, or public write-ups of how client verification works

- Building or maintaining a patched browser

- Networks, proxies and IP reputation

- Internet-scale distributed systems, Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure

The kind of problems you will work on

- A site returns a different response to our client than to Chrome on the same network path. Find out why, and fix that cause.

- A site changes how it verifies clients and success drops across a group of sites. Find what changed, adapt, and make the next change cheaper to catch.

- Switching to a browser-like network profile makes results worse on some hosts. Work out what no longer matches.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

postings.title: Senior Software Engineer (Agentic Search) – Web Rendering (Chromium)
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The Product

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on AI agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible. We are building an agent-native search platform designed specifically for AI systems rather than human users. Our product provides programmatic, low-latency, and observable search APIs that AI agents use to retrieve, filter, and reason over real-world information at scale.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to work on the rendering infrastructure of a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption.

In this role, you will focus on loading modern web pages in a browser that we patch and build ourselves, so that content is rendered completely and reliably at a cost that works across billions of pages. You will work inside Chromium to remove what we do not need, make the rest faster and cheaper, and keep our build current as Chromium moves. Your work ensures that high-quality content is consistently available to the indexing and retrieval systems downstream.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

- Change Chromium in its heavy core (Blink, the V8 integration, the compositor, the network service) to cut CPU, memory and startup cost per page

- Strip Chromium down for agent workloads: skip what nobody needs, such as image and media decoding, web font downloads, and rasterization and GPU work where no one needs pixels, while keeping what page scripts depend on to run correctly (style, layout, animation frames, observers), and work out what breaks, or renders differently, when you do

- Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render

- Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling

- Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser

- Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)

- Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service

- Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems

- Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs

- Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management

- Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with

- Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine

- Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for

- Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol

- Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)

- Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on

- Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?

- Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?

- A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?

- Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?

- Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

We conduct coding interviews as part of the process.

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

- Keep the browser compatible with the web: make sure that what we remove does not change how the sites we load behave or render

- Profile and tune fleets of browsers: the process model, memory per renderer, startup, isolation and crash handling

- Build the production system around it: how browsers are launched, pooled, recycled and monitored

You may be a good fit if you

Have 5+ years of experience building production systems, and are an expert in several of the following areas.

Inside the browser

- Strong C++ in a large, performance-critical codebase, ideally Chromium, Blink or V8, or a comparable browser engine (Rust is a plus)

- Chromium architecture: the process model, Mojo IPC, the rendering pipeline (DOM, style, layout, paint, compositing), and the network service

- Building, debugging and shipping custom Chromium builds: the build system, tracing, crash analysis, and maintaining patches across releases

Performance and systems

- Profiling CPU, memory and I/O for browser fleets, with tools such as perf, tracing and flame graphs

- Linux process isolation and resource management, concurrency, and memory management

- Have run browsers in production, or built the infrastructure that does, and can describe where the time and memory went

Strong candidates may also have experience with

- Contributions to Chromium, Blink, V8, Firefox, WebKit or another browser engine

- Building or maintaining a patched browser that you wrote the patches for

- Browser instrumentation, including the Chrome DevTools Protocol

- Working familiarity with how modern frontend frameworks render (SSR, CSR, streaming, hydration)

- Distributed systems, Kubernetes, and Go or Python

The kind of problems you will work on

- Cut the cost of loading a page in half. Where do CPU and memory go, and what would you change in the browser?

- Turn off the GPU and image decoding for agent workloads. What breaks, and what changes in how pages load and render?

- A page runs a script that never yields. How do we detect and stop it without help from the page?

- Chromium ships a new version. How do we bring a large set of patches forward in days, not weeks?

- Decide when a page is finished, for pages with analytics beacons, long polling and endless scrolling.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

The role

#LI-MM1

We’re looking for a Software Engineer with strong C++ expertise to join the team building and operating Nebius Data Platform — a distributed storage and a processing platform that acts as the company’s “source of truth” and the backbone of many internal (and some external) products.

Nebius Data Platform is a single multi-tenant ecosystem based on YTsaurus — instead of running separate HDFS/Kafka/HBase-style systems, we provide storage, compute, and analytics capabilities inside one platform.

Built on top of the open-source YTsaurus ecosystem, we run and extend our own Nebius distribution and develop significant in-house functionality (core and platform-level). We can design, implement, and roll out features end-to-end on our clusters without waiting for upstream approvals and contribute upstream when it makes sense.

At scale today, this includes~500 servers, ~20k CPU cores and ~10 PB of compressed data in our largest production cluster, supporting workloads ranging from business-critical pipelines and financial transactions to large-scale ML/LLM training datasets and compute.

What’s inside the platform

You’ll work on a system that includes (and ties together):

- Distributed Storage (Cypress): transactional semantics, tiered storage, erasure coding, replication, and strong reliability expectations.

- Compute & ETL: a cluster-wide job scheduler (tens of thousands of cores), MapReduce, YQL for SQL-like data processing, and SPYT (Spark over YTsaurus) for modern data engineering.

- Interactive analytics (CHYT): ClickHouse® instances spun up directly on compute nodes for fast SQL over data in-place.

- Dynamic Tables: low-latency NoSQL KV with distributed ACID transactions for OLTP-style workloads and feature stores.

- Orchestracto: workflow orchestration deeply integrated with the platform (Airflow-like, but platform-native).

What you’ll do

We’re looking for engineers who combine strong systems skills with product sense: understanding who uses the platform, why certain capabilities matter, and making pragmatic trade-offs to maximize impact. On our team, engineering work is expected to be connected to real users and outcomes — you’ll regularly align with internal stakeholders, clarify requirements, and help drive prioritization.

In this role, you will:

- Design and implement new functionality in YTsaurus core (C++) with production reliability in mind.

- Build and evolve platform-level capabilities: platform architecture and operating model—multi-cluster growth, shared primitives, and a consistent experience that scales with new teams and use cases.

- Improve end-to-end platform experience for internal (and external-facing) users: APIs, guardrails, debugging workflows, and automation.

- Own production quality: incident response / on-call rotation, root cause analysis, and turning learnings into durable fixes.

Example projects

- Roll out sharded YTsaurus masters (incl. Kubernetes operator support) and build automatic balancing of metadata across master cells (consensus groups) to remove control-plane bottlenecks and unlock 10–100x cluster growth.

- Make CHYT interactive SQL faster and more predictable at high load via performance work like data-skipping / min-max-style indexes and improved execution introspection.

- Turn Orchestracto into a platform product by defining the building blocks, developer experience, and governance for how teams create and share workflows.

- Scale and harden Parquet-on-S3 for native YTsaurus workloads by tackling replication/movement, consistent lifecycle semantics, and master-server metadata optimizations for performance and reliability.

- Design and ship complete, trustworthy audit trails for data changes (who/what/when) across heterogeneous storage and compute paths.

Tech stack

- Core: modern C++ (C++20, async + multithreaded primitives)

- Services & tooling: Go and Python (microservices, utilities, integration tests)

What we expect

- 5+ years of software engineering experience.

- Strong C++ skills (you’ll write core code).

- Working knowledge of Python and/or Go (you don’t have to be expert, but should be comfortable navigating them).

- Experience developing and/or operating high-load, distributed services.

- Production mindset: ability to use SSH, read logs/metrics/traces, and debug distributed systems behavior.

- Solid CS fundamentals: algorithms, data structures, concurrency basics.

Nice to have

- Experience with Big Data systems (YTsaurus/Hadoop/Spark/ClickHouse/Kafka-like ecosystems).

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

The YDB Development Team at Nebius is hiring mid- and senior-level software developers with C++ expertise.

YDB is an open-source platform with two roles within Nebius:

- Providing the binary object storage foundation for S3 Object Storage, Shared Filesystems and Network Block Storage

- Serving as a distributed relational database and message broker for services such as IAM, billing, audit trails and logging

We operate YDB clusters in more than 10 regions using HDD and NVMe storage. Individual clusters span tens of thousands of nodes, manage hundreds of petabytes of data and deliver terabytes per second of throughput. Our infrastructure includes x86 and Arm-based systems, including NVIDIA GB300 nodes.

What you’ll work on

- Evolve YDB’s architecture for new hardware, redesigning core components when incremental optimization is insufficient:

- QLC NVMe drives: increase storage density while controlling RAM/CPU consumption and write amplification

- Dual 800 Gb/s network adapters: reduce CPU overhead and memory bandwidth consumption to utilize the available NIC bandwidth

- NVIDIA GB300-based systems: ensure efficient operation on Arm-based hosts and offload storage and networking processing to BlueField DPUs

- Support high-capacity SMR HDDs by designing data placement, sequential writes, garbage collection and recovery around zoned-write constraints

- Develop wide erasure-coding schemes to reduce space aplimfication while maintaining durability and availability

- Reduce recovery and rebalancing times after device outages while limiting the impact on foreground workloads

- Prevent, detect and recover from silent data corruption across memory, networking and storage

- Provide the system capabilities and interfaces required by fleet-wide automation so that hundreds of production clusters can be deployed, configured, upgraded, diagnosed and operated consistently

We move quickly and focus on delivering practical value. Features and optimizations merged into the production branch are typically deployed within weeks. You’ll see your work solving real problems in live clusters—not waiting years to make an impact.

Requirements:

- 5+ years of professional experience developing high-load systems in C or C++. Candidates with 3+ years will also be considered if their experience includes relevant work on distributed storage systems

- Experience developing high-performance, low-latency software components

- Understanding of core dumps, flame graphs and sanitizer-enabled builds

- Understanding of CPU caches, atomic operations and NUMA architectures

Nice to have:

- Experience designing and developing production-grade distributed storage systems and/or databases

- Experience with on-disk data structures such as LSM trees and B+ trees, and storage algorithms such as erasure coding and checksumming

- Understanding of NVMe, conventional HDD and SMR HDD internals

- Experience with debugging and profiling tools such as perf, VTune, bpftrace and gdb

- Familiarity with the Linux kernel, SPDK/DPDK, libaio and io_uring

- Knowledge of IP, TCP, UDP and DNS, and ideally InfiniBand or RoCE/RDMA

- Experience with Kubernetes and Grafana

- Experience responding to production incidents

- Knowledge of availability and durability calculations

For Senior candidates, we offer hybrid working or the flexibility to work remotely within EU.

- 

In a rapidly evolving world, trust in AI depends on agents being grounded in fresh, verified real-world data. Search is the foundation that makes this possible.
We’re looking for an experienced Data Analyst who has built evaluation systems for complex technology products and is excited to take end-to-end ownership of quality in search built for AI agents.

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

About Tavily 

We're building the infrastructure layer for agentic web interaction at scale. Our API is designed from the ground up to power Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and real-time reasoning in AI systems. By connecting LLMs to high-quality, trustworthy web content, we help developers build agents that are not only intelligent — but also informed. 

We work with some of the most innovative teams in AI — from small startups shaping the ecosystem to the largest enterprises deploying AI at scale. Whether it's powering sales assistants, research copilots, or internal knowledge tools, we're the missing link between LLMs and the real world. 

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to design and build the billing platform behind a novel search engine tailored for agentic AI consumption. This role is based in our New York office, hybrid with the NYC team.

Our APIs are used by millions of developers and the AI agents acting on their behalf, all paying based on what they consume. You will own the systems that turn product usage into accurate, trustworthy revenue, supporting flexible billing models—usage-based pricing, subscriptions, prepaid balances with auto top-up, and enterprise contracts. Correctness is non-negotiable: every event must be measured precisely and every invoice must be right to the cent.

‌

In this position, your responsibility will be to:

- 

Design and operate the billing platform end to end, from usage events to invoices

- 

Build metering and usage-aggregation pipelines that turn high-volume events into billable amounts

- 

Design and operate prepaid credit/wallet systems with auto top-up and balance management

- 

Support enterprise/contract billing with custom pricing, negotiated terms, and scheduled invoicing

- 

Build reconciliation, idempotency, and invoice-accuracy safeguards to ensure revenue data is always correct

- 

Lead the migration to the next generation of our billing system with no revenue loss or downtime

- 

Define observability and quality metrics for billing correctness, freshness, and throughput

- 

Ensure billing systems meet audit and compliance requirements (SOX, financial audit)

‌

What we're looking for:

- 

6+ years building production backend systems, of which 3+ years actively building and operating billing or metering systems in production

- 

Hands-on experience with usage-based / metered billing: rating, aggregation, and proration logic

- 

Hands-on experience with subscription / recurring billing alongside usage-based models

- 

Hands-on experience with prepaid credits / wallet systems and auto top-up mechanics

- 

Hands-on experience with enterprise / contract billing: custom pricing and negotiated terms

- 

End-to-end integration of a third-party billing platform (Stripe Billing, Metronome, Orb, or Zuora)

- 

Strong expertise in Python and TypeScript/Node (Go a plus)

- 

Production experience with transactional databases (Postgres or equivalent) for financial-grade data

- 

Built high-volume event / usage pipelines into a data warehouse (Kafka or Kinesis → Snowflake or BigQuery)

- 

Owned billing correctness in production: reconciliation, idempotency, invoice accuracy

- 

Product-Led Growth (PLG) experience: worked on billing for high-volume, self-serve users

- 

Hands-on with Auth0, Okta, or similar identity systems in production

- 

Shipped revenue systems under SOX or financial audit constraints

Nice to have:

- 

Led a billing system migration or re-platform with zero revenue loss or downtime

- 

Built hybrid billing combining usage, subscriptions, and prepaid in one system

- 

Worked across both a payments layer (Stripe) and a metering / rating layer (Metronome / Orb)

- 

Billed a developer-facing / API product with pay-as-you-go and API-key metering

- 

Used Snowflake for usage aggregation and revenue analytics

Why Tavily? 

- Full ownership — small team, you own the entire infrastructure, not a slice of it 

- Real scaling challenges — bursty scraping workloads, cache invalidation, multi-region, millions of daily requests

The role

The VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) team builds and operates the core networking layer of our cloud platform. We enable virtual machines to communicate reliably by abstracting them from the underlying physical network, providing seamless IP-based connectivity even as workloads move across the datacenter.

Our team designs secure, isolated private networks for customers, connects them to the public internet, and delivers essential networking services such as load balancers, firewalls, and security groups. Because nearly every cloud application depends on networking, VPC is a foundational service for the entire platform.

Stability and resilience are our top priorities—we engineer systems to remain reliable and operational even when parts of the cloud experience failures.

Our team both develops the control-plane, written in Golang, and supports open-source based dataplane, written mostly in C. This makes us quite unique in that we both have high-level control plane tasks and low-level system research tasks, with different team members focusing more on one part or the other.

What we do:

- Increase service scalability and reliability

- Develop the control & data plane for Nebius Cloud network services

- Develop service functionality (e.g. IPv6 support, service endpoints, VPC peering, L7 load balancers and other networking services)

- Improve the internal architecture, optimizing interaction with related services

- Capable of writing reliable, high-performance concurrent code

- Familiar with routing network traffic

- Worked with OVS, VPP, DPDK, Linux kernel network subsystem or other network dataplanes

Your scope will be defined by what you bring. We will match your technical strengths, customer experience, and product instincts to the area of the platform where you can have the most impact. The platform is broad — and at our scale, every slice is mission-critical.
If you want to help build the best AI cloud in the world — and you have the technical depth to engage engineering leaders as a peer (not as a translator) and the comfort to talk to customers directly — this team is for you.

The platform you'll help build:

- Hardware platforms & launch — bringing new GPU and CPU platforms (GB300, Vera Rubin, ARM/Grace, future generations) to production with full launch readiness across the stack.

- Cluster lifecycle & fleet operations — new region launches, 100,000+ GPU cluster bring-up, platform sharding and allocation architecture, release engineering, host-lifecycle automation, operational efficiency.

- Reliability & Mission Control — autohealing, health checks, SLA, fault-tolerant training, MTTR reduction, customer trust at scale, observability as a product.

- Customer experience & developer surface — Compute APIs, console, CLI, IMDS and in-VM signals, self-service workflows, notifications, customer-facing observability, unified UX across the product line.

- GPU & InfiniBand foundational services — drivers, firmware, NCCL, IB/RoCE, NVLink topology, the foundational layer everything else builds on.

- Cross-platform program & delivery — NVIDIA partnership programs, major-maintenance orchestration, cross-stream releases.

You will own one of the slices of this platform end-to-end — from strategy and roadmap through delivery, adoption, and measurable outcomes.

Your responsibilities will include (regardless of which slice you own):

- Own end-to-end product responsibility for your area — strategy, roadmap, discovery, delivery, adoption, measurable customer and platform outcomes.

- Design and own the platform contracts customers depend on — APIs, semantics, system events, customer-facing surfaces, operational behavior — at hyperscaler quality.

- Drive cross-team execution across platform engineering, networking, storage, Soperator/MK8S, observability, IAM, billing, capacity planning, support, and product design.

- Turn customer pain into product commitments through structured discovery — interviews, usage analytics, support patterns, incident postmortems. Close the loop so the same class of failure or friction does not recur.

- Engage engineering as a technical peer — debate API design, reason about system trade-offs, judge the quality of platform internals, and push back when the design is wrong.

- Define and own success metrics — what you ship is measured by what changed for the customer or the platform, not by the size of the spec.

- Be the product voice that customer-facing teams (Support, CX, TAMs) escalate to when a system behavior, API contract, or operational pattern needs a product decision, not a workaround.

We expect you to have:

- 6+ years in Product Management, Platform PM, Infrastructure PM, or SRE / Engineering Lead with strong product instincts.

- Strong technical foundation and cloud-infrastructure depth — comfort reasoning about API semantics, control-plane vs data-plane behavior, system events and lifecycle, multi-tenant operational realities. You can engage engineering leaders as a peer, not as a translator.

- Experience with cloud, GPU, or HPC infrastructure — either building one or operating one at meaningful scale (thousands of nodes, multi-region, multi-tenant).

- Track record of shipping technically complex platform products with measurable customer or platform impact — quantitative results, not aspirational bullets.

- Strong analytical skills: comfort defining and instrumenting product metrics, working with telemetry, building data-informed roadmaps.

- Experience leading discovery-heavy work — structured customer interviews, usage analytics, support-ticket analysis — and turning insights into shipped product.

- Strong communication and ability to align engineering, SRE, customer-facing teams, and exec stakeholders.

- High ownership, bias to ship, comfort with messy operational reality, and the instinct to push back on engineering when the customer experience or platform quality would suffer.

It will be an added bonus if you have (these are not all required — different strengths fit different slices of the platform):

Customer-facing experience and lived-it perspective:

- Direct PM experience with frontier AI customers — ML platform teams, MLOps engineers, training and inference at scale.

- Familiarity with Kubernetes, Slurm, or HPC environments from the user side, and ML training workflows.

- Hands-on experience with ML training and inference workflows — especially distributed training at scale (multi-node, multi-GPU; comfort with checkpointing, NCCL, fault-tolerant training, debugging large training jobs).

- Experience as a customer of AI cloud infrastructure at large scale — especially as part of an internal ML platform team that built and operated infrastructure for ML engineers inside your own company. If you have lived through what frustrates customers about clouds, you will know exactly what we are trying to fix.

Hardware, GPU, and HPC depth:

- Direct experience with NVIDIA reference architectures (NVL72, SuperPOD, MGX, DGX) and the NVIDIA stack (drivers, CUDA, NCCL, DCGM).

- Familiarity with InfiniBand / RoCE fabrics, firmware lifecycle, topology-aware scheduling.

- Hands-on with GPU clusters or HPC fabrics at thousands-of-nodes scale.

Cluster and fleet operations:

- Background in Kubernetes lifecycle (CAPI, cluster upgrades, node-pool management) or Slurm at scale.

- Experience launching new cloud regions or data-center bring-ups end-to-end.

- Background in release engineering, change management, or major-maintenance orchestration in production environments.

Customer experience and developer surface:

- Exposure to console / CLI / API design at hyperscaler quality — AWS, GCP, Azure depth on consistency, versioning, idempotency, error semantics, deprecation policy.

- Background in observability product — Grafana, Datadog, Honeycomb, New Relic.

- Familiarity with developer-experience product patterns — Stripe, Cloudflare, Vercel, Supabase, Render.

Reliability and operational outcomes:

- Background in SRE, reliability engineering, or fault-tolerant systems for paying customers.

- Familiarity with reliability metrics that matter: Goodput, MFU, MTTR, MTBF.

- Experience with autohealing systems and graceful failure semantics.

Emerging workloads and integrations:

- Familiarity with RL / agentic / inference workload patterns — vLLM, SGLang, Ray, Token Factory-style serving, sandbox technologies (Firecracker, gVisor, Kata).

The team 
The Hardware Automation team builds the internal platforms and tooling that power how Nebius operates its data center infrastructure at scale. Our mission is to eliminate manual effort, reduce human error, and give every team in the Hardware Infrastructure department real-time visibility and control over the systems they own.

We operate as a product engineering team embedded within hardware infrastructure — meaning we don't just write requirements and hand them off. We own the full stack: from requirements gathering with data center operations and hardware engineering, through design and build, all the way to rollout and ongoing reliability.

The role
We are looking for a Technical Project Manager to drive the programs that turn manual hardware operations into automated, scalable workflows. You will own the delivery of automation initiatives across the full hardware lifecycle — from automated server provisioning and firmware update orchestration through intelligent fault detection, self-healing remediation, and data-centre-scale operational tooling — coordinating engineers, operations teams, and infrastructure stakeholders to ship systems that meaningfully reduce human toil at fleet scale.

The responsibilities 

- Initiating and driving cross-team projects with clear goals and timelines

- Aligning conflicting priorities and stakeholder needs, including C-level

- Facilitating technical and procedural decision-making

- Establishing and scaling repeatable processes

- Collaborating closely with engineering, infrastructure, and business teams

The profile :

- Engineering Manager wanting to move from vertical to horizontal impact, from team to org level, designing and carrying a unified roadmap and strategy across multiple engineering teams. In this case, we are talking about 6 teams for more than 30 engineers.

- Technical Project/Program Manager with an Engineering Management background. 

- Strong operational risk awareness: track record of structuring staged rollouts, defining rollback criteria, and insisting on safety gates before automation runs unsupervised on production infrastructure.

- Experience coordinating across engineering and operations stakeholders with different risk tolerances — bridging teams that move fast and teams that prioritise stability without letting that tension stall delivery.

Preferred / Nice to Have

- Experience with specific hardware automation domains: zero-touch provisioning, firmware orchestration, automated hardware testing frameworks, or self-healing remediation systems.

- Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code and configuration management tooling (Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes) from a delivery and rollout management perspective.

- Exposure to data centre operations — rack and stack, cabling, power and cooling management — sufficient to understand what automation means to a technician on the floor.

- Experience with site reliability engineering (SRE) practices: toil measurement, error budgets, and the discipline of treating operational automation as a first-class engineering investment.

- Knowledge of observability platforms (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or equivalent) used to monitor automation system health and measure operational outcomes.

Administer selected corporate IT systems and services according to operational requirements, including access and permissions management, service configuration and automation.

Maintain and improve Service Desk procedures, runbooks, escalation paths and knowledge base; propose technical standards for approval by Service Desk management and maintain them once approved; advise on operational priorities.

Contribute to creating and updating documentation: runbooks, process documents, technical standards and knowledge-base articles, setting the standard for documentation quality across the team.

Analyze ticket, escalation and SLA data to identify systemic issues and contribute to SLA reporting; lead root-cause analysis and problem management; design process, tooling and automation changes that improve first-time resolution and reduce escalation volume.

Assess proposed solutions and operational changes for supportability and user impact; advise management and partner teams on the support implications of technology decisions.

Provide organizational context on existing and legacy IT processes, systems, decisions and ownership structures; apply it when evaluating current processes, and improve legacy practices where appropriate.

Identify gaps or ambiguities in operational ownership and work with the relevant stakeholders to establish practical solutions.

Own and improve employee-lifecycle processes, including hardware provisioning and, with Onboarding and People teams, new-hire IT onboarding across EMEA and APAC.

Recommend standards for company-provided laptops, peripherals and other end-user equipment, balancing business need, supportability, lifecycle and market availability; maintain the approved standards.

Contribute to forecasting and budget planning for employee technology and Service Desk requirements.

Support Service Desk contracts, renewals and licensing; maintain working relationships with hardware and Service Desk vendors.

We’re looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to help build and run the fundamental part of Nebius - the Network - the infrastructure everything else depends on. This is an engineering-first SRE role: you’ll set clear reliability targets, build the tooling and automation to meet them, and make the network safer to operate as we scale quickly.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Strong production Linux fundamentals and a structured approach to debugging complex systems

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role 

The Site Selection & Colocation Manager is responsible for identifying, evaluating, and securing optimal locations for new data center developments and colocation expansions. This role combines real estate strategy, technical due diligence, market analysis, and vendor management to support the company’s global data center growth. The manager will collaborate closely with engineering, construction, finance, legal, and network planning teams to ensure that selected sites meet operational, technical, and business requirements.

You’re welcome to work in our office in Amsterdam or Remote in the EU. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

Site Selection & Market Analysis

- Lead the end-to-end site selection process for new data center facilities.

- Conduct market assessments, including power availability, fiber connectivity, land suitability, regulatory requirements, and risk factors.

- Build and maintain market intelligence on emerging data center regions, supply trends, energy markets, and colocation pricing.

- Evaluate and shortlist candidate sites through comparative analysis, scoring models, and feasibility studies.

Technical & Environmental Due Diligence

- Coordinate environmental, geotechnical, hydrological, and seismic assessments.

- Assess infrastructure availability (power, water, fiber) and future scalability.

- Evaluate construction constraints, climate conditions, logistics access, and permitting feasibility.

- Work with engineering teams to ensure sites meet mechanical, electrical, and network resilience requirements.

Colocation Strategy & Vendor Management

- Identify colocation providers and evaluate facilities based on technical specifications, SLA requirements, and cost structure.

- Lead RFPs, negotiations, and contract execution with colocation and connectivity partners.

- Manage colocation lifecycle: renewals, expansions, migrations, and optimization of space/power allocations.

- Monitor vendor performance against SLA, uptime, compliance, and efficiency metrics.

 Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Work with data center design and construction teams to validate site feasibility and development timelines.

- Partner with legal on contract terms, property acquisition, lease terms, and regulatory compliance.

- Support finance with CapEx/OpEx modeling, ROI calculations, and business case development.

- Coordinate with public authorities, utilities, and permitting agencies as needed.

 Risk Assessment & Compliance

- Evaluate risks related to natural hazards, geopolitical risk, security, environmental constraints, and utility reliability.

- Ensure compliance with local regulations, zoning laws, and corporate standards.

- Maintain documentation for audits, reporting, and internal approvals.

We expect you to have: 

- Bachelor’s degree in Real Estate, Engineering, Business, Geography, or related field.

- 5–8+ years of experience in site selection, real estate development, colocation management, or data center infrastructure.

- Strong understanding of data center power, cooling, and network requirements.

- Experience in evaluating colocation providers and negotiating leases/SLAs.

- Analytical skills in market research, cost modeling, and risk assessment.

- Ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects across regions.

- Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Experience with hyperscale or large-scale data center development.

- Knowledge of utility procurement (power, water), renewable energy markets, and substation planning.

- Familiarity with geospatial tools (GIS), risk modeling, or data center capacity planning.

- Understanding of permitting processes and environmental regulations.

- Career growth and learning opportunities

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. About the role 

The AI conversation is happening on X. We want Nebius at the center of it. 
We're looking for a creative, culturally fluent, and highly engaged Social Media Specialist to build Nebius's presence and influence on X. You'll help shape how developers, researchers, founders, and industry leaders discover, talk about, and engage with Nebius. 

This isn't a role focused on filling a content calendar. You'll help define the conversations we participate in, build relationships with the people shaping the AI industry, and create content that earns attention and drives growth. 

You'll have the freedom to experiment, move quickly, and bring your own ideas to life. One day, you might be turning a technical breakthrough into a compelling thread. The next, you'll be engaging with a leading AI researcher, jumping into an industry debate, or finding a creative way to make Nebius part of a trending conversation. 
You'll work closely with product marketing, design, engineering, and the broader marketing team to bring Nebius's story to life. We're looking for someone who knows the platform, loves the pace, and is excited to help make Nebius a recognized and respected voice in AI. 

What you'll do

- Own our presence on X. Drive Nebius's X strategy and daily execution, building an engaged audience and growing our influence within the AI ecosystem. 

- Shape the conversation. Identify emerging trends, industry debates, and cultural moments where Nebius can contribute a compelling perspective. Know when to jump in, how to stand out, and when to let a conversation go. 

- Build relationships that matter. Engage with influential developers, researchers, founders, creators, and industry tastemakers. Make Nebius a brand that people in the AI community know, trust, and want to engage with. 

- Create content people actually want to read. Develop original posts, threads, replies, and creative formats that are insightful, relevant, and native to X. Bring personality and creativity without sacrificing technical credibility. 

- Bring Nebius's story into the spotlight. Partner with product marketing, engineering, design, and content teams to turn launches, technical achievements, customer stories, and company milestones into conversations that resonate. 

- Experiment, learn, and grow. Test new formats, ideas, and approaches to expand our reach and deepen engagement. Use data and community feedback to continuously improve performance. 

- Stay ahead of what's next. Keep a pulse on the AI ecosystem, from model releases and infrastructure breakthroughs to emerging voices and industry conversations. Bring fresh ideas and insights back to the team. 

- Move fast and take initiative. Spot opportunities, develop ideas, and execute independently. Use AI and other tools to work smarter while maintaining a high bar for quality and authenticity. 

What you'll bring

- 1–3 years of experience managing social media for a brand, startup, or creator, with a strong focus on X. 

- A genuine passion for X. You're an active participant in the platform, understand its culture and dynamics, and can point to content or conversations you've helped grow. 

- Strong creative instincts and excellent writing skills. You know how to capture attention, communicate complex ideas simply, and adapt your voice to different conversations. 

- An understanding of the AI ecosystem. You follow the companies, technologies, people, and debates shaping AI and are excited to deepen your expertise. 

- A natural ability to build connections. You understand how communities form, how influence works, and how to turn authentic engagement into meaningful relationships. 

- A bias for action. You're resourceful, proactive, and comfortable taking an idea from concept to execution without extensive direction. 

- An experimental mindset. You use performance data, audience signals, and your own judgment to understand what's working and find new ways to grow. 

- Strong editorial judgment. You know the difference between joining a conversation and forcing your way into one—and how to make a brand feel like a credible participant rather than an advertiser. 

Bonus points

- Experience working in AI, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, or another technical industry. 

- Active participation in AI, machine learning, developer, or open-source communities. 

- Experience creating short-form videos, graphics, memes, or other social-first content. 

- Familiarity with X analytics, social listening, publishing tools, and automation. 

- A sense of humor and a strong understanding of the personalities, trends, and culture of the AI community. 

Key employee benefits in the US:

- Health insurance: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and families.

- 401(k) plan: Up to 4% company match with immediate vesting.

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Remote work reimbursement: Up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

- Disability & life insurance: Company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Pay Transparency

We’re looking for a Software Engineer to build software that makes network operations safe, scalable, and boring — even as we launch new data centers and expand fast. - Make network changes safe and transparent: CI/CD workflows, diff/review tooling, staged rollouts/rollbacks, audit trails, and guardrails

- Develop observability systems that scale across many sites: telemetry pipelines, signal quality, and tooling that shortens incident investigations

- Close “last mile” gaps between the network and the platform: integrate source-of-truth data, expose APIs, and build reliable automation around it

- Collaborate closely with network engineers and SREs to turn real operational pain into product-quality tooling

- 5+ years of professional software engineering experience (or equivalent practical background)

The goal is to improve deal velocity, accuracy, predictability, and scalability as the business grows. 

This is a 0→1 and 1→n transformation role. You will assess the current state, define the target operating model and transformation roadmap, and drive implementation across processes, policies, systems, data, and ways of working. You will partner closely with Sales, Commercial Ops, Legal, Finance, GTM Ops, GTM Systems, Billing Engineering, and Billing Product. 

Responsibilities 

- Lead the transformation of the end-to-end Quote-to-Cash lifecycle, initially focusing on deal initiation, structuring, approval, contracting, billing setup, and customer activation. 

- Assess current-state processes, identify root causes of friction and rework, and define a scalable future-state operating model. 

- Develop and execute a prioritized transformation roadmap spanning processes, policies, systems, data, controls, and organizational responsibilities. 

- Redesign complex, fragmented, or manual workflows to improve speed, accuracy, automation, and the customer and seller experience. 

- Define and implement policies, governance frameworks, approval authorities, and deal guardrails that enable scale without unnecessarily slowing the business.

- Partner with Sales and Commercial Ops to improve deal quality and enable first-time-right deal structuring. 

- Collaborate with Legal and Finance to simplify approvals, standardize contract terms, and maintain appropriate commercial and financial controls. 

- Work with GTM Systems to embed workflows, policies, data requirements, and controls into CRM, CPQ, contract management, and related tools. 

- Partner with Billing Engineering and Billing Product to create a reliable and increasingly automated flow from order form to billing and customer activation. 

- Standardize the handling of complex deal constructs, including usage-based pricing, multi-year agreements, ramp structures, prepayments, and custom commercial terms. 

- Establish clear ownership, handoffs, and service expectations across teams involved in the Quote-to-Cash lifecycle. 

- Develop playbooks, guidance, and change-management programs that drive adoption of new processes and tools.

- Ensure reliable operation of crawling infrastructure under high-throughput conditions

- Define observability and quality metrics for crawl coverage, freshness, throughput, and content quality

- Monitor resource usage, bandwidth consumption, and infrastructure cost

- Collaborate with indexing and ML teams to ensure acquired content meets retrieval and ranking requirements

- Enable safe experimentation with crawling strategies and content acquisition policies

- 8+ years of experience building backend or distributed systems

- Strong Go or C++ expertise 

- Experience with large-scale distributed systems (10k+ RPS, billions of URLs, high-throughput pipelines)

- Understanding of web protocols (HTTP, DNS, TLS), crawling, scraping, and content extraction

- Experience operating production systems and debugging failures in distributed environments

- Strong understanding of scalability, fault tolerance, and resource management

- Web crawling

- Building streaming data pipelines and event-driven systems

- Kafka, Pulsar, NATS, RabbitMQ, or similar messaging platforms

- Build well-tested components with clear responsibilities and interaction contracts, while remaining flexible as the system evolves

- Define and implement observability primitives, including structured logs, metrics, and data quality signals across offline and nearline pipelines

- Monitor throughput, resource usage, and cost, and drive optimisations when business needs require it

- Collaborate with runtime and ML teams to ensure indexing outputs meet retrieval and ranking requirements

- Enable safe experimentation on indexing strategies and data processing logic through controlled rollouts and clearly defined quality signals
