- 8+ years of experience building production backend or data infrastructure systems

- Strong Go experience (C++/Rust is a plus)

- Experience with large-scale data processing systems (10+ GiB/sec throughput, petabyte-scale datasets, etc.)

- Experience building or operating databases, storage systems, data planes, or indexing pipelines

- Strong understanding of distributed systems, fault tolerance, consistency, and scalability

- Experience running production systems and handling operational incidents

- Systems-thinking mindset and ability to reason about end-to-end data flows

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

- Distributed data processing frameworks such as Spark, Flink, MapReduce, or Beam

- Content systems including, scraping, proxying, or anti-bot infrastructure

- Ad tech, social networks, or other large-scale content platforms

You will design and operate systems that handle thousands of requests per second under strict latency budgets, optimising every layer from request handling to data access and response assembly.

In this position, your responsibility will be to

- Design, implement, and operate core runtime services for serving search queries at scale

- Build and optimise request flows, including query processing, retrieval orchestration, and response assembly under strict latency budgets

- Develop systems that maintain performance and predictability under high load

- Optimise CPU, memory, and data access patterns in performance-critical paths

- Ensure reliability, observability, and predictability across production services

- Build well-tested systems with clear responsibilities and interaction contracts, while remaining flexible as architecture evolves

- Define and implement observability primitives, including structured logs, metrics, traces, and latency breakdowns

- Monitor throughput, latency, and resource usage, and drive improvements in performance and cost efficiency

- Collaborate with indexing and ML teams to integrate retrieval and ranking components, keeping ML logic decoupled from core system internals

- Support experimentation and iteration through controlled rollouts and rigorous benchmarking

You may be a good fit if you:

- Have 8+ years of experience as a software engineer working on production backend systems

- Have strong hands-on expertise in C++ or Rust in real-world, high-load services

- Have built and operated high-load, low-latency user-facing systems handling thousands of RPS under strict latency constraints

- Understand performance at a systems level — CPU, memory, networking, and data access

- Have operated your own code in production: deployed it, debugged incidents, and rolled back changes when necessary

- Think end-to-end about request flows rather than staying within isolated components

- Can balance correctness, latency, and development velocity, making pragmatic tradeoffs when scope or time requires

- Collaborate effectively across engineering, ML, and product teams, communicating clearly in cross-functional settings

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

- DBMS internals (open source or SaaS) and cloud infrastructure

- High-load web applications or large-scale APIs

- Performance-critical systems such as trading platforms or real-time data pipelines

- Low-level performance tuning and hardware-level optimisation

- Open-source contributions or active involvement in the engineering community

- Competitive programming or CTF participation

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group

The Infrastructure Acquisition Group secures the land, power, and data center capacity that enables the Nebius AI Cloud. We identify where Nebius should grow next, structure the commercial agreements that make that growth possible, and partner across engineering, energy, finance, legal, and development to bring new AI infrastructure online.

We're a small, founding team building this function from the ground up across the Americas, leading the acquisition of colocation, build-to-suit, powered land, and other strategic infrastructure opportunities as one of the world's fastest-growing AI cloud platforms scales.

Examples of Problems We're Solving

Determine whether a site can actually support the AI infrastructure we're planning to build. Lead multidisciplinary technical due diligence across geotechnical, environmental, civil, utility, and entitlement workstreams to determine whether a project is technically feasible before Nebius commits capital.

Build a repeatable technical due diligence program. Help establish the standards, consultant network, playbooks, and review processes that ensure every infrastructure opportunity is evaluated consistently across the Americas.

Identify technical risk before it becomes commercial risk. Work with Site Selection, Project Development, Engineering, and external consultants to identify development constraints early enough to influence negotiations, investment decisions, and project schedules.

About the Role

As a Technical Due Diligence Manager, you'll evaluate the technical feasibility of AI infrastructure opportunities across the Americas before Nebius commits capital. Working within the Infrastructure Acquisition Group, you'll lead multidisciplinary engineering due diligence across powered land and build-to-suit developments, partnering with Site Selection, Engineering, Energy, Legal, and Project Development to identify technical risk, assess development feasibility, and support investment decisions.

This is a build-phase role on a build-phase team. Many of the standards, playbooks, consultant relationships, and technical review processes you'll use are still being written—in some cases, you'll help write them. postings.title: Technical Product Manager – Storage
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The Role

Nebius is looking for a deeply technical Technical Product Manager – Storage to join the team. In this role, the candidate will own the vision, roadmap, and priorities for storage services in Nebius Cloud, including block storage, file and parallel file systems, object storage, and the storage capabilities that underpin AI/ML and HPC workloads.

The candidate will be responsible for shaping and managing backlogs for storage service teams and leading company-wide initiatives related to storage. This is a hands-on, technically demanding role: the candidate is expected to reason about storage internals, data paths, and performance trade-offs directly with engineers. It requires strong technical depth combined with the ability to coordinate across engineering, development, product, technical support, and go-to-market teams.

Responsibilities

- Own and manage the product backlog for storage service teams (block, file, parallel/HPC, and object storage)

- Lead and coordinate cross-company initiatives involving storage, including data durability, performance, capacity, and cost initiatives

- Work closely with engineering and architecture teams to define product requirements at the level of data paths, consistency models, replication and erasure coding, and performance characteristics, and deliver new storage features

- Make informed technical trade-offs on durability, availability, latency, throughput, and cost, and defend them with data

- Partner with product marketing and technical pre-sales/post-sales teams on technical publications, go-to-market activities, customer engagement, acquisition, and retention related to storage

- Ensure the delivery of storage services that meet high standards for durability, availability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency, including storage for AI/ML training and inference and HPC

Requirements

- Hands-on experience building storage products in the cloud is the single most important requirement: the candidate must have designed, built, or operated cloud storage services (not just used or integrated them), in senior engineering, architecture, or technical leadership roles at hyperscalers, cloud providers, storage vendors, or other advanced technology companies

- Deep understanding of storage systems internals: block, file, and object storage architectures, distributed storage, replication and erasure coding, consistency and durability models, and the read/write data path

- Hands-on familiarity with technologies and interfaces such as NVMe/NVMe-oF, iSCSI, POSIX and parallel file systems (e.g., Lustre, GPFS/Spectrum Scale, BeeGFS), Ceph, S3-compatible object storage, and RDMA-based data paths

- Ability to reason quantitatively about IOPS, throughput, latency (including tail latency), and cost per usable TB, and to read and interpret benchmarks

- Strong technical expertise in at least two of the following areas:

- Block storage and virtualization (volumes, snapshots, replication, NVMe-oF)

- File and parallel file systems for HPC/AI (Lustre, GPFS, BeeGFS, NFS)

- Distributed storage internals (replication, erasure coding, consistency, repair)

- Storage performance engineering and benchmarking

- Object storage at scale (S3-compatible APIs, metadata, multipart, lifecycle)

- Proven track record of delivering complex technical initiatives requiring coordination across multiple teams or stakeholders

- Technical leadership experience is a strong plus

- Product management experience is not required, but a strong willingness to learn and grow into the role is essential

Nice to Have

- Experience with storage for AI/ML training pipelines and large-scale HPC (checkpointing, data loading at scale, high-throughput sequential and random access patterns)

- Experience creating technical documentation, guides, tutorials, or reference architectures for storage products

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a technically strong professional with a background in cloud or cloud storage products at hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure), other public cloud providers, storage vendors, their partners, or highly digitalized enterprises.

The candidate may come from a background in storage engineering, distributed systems, architecture, SRE, or technical leadership, with hands-on experience building cloud storage services, distributed storage systems, or high-performance storage for ML and HPC. Experience in technical product or platform ownership or technical leadership is highly valued, even if the candidate has not held a formal manager title.

Relevant experience in ML and HPC environments is strongly desirable given the storage demands of these workloads, though the candidate is expected to adapt quickly and learn new domains.

About Nebius

Nebius AI is an AI cloud platform with one of the largest GPU capacities in Europe. Launched in November 2023, the Nebius AI platform provides high-end, training-optimized infrastructure for AI practitioners. As an NVIDIA preferred cloud service provider, Nebius AI offers a variety of NVIDIA GPUs for training and inference, as well as a set of tools for efficient multi-node training. 

Nebius AI owns a data center in Finland, built from the ground up by the company’s R&D team and showcasing our commitment to sustainability. The data center is home to ISEG, the most powerful commercially available supercomputer in Europe and the 16th most powerful globally (Top 500 list, November 2023). 

Nebius’s headquarters are in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with teams working out of R&D hubs across Europe and the Middle East. 

Nebius AI is built with the talent of more than 500 highly skilled engineers with a proven track record in developing sophisticated cloud and ML solutions and designing cutting-edge hardware. This allows all the layers of the Nebius AI cloud – from hardware to UI – to be built in-house, distictly differentiating Nebius AI from the majority of specialized clouds: Nebius customers get a true hyperscaler-cloud experience tailored for AI practitioners. We’re growing and expanding our products every day. 

If you’re up to the challenge and are excited about AI and ML as much as we are, join us!

- Flexibility and ownership

- Build reporting mechanisms and dashboards that give leadership clear visibility into site health, SLA performance, maintenance status, and open risk across the portfolio.

- Lead incident coordination and post-incident follow-up, including root cause analysis and corrective action tracking with landlords and internal teams.

- Track and manage contractual operational obligations, deliverables, and timelines across multiple sites and providers simultaneously.

The Data Center team is responsible for the physical infrastructure that underpins Nebius' AI cloud. We manage the full lifecycle of our COLO and BTS footprint — from bringing new capacity online to keeping live sites running reliably at scale. postings.title: Technical Project Manager - Network Infrastructure - EMEA
postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The Role

We're looking for a Technical Project Manager for Network Infrastructure. This is not a "make slides, chase tickets, and ask engineers for status" job. It is a role for someone with an engineering skeleton: a person who has built, operated, broken and recovered things, and can earn trust in a room full of SREs, SWEs, network engineers, security and platform teams. You will work with a high degree of independence, set up the project management practices for your area from scratch, and stay close to the technical details yourself.

The "T" matters. You don't need to be the deepest expert in every area, but you should be technical enough to understand real trade-offs: why rollback is not optional, why "just automate it" can create a bigger blast radius, why a provisioning flow must survive real-world constraints, why SLOs without ownership are decoration, and why network device CI/CD is very different from deploying a stateless service. You can read a design doc, challenge missing assumptions, notice unclear failure modes, ask sharp questions, and turn a vague but important problem into an executable plan.

The "P" is project delivery with a product mindset, even if the product is internal infrastructure. Your product may be secrets and robot-user management, an SLO framework, a firmware rollout process, a network observability platform, CI/CD for network devices, or automation that makes day-0 and day-N operations safe. The job is not done when the technical pieces exist. It is done when engineers trust the tool, the NOC actually uses the workflow, alerts are actionable, runbooks are real, and the new way becomes the default way. That means adoption, communication, documentation, feedback loops, and sometimes a bit of internal "marketing": the ability to convince smart technical people that the thing is worth using.

The "M" is management of execution, not people management. You will not be responsible for engineers' careers, performance reviews or promotions. You will be responsible for making important cross-team initiatives land: defining scope, aligning owners, exposing risks, driving decisions, tracking dependencies, creating clarity where things are unclear, and making sure we ship useful outcomes instead of collecting half-finished initiatives.

This is a high-leverage role in an early-stage and fast-scaling network infrastructure organisation. Many important systems are being built now: automation, observability, reliability standards, provisioning flows, operational safety, and cross-site consistency. You won't be maintaining a mature machine from the sidelines. You'll help shape how the machine works.

Your responsibilities will include:

- Own end-to-end delivery of cross-team network infrastructure initiatives, from a vague problem statement to an executable plan to adoption

- Define scope and success criteria, align owners across SRE, SWE, network, security, platform and data center teams, and drive decisions to closure

- Review designs and technical proposals, challenge missing assumptions, and surface failure modes, dependencies and risks early

- Track dependencies and risks across teams and time zones, and keep stakeholders informed with clear, honest status

- Drive adoption: make sure tools and workflows become the default way of working, with real documentation, runbooks and feedback loops

- Establish and run lightweight, effective project management practices: planning, prioritization, reviews, and post-launch follow-up

- Work with regional teams and external partners (vendors, carriers) on the rollout of new network capabilities

- Turn operational pain and engineering input into a clear, prioritized backlog

We expect you to have:

- 7+ years of experience in technical project management, engineering management or a hands-on engineering role (SRE, SWE, network or infrastructure), with a track record of delivering complex cross-team infrastructure projects

- A real engineering background: you have built and operated production systems and can earn the trust of deeply technical teams

- Ability to read design docs and technical proposals, understand trade-offs, and ask sharp questions about reliability, rollback, blast radius and failure modes

- Strong understanding of infrastructure fundamentals (Linux, networking, automation, CI/CD) at the level needed to hold your own in technical discussions

- Proven ability to drive decisions and create clarity in ambiguous, fast-changing environments without formal authority

- Excellent written and verbal communication, including documenting plans and decisions and influencing smart technical people

- Ability to work independently and to build processes from scratch

- Professional working proficiency in English (spoken and written) and comfort working across time zones

It will be an added bonus if you have:

- Experience with network infrastructure: network automation, observability, or network device lifecycle management

- Experience with SLO/SLI frameworks, incident management, or production readiness processes

- Experience with CI/CD or change management for network or other high-blast-radius infrastructure

- Experience delivering projects with distributed teams across European, Middle Eastern and African time zones

- Experience with secrets and access management, firmware rollout or fleet-wide operational initiatives

- Hands-on engineering contributions (scripts, tooling, automation) alongside project work

Examples of initiatives you may own:

- A user and secrets management system for network infrastructure, including robot-user lifecycle, safe key/password rotation, revocation, break-glass access, mixed agent/push-based device support, and integration with existing secrets backends

- An SLO framework for network services and components, including SLIs, SLOs, dashboards, alerts, ownership, tiering, and a clear link between reliability targets and engineering investment

- CI/CD for network devices, where configuration changes, validation, staged rollout, rollback, and blast-radius control become disciplined and repeatable instead of manual and risky

- Fleet-wide operational initiatives such as firmware consistency, device lifecycle hygiene, observability coverage, monitoring quality, alert ownership, or production readiness for new network capabilities

postings.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.
The role

We are seeking an experienced Threat Hunting Team Lead to join the Cyber Security organization, reporting to the Head of Proactive Security under the CISO. 
This role is responsible for leading the organization's proactive threat hunting program across Nebius's corporate IT environment, cloud platforms, and data center infrastructure. You will lead a team of threat hunters focused on identifying advanced threats, uncovering adversary activity before it becomes an incident, and continuously improving the organization's detection capabilities. 
The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with an attacker mindset and a passion for proactive defense. You will work closely with SOC, Incident Response, Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, and Security Engineering teams to identify emerging threats, develop hunting methodologies, and strengthen Nebius's overall cyber resilience. 

Your responsibilities will include: 

- Lead and manage the Threat Hunting team, including mentoring, prioritization, and professional development. 

- Define and execute the organization's proactive threat hunting strategy across corporate IT, cloud environments, and data center infrastructure. 

- Lead hypothesis-driven threat hunting activities to identify advanced threats, persistence mechanisms, and malicious activity not detected by existing security controls. 

- Develop and continuously improve threat hunting methodologies, playbooks, and operational procedures. 

- Leverage threat intelligence, adversary TTPs, and MITRE ATT&CK to drive hunting campaigns and prioritize hunting efforts. 

- Hunt across endpoint, identity, network, cloud, and application telemetry to identify suspicious behavior and indicators of compromise. 

- Collaborate with SOC and Incident Response teams to validate findings, support investigations, and improve incident response capabilities. 

- Partner with Detection Engineering to convert successful hunts into automated detections and improve security monitoring coverage. 

- Work closely with Security Engineering and Infrastructure teams to identify security gaps and recommend improvements.

The role focuses on air freight and road transport across APAC, with a primary emphasis on shipments originating from or transiting through Taiwan, and deliveries into key APAC markets including Singapore, India, South Korea, Japan, Malaysia, and additional destinations as the business expands.

You will be responsible for day-to-day execution of inbound and outbound shipments, RMA and RMS flows, cross-border customs coordination, and inter-facility transfers within the region. This is a hands-on, operationally focused role requiring deep knowledge of APAC freight markets, strong carrier and forwarder relationships, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

Logistics Operations

- Manage end-to-end transport of IT hardware — rack systems, servers, GPUs, and other data center equipment — across all APAC lanes, including inbound shipments from Taiwan, inter-regional moves, and outbound flows as required.

- Coordinate air freight and road transport scheduling, carrier and freight forwarder selection, and delivery execution to ensure on-time, damage-free arrival at APAC data center sites.

- Handle all RMA and RMS shipments within the APAC region, including coordination with vendors, carriers, and internal teams to ensure accurate and timely processing.

- Manage equipment transfers between company warehouses and data center facilities across the region, optimising routes and minimising handling risk.

- Maintain full visibility over active shipments across all APAC lanes and proactively resolve transit issues, delays, or exceptions.

- Develop contingency plans and alternative routing strategies to ensure business continuity.

- Manage time-critical air freight shipments where required, including carrier selection, booking, and end-to-end tracking to ensure expedited delivery of hardware.

Coordination & Documentation

- Maintain accurate in-transit inventory records and ensure proper chain-of-custody documentation for all shipments.

- Manage all shipment-related documentation in relevant systems (Jira, TMS, or equivalent), ensuring records are complete, accurate, and audit-ready.

- Manage customs documentation and clearance processes for all cross-border shipments within APAC, including imports into Singapore, India, South Korea, Japan, and Malaysia.

- Process and reconcile logistics invoices; manage payments for transportation operations, including ZIP payments to the appropriate vendors and partners.

- Work with the security team to establish and maintain secure shipment protocols for high-value hardware across the region.

Compliance & Quality

- Ensure all shipments comply with applicable regulations across APAC jurisdictions, including country-specific import/export requirements, customs procedures, and trade compliance obligations.

- Manage duties, taxes, and customs declarations for inbound and outbound shipments across the region, ensuring correct classification and valuation of high-value IT hardware.

- Maintain audit-ready documentation for all logistics activities, supporting internal (SOX) and external compliance requirements.

- Establish and enforce SLAs and KPIs with freight carriers, forwarders, and 3PL partners; drive accountability through regular performance reviews.

- Identify and escalate compliance gaps or process deviations, implementing corrective actions as needed.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

- Partner with hardware engineering, procurement, finance, and data center operations to align APAC logistics execution with deployment timelines and business priorities.

- Collaborate with OEM suppliers based in Taiwan to coordinate international shipping windows, batch tracking, customs documentation, and inbound scheduling into APAC facilities.

- Act as the primary escalation point for transport-related issues across the APAC region.

- Work closely with the global transport team to ensure regional operations align with global standards, processes, and reporting requirements.

- Drive continuous improvement initiatives through KPI tracking, root cause analysis, and process standardisation.

Planning & Cost Management

- Forecast transportation demand across APAC based on data center expansion plans, hardware deployment schedules, and capacity needs.

- Identify cost optimisation opportunities through carrier consolidation, routing improvements, and smarter scheduling across APAC lanes.

- Track and report on regional logistics costs, flagging variances and recommending corrective actions.

- Support data-driven decision-making through regular reporting, dashboards, and operational analytics.

Requirements

- 5+ years of experience in transportation, freight, or logistics management, with a strong focus on international shipping within the APAC region.

- Deep, hands-on knowledge of APAC freight markets, air freight lanes, and road transport operations — particularly routes involving Taiwan, Singapore, India, South Korea, Japan, and Malaysia.

- Proven experience managing high-value, time-critical IT hardware shipments — server racks, GPUs, data center equipment, or similar cargo.

- Strong understanding of customs regulations, import/export procedures, and trade compliance across multiple APAC jurisdictions.

- Experience managing and negotiating with carriers, freight forwarders, and 3PL partners across the APAC region.

- Hands-on experience with RMA/RMS shipment processes and reverse logistics flows.

- Familiarity with TMS platforms, Jira, or similar systems used for shipment tracking and documentation.

- Excellent organisational and documentation skills with a high standard for accuracy and completeness.

- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills; ability to work cross-functionally across technical and non-technical teams in a global environment.

- Self-starter mindset with the ability to operate independently in a remote environment with minimal supervision.

- Based in the APAC region; Singapore, India, or South Korea preferred. Must be eligible to work in the country of residence.

- Fluency in English required; additional Asian languages (Mandarin, Korean, Hindi, or similar) are a strong advantage.

Nice to Have

- Experience in a hyperscaler, cloud provider, or large-scale data center build-out environment.

- Familiarity with ATA Carnet processes and temporary import/export mechanisms for repair and return shipments.

- Experience with Taiwan-origin shipments and familiarity with Taiwanese export procedures and OEM supplier logistics coordination.

- Background in supply chain analytics, reporting, or continuous improvement methodologies.

- Familiarity with physical security protocols for high-value hardware shipments.

- Experience supporting logistics operations across emerging APAC markets such as Indonesia, Vietnam, or Thailand.

The role 

The Warehouse Logistics 3PL Manager oversees warehouse and logistics operations for AI data center hardware stored at third-party logistics (3PL) facilities across the U.S. The role is responsible for launching new 3PL warehouses and managing inbound and outbound shipments that support U.S. and international data center deployments, ensuring operational excellence and on-time delivery. As the primary liaison between the company and 3PL providers, this position owns warehouse performance, supplier relationships, SLA compliance, inventory accuracy, cross-functional coordination, risk management, and process standardization. The role starts as an individual contributor with the opportunity to build and lead a team as the 3PL network expands.

Travel: Regular travel to 3PL warehouses and availability for other business trips.

Your responsibilities will include: 

New Warehouse Setup & Onboarding

- Lead the setup and launch of new 3PL warehouses across the US, from site selection input and requirements definition through go-live and stabilization.

- Define operating requirements for each site, including layout, racking, security, access control, systems integration, and staffing, with internal stakeholders and the 3PL.

- Develop and maintain onboarding playbooks, SOPs, and training for new 3PL partners and sites so the network scales consistently into new regions.

- Validate readiness before go-live, including systems connectivity (WMS/ERP/TMS), process walk-throughs, and security and audit checks.

Shipment & Warehouse Operations

- Ensure timely and accurate processing of inbound and outbound shipments, from dock to stock, within agreed SLAs across all 3PL warehouses.

- Direct outbound shipments to support data center locations in the US and internationally, working with carriers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers.

- Establish, standardize, and maintain SOPs for receiving, shipping, staging, kitting, and material handling; ensure 3PL adherence.

- Oversee packaging, labeling, and handling standards for sensitive, high-value equipment.

- Manage escalations and exceptions, including delays, damage, customs hold, and carrier bottlenecks.

- Identify bottlenecks and drive workflow, tooling, and automation improvements across the 3PL network.

Inventory, Asset Control & Returns

- Own inventory accuracy across all 3PL warehouses through cyclical and annual inventory programs and reconciliation with 3PL records.

- Guarantee data accuracy in inventory and asset systems (ERP/WMS), with chain-of-custody controls, asset tagging, and serial number capture from receipt through deployment, returns, and decommissioning.

- Support controls required for financial compliance (e.g., Sarbanes-Oxley) applicable to warehouse operations and inventory.

- Oversee RMA and warranty flows handled at 3PL sites, including secure handling of data-bearing devices and disposition per company policy.

- Perform root-cause analysis on discrepancies related to 3PL operations and implement preventive measures.

3PL Supplier Relationship Management

- Own the lifecycle of 3PL partner relationships, including selection input, onboarding, performance tracking, and exit or transition planning.

- Define, implement, and enforce SLAs, KPIs, and scorecards (e.g., dock-to-stock, inventory variance, pick accuracy, on-time shipping); run regular business reviews.

- Lead 3PL execution in compliance with company policies, procedures, and security requirements.

Stakeholder Communication

- Act as the focal point of communication for internal customers and stakeholders, including data center operations, project managers, capacity planning, supply chain, procurement, and finance.

- Understand current and future internal customer needs and align 3PL capacity with deployment and build schedules.

- Report KPIs, risks, and improvement opportunities to leadership; develop operational and financial objectives and key results (OKRs) tied to KPIs.

Risk, Security & Compliance

- Assess and mitigate risks related to 3PL operations, including equipment damage, delays, theft, and supplier concentration.

- Ensure 3PL partners meet security, safety, and chain-of-custody requirements for high-value equipment, including physical security and access controls.

- Ensure compliance with trade, customs, and export control requirements for domestic and international shipments.

- Oversee root-cause analysis of logistics incidents and implement corrective actions; maintain audit readiness.

We expect you to have: 

- 7+ years in global logistics, distribution, or supply chain management, preferably in IT hardware or data centers, with a proven track record in operations.

- Experience managing outsourced logistics services and 3PL partners, including operational experience at or with a logistics provider.

- Hands-on experience with logistics management systems (ERP/WMS).

- Working knowledge of data center hardware (servers, GPUs, networking, optics).

- Demonstrated leadership experience, such as influencing partners and organizations, mentoring, and supporting the growth of others.

- Ability to use quantitative and qualitative data to identify trends and drive supply chain execution, including standardizing analysis across finance, planning, and fulfillment.

- Experience driving continuous improvement, standardization, and implementation of processes and systems.

- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, including vendor negotiation and performance management.

- Ability to work in a warehouse and data center environment.

It will be an added bonus if you have: 

- Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations or related field.

- Knowledge of ERP, WMS, TMS, and dock schedulers.

- Experience launching or onboarding new warehouses or 3PL sites.

- Experience with import/export environments of a 3PL or carrier, including customs and export controls.

- Experience in logistics operations in a global, high-growth, automated environment.

- Exposure to GPU infrastructure or AI/ML compute environments.

- Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development and ability to integrate AI tools to redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements), applying responsible and ethical AI practices.

Key employee benefits:

- Parental leave: 20 weeks paid for primary caregivers, 12 weeks for secondary caregivers.

- Remote work reimbursement: up to $85/month for mobile and internet.

- Disability & life insurance: company-paid short-term, long-term and life insurance coverage.

Compensation

We offer competitive salaries ranging from $107K-130K, plus performance bonus.

Join Nebius Today!

The role

The Warehouse Specialist runs day-to-day warehouse operations at a Nebius data center site. The role receives, stores and issues high-value hardware (GPU racks, servers, network equipment, spare parts), keeps stock and asset records accurate, and provides equipment to data center engineers on time.

The specialist is the site's hands-on link to the wider logistics function: Transportation and Transport Coordination for arrivals and pickups, Logistics Planning and 3PL Planning for schedules, Back Office for system records, and the Project Office for new processes and tools.

Your responsibilities will include:

1. Receiving & Dispatch

- Receive inbound shipments per the delivery schedule; check seals, packaging and contents against ASN, packing list and PO.

- Record damage and discrepancies with photos on arrival and hand them to Transport Coordination for insurance cases.

- Prepare outbound shipments and RMA returns: picking, packing, labelling, documents; hand over to carriers at the agreed pickup time.

- Follow handling standards for heavy, fragile and high-value equipment.

2. Provisioning to Data Center Operations

- Issue equipment and spare parts to DC engineers on time, according to requests and project priorities.

- Stage and kit hardware for rack deployments as agreed with ITDC and Project Managers.

- Keep a clear view of what is available on site and flag shortages to the Team Lead and Logistics Planning.

3. Inventory & Asset Control

- Post receipts, issues and transfers in ERP/WMS on the same day as the physical movement.

- Create inventory and asset records for received equipment, including serial numbers.

- Carry out cycle counts and annual stock takes; investigate and report discrepancies to Back Office.

- Keep the warehouse tidy, labelled and organised by location.

4. Security, Safety & Compliance

- Follow site security procedures for deliveries, access control and storage of high-value items.

- Apply safety rules for handling equipment and operating material handling equipment.

- Keep records complete and audit-ready (SOX, internal and external audits).

5. Process & Continuous Improvement

- Work according to global SOPs and site-specific instructions.

- Suggest improvements and report recurring issues to the Team Lead and the Project Office.

- Take part in pilots and rollouts of new processes and tools (WMS/TMS, automations) at the site.

6. Local Expertise

- Provide site-specific knowledge (access rules, dock limits, local carriers and customs specifics) to Transport, Planning and 3PL teams.

- Identify local operational risks and propose practical mitigation.

7. Add-on Roles (when assigned)

- + RMA: own RMA flows at the site — intake, documentation, return shipment, status tracking.

- + Key User (IRG / NetSuite / Project44): first-line support and training for colleagues on the system, test changes, collect feedback for the Project Office.

We expect you to have: 

- Autonomy: Independently runs daily warehouse tasks at the site within SOPs; escalates discrepancies, damage and security issues to the Team Lead.

- Impact: Keeps DC engineers supplied with the right hardware on time and keeps site stock accurate.

- Communication: Clear, timely updates to the Team Lead, DC engineers and logistics teams.

- Travel: Occasional support to other sites during launches or peaks.

- Work Mode: On site; remote work not expected.
